Description: A ro-pax vessel crew member was cleaning up oil from a leak on forward main engine (running at time) near the fly wheel when they put their fingers around the edge of the guard plate whereupon the moving flywheel made contact and caused a deep cut to the tip of the ring finger on the right hand. First aid was given and later on further medical treatment was required.

Short_Description: A service vessel crew member sustained an eye injury from a corrosive cleaner
Description: A service vessel crew member was carrying a routine clean of the galley when a corrosive cleaner got into the crew member's eye. The crew member was medivac'd by helicopter to shore for assessment and treatment at a hospital. The crew member was medically disembarked.

Short_Description: A pilot vessel had a drogue line caught under the hull and could not retrieve it
Description: A pilot vessel was carrying out crew training when it was reported that a line from a drogue was caught on the hull approximately midships and could not be retrieved onboard, it was thought that line was caught behind/under the hull anode. The vessel was lifted and the line removed from behind the anode. Vessel returned to service.

Short_Description: A guard vessel crewmember fell over on deck and was medically evacuated due to their injuries.
Description: A guard vessel crew member was exiting the galley when they fell onto the deck, due to the movement of the ship, which was rolling in rough seas. They sustained multiple injuries from the fall including an open wound to their head, pain in their arm, neck and chest. The other crew on board provided first aid but the crew member was in a lot of pain and did not want the crew to touch the open wound on their head. The crew stabilised the injured crewmember's head to protect their neck and proceeded back to port. The coast guard initially dispatched a helicopter however it was not needed and once the vessel was back alongside, the injured crew member was extracted ashore and was taken to hospital for further treatment. In hospital they were diagnosed with a broken arm, broken leg, broken neck bone and an open wound on their head.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations
Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged to SOLAS regulations. Accommodation ladder platform only 1 metre above water level.

Short_Description: An exercise was being conducted by a service ship when a crew member got injured.
Description: As part of a service ship's afloat exercise the launch rope for the daughter craft become lose from the capstan allowing the craft to descend freely the last 4-6 ft down the launch ramp into the water. A crew member was tailing and operating the winch, paying out the rope and feeding the line from the storage bin. The line became loose for an unknown reason and allowed a turn to come from the capstan. This allowed the remaining to unravel and the boat to run freely down the launch ramp. At the time of the incident there were no reported injuries however, later in the evening the crew member reported injuries which resulted in them needing surgery in order to reattach the bicep muscle.

Short_Description: Alternator bearing failure on a  ro-pax passenger ferry
Description: Alternator bearing failure on 12 volt alternator.  An inshore ro-pax vessel was alongside when the fire alarm for the engine room was activated and smoke was seen coming through the vents. The three crew on board initiated fire fighting attempts and called for shore assistance. The crew were able to extinguish the fire, which was on the aft main engine alternator, before shore fire fighting crews arrived. The fire crews advised to keep the engine room shut down to ensure that there was no risk of re-ignition. The source of the fire was reported to be from the aft engine alternator bearings failing. There were no injuries or pollution reported.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship

Short_Description: General cargo's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: General cargo's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. On disembarkation it was noted the end of pilot ladder was not secured to a strong point on deck, crew instructed to secure before disembarkation

Short_Description: A fishing vessel fouled their propeller and were towed back to harbour.
Description: A fishing vessel fouled their propeller on a net and were towed to harbour by a search and rescue (SAR) vessel.

Short_Description: See MAIB investigation report, when available
Description: See MAIB investigation report, when available
Damage_Description: See MAIB investigation report, when available

Short_Description: Cruise ship crewmember broke their finger while using a cabin door.
Description: A cruise ship crewmember was exiting their cabin when they opened the door, stood in the door frame whilst holding the door open with their foot. They placed their fingers on the door frame near the inside edge of the opened door. The crewmember then turned and leaned inside the cabin to check that the lights were turned off. During this process the crew member's foot moved, causing the door to close against their fingers, crushing them between the door and frame causing a fracture to their ring finger. They have been signed off work for three to four weeks and were medically disembarked.

Short_Description: Chemical tanker suffered an engine failure however, no damages.
Description: A pilot on a chemical tanker ordered dead slow astern while approaching berth when they received no response. They then completed the swing with the assistance of tugs. While ordering a slow ahead, there was response from the engine. The pilot managed to safely berth the vessel without causing any damages.

Short_Description: A small inshore passenger vessel collided with a moored rib resulting in minor damage.
Description: An inshore sightseeing vessel was being manoeuvred by a crew member when the port engine got stuck in reverse gear. The crew member shut the engine down but there was still significant stern way and the transom collided with the starboard beam of a high speed crew transport vessel that was moored near by. There was some damage to the railings of the inshore sightseeing vessel and the inflatable tube on the starboard side of the crew transport vessel was punctured. Repairs were carried out to the puncture shortly after the accident. There was no pollution, injuries or severe damage.
Damage_Description: Puncture to inflatable tube, repaired shortly after the incident.

Short_Description: A small inshore passenger vessel collided with a moored rib resulting in minor damage.
Description: An inshore sightseeing vessel was being manoeuvred by a crew member when the port engine got stuck in reverse gear. The crew member shut the engine down but there was still significant stern way and the transom collided with the starboard beam of a high speed crew transport vessel that was moored near by. There was some damage to the railings of the inshore sightseeing vessel and the inflatable tube on the starboard side of the crew transport vessel was punctured. Repairs were carried out to the puncture shortly after the accident. There was no pollution, injuries or severe damage.
Damage_Description: Bent railing. Gear linkage failure at the gearbox.

Short_Description: General cargo vessel's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: Ladder was not rigged per current SOLAS regulations. The rigging of the pilot ladder was not checked, or the embarkation and/or disembarkation of the pilot was not supervised by a watch keeping deck officer.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel crewmember fell and injured their ankle.
Description: A general cargo vessel crew member was walking on deck when they rolled their ankle and sustained a sprained ankle. The shore side ambulance service was initially called, however the crew of the vessel were able to arrange a taxi to the hospital as the injury was not severe and the crew member was able to walk with some assistance.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel grounded on a sand bar and re-floated later with no damage.
Description: A search and rescue vessel grounded on a sand bar. The crew disembarked the vessel and waded ashore before returning as the tide was rising to recover the vessel when it re-floated. They were then able to take the vessel back to port without further incident. There were no damages, pollution or injuries.

Short_Description: A tanker had an inadequate pilot ladder arrangement.
Description: A chemical tanker had an inadequate pilot ladder arrangement due to the fact that it was in poor condition, missing a bottom step and some chocks.

Short_Description: A container vessel crew member was trapped by a mooring line and fractured their ankle.
Description: A container vessel crew member was on aft mooring stations when their foot was caught by a mooring line and they sustained a fracture. They were medically disembarked from the vessel.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel fouled its propeller and required a tow
Description: A fishing vessel fouled its propeller and deployed an orange smoke. They were towed back to harbour by a search and rescue vessel. No injuries to crew.

Short_Description: Cargo ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations
Description: Cargo ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. Vessel has pilot ladders on winch reels port and stbd side on upper deck. Access is a step across via shell door but the platform does not extend 75cm outboard for safe footing and also has insufficient stanchions for a safe transition from the ladder. Belting is not cut away the required 6m and is only around 2m. Master very receptive to the issues alongside the ME control concerns.

Short_Description: A cruise ship passenger fell down a set of steps resulting in a fractured arm
Description: A cruise ship passenger was walking across a deck and went down two steps where they fell and sustained a fracture to their right upper arm. The passenger stated that they missed the stairs and fell on their arm. The passenger went to medical centre the next day where it was diagnosed that they had sustained the fracture. The area was inspected, the stairs, carpet and lighting were found to be free of defects and in good working order.

Short_Description: A cruise ship passenger tripped and fractured their wrist.
Description: A cruise ship passenger was walking towards a toilet when they tripped and fell down a step. When they put their hands out to break their fall, they fractured their wrist. After receiving treatment on board they were deemed healthy enough to remain on the vessel for the rest of their cruise. There were no defects found in the area.

Short_Description: Cruise ship passenger fractured foot after tripping over a lamp.
Description: Cruise ship passenger fractured foot after tripping over a lamp. The incident was initially treated as a minor injury until an x-ray revealed 3 broken metatarsal bones.

Short_Description: Crude oil tanker used a weighted heaving line for transfer of pilots bags.
Description: Weighted heaving line (Shackle) deployed for pilots embarking for departure. Line confiscated by Pilot Boat.

Short_Description: A tanker had an inadequate pilot ladder arrangement.
Description: A crude oil tanker had two poor condition pilot ladders. Starboard combination - ladder in very poor condition. Steps not horizontal. Steps loose between chocks. Bottom rubber step cracked. Side ropes showing signs of degradation. Vessel then rigged port side ladder which appeared to be in better condition but upon climbing a number of steps were noted to be loose. Vessel had a spare ladder on board and has replaced the starboard ladder. Master advised that port side ladder also needs to be condemned and replaced. The ladder had reportedly been taken out of service but mistakenly rigged as it had not been tagged/cut to indicate that it was not for use.

Short_Description: Private leisure vessel suffered water ingress and fire resulting in total loss of vessel.
Description: Yacht suffered a water ingress which was followed by a fire on board due to a short circuit. There were three crew members on board when the incident occurred however, they managed to evacuate to an attending coastguard vessel before the yacht sank. No injuries reported.

Short_Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel had an inadequate pilot ladder arrangement.
Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel had an inadequate pilot ladder arrangement due to the fact that it was secured to the deck strong points using metal shackles.

Short_Description: A sail training vessel grounded on a submerged wreck and was undamaged.
Description: A sail training vessel grounded on a submerged wreck. The crew were navigating the vessel near the coast as it was a land mark however the crew underestimated the effect of the tide and the vessel drifted onto a submerged wreck. The crew felt the contact however the vessel did not become stuck and was able to make its way to port. There were no injuries, damage or pollution.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel was on a training exercise when it sustained damage due a swell.
Description: A training exercise was being carried out to put a search and rescue (SAR) vessel's bow onto the rocks/shore to allow the crew to go ashore and practice for casualty recover was being conducted. Whilst doing this, on the first attempt the bow was placed against a rock and held the boat in position. A swell then rolled in which caused the sea to drop at that point. The bow of the SAR vessel scraped against the rock causing damage to the gel-coat on the bow of the hull.
Damage_Description: Damage to gel-coat on the bow of the hull

Short_Description: A sailing vessel that had ran aground later sank whilst under tow
Description: A sailing vessel ran aground on a rock formation, the bow was holed and started taking on water. Search and rescue vessels went to assist with salvage pumps and to undertake a tow. Whilst under tow the salvage pumps were unable to cope, the skipper abandoned and the vessel sank.
Pollution_Result: Small amounts of debris from vessel and fuel/oil

Short_Description: Container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: Container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. Ladder secured with shackles on side ropes.

Short_Description: A cruise ship passenger fell and sustained a wrist fracture
Description: A cruise ship passenger was walking a deck when they stumbled and fell fowards. The passenger sustained a fracture the left wrist, the passenger remained onboard until the end of the cruise. An inspection of the area was conducted,  no visible defects were found on the carpet and the small section of marble floor. The area was well lit by the ship's artificial lighting .

Short_Description: Duplicate of 2493/2024
Description: Duplicate of 2493/2024

Short_Description: A service vessel's crew member got pressurised oil in the face.
Description: A service vessel's crew member got pressurised oil in the face. When removing the filter itself from the housing, a large quantity of oil, under pressure was ejected from the filter housing and was inadvertently directed towards the crew member while trying to replace the lid, which could not be done because of the seal becoming damaged.

Short_Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel suspected a fire in a container containing briquettes
Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel was on approach to a port, smoke was seen coming from one of the containers containing coal and wood briquettes. No visible flames were seen, the container was opened to allow access for water spray on the smoking cargo in an attempt to stop a possible fire. The vessel arrived in port, the fire service attended but was not required due to the container not being at risk of igniting. The container was removed from the vessel.

Short_Description: A cruise ship passenger fell on their side after their foot caught in a sun lounger.
Description: A cruise ship passenger got their left foot caught under a sun lounger and the momentum caused the passenger to fall on their right side. This fall resulted in a suspected periprosthetic fracture to the hip. The passenger was medically disembarked to a shoreside hospital.

Short_Description: Container ship pilot ladder not rigged per SOLAS regulations.
Description: Container ship pilot ladder not rigged per SOLAS regulations. The ladder was secured by a bar. The master was informed and correct rigging procedures using side ropes were explained. The mater undertook the changes to rectify for departure.

Short_Description: Cruise ship's passenger fell and sustained a serious injury.
Description: Cruise ship's passenger sustained bone fracture injuries. The passenger was walking down a set of stairs and turned to the right towards a lift when their flip-flop got caught under the doorway threshold. This resulted in loss of balance and a fall. The individual landed on the carpet floor sustaining injuries in their hand and knee. Area was inspected and found in good condition.

Short_Description: A sailing yacht suffered an electrical fire that was quickly extinguished
Description: A sailing yacht with two crew onboard suffered an electrical fire. The crew were able to extinguish it themselves, a search and rescue vessel was tasked to assess and provide safety cover if the fire re-ignited. The fire was confirmed as extinguished and the yacht made it's way to harbour. No injuries to crew.

Short_Description: A moored fishing vessel's gas cylinder released gas
Description: A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was tasked to investigate an EPIRB activation, registered to a fishing vessel.  The SAR vessel berthed alongside the quay, two crew members went ashore and with two coastguard rescue team (CRT) went aboard the fishing vessel to locate the EPIRB. It was confirmed that the vessel had no one onboard, with the EPIRB located the CRT members exited the vessel. As the SAR crew went to leave they walked past a large cylinder laying down on the deck. There was a loud hissing, and a plume of white smoke/gas emitted, one of the SAR crew and turned round and as they moved away from the gas, they tripped over a line that was looped from a life ring to the mooring bits and landed on the left shoulder. Once ashore the injured SAR crew member was taken to hospital where they were treated for a fracture to the left shoulder.  The cylinder was a 50kg carbon dioxide, the safety pin was removed & hanging from the valve, with no valve protector fitted.

Short_Description: Inshore lifeboat crewmember fell overboard during a rescue mission.
Description: An inshore lifeboat was tasked to retrieve 6 casualties caught in a rip current. One of the crew fell overboard whilst trying to retrieve one of the casualties. The crew was recovered without injury.

Short_Description: Chemical tanker used a weighted heaving line resulting in no injuries/damage.
Description: Chemical tanker used a weighted heaving line. The heaving line was a large rubber block. No damage and/or injuries reported.

Short_Description: General cargo ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations
Description: General cargo ship's pilot ladder was rigged incorrectly.

Short_Description: Container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: Container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. The access was obstructed.

Short_Description: Container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: Container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. Ladder secured by deck tongue. Guidance provided on correct securing and corrected whilst pilot onboard.

Short_Description: Cargo vessels crew member fell overboard during a POB exercise, resulting in no injuries.
Description: Cargo vessels crew member fell overboard during a POB exercise, resulting in no injuries. Whilst recovering the vessels Daughter Craft after completing an MOB exercise. The fwd boatman fell overboard whilst attempting to hook onto the fwd davit fall. They kept in contact with the DC and then managed to climb on the davits cradle where they where recovered by the Daughter Craft

Short_Description: A tug crew member slipped and injured their shoulder
Description: The tug crew member slipped on deck and fell injuring their right shoulder.  The deck crane on board was found to have a leak from the valve. The drew member was off work for 24 days.

Short_Description: A tanker used an unsafely weighted heaving line.
Description: A chemical/products tanker crew used an unsafely weighted heaving line when sending it down to a tug before departing a berth. The weight was a hard rubber weight of 0.7kg. The crew of the tug cut off the weight and confiscated it. The vessel crew were informed and after departure they carried out a refresher training on the safe way to weight heaving lines.

Short_Description: Fishing vessel three crew member were overcome by diesel fumes
Description: A fishing vessel crew were carrying out an emergency fire fighting drill as organised by the skipper. Standard practice is to carry out the drill on either the shelter deck or top deck where it is ventilated using a petrol generator. The crew decided to take the generator into the fish room. The skipper returned and notified by another crew member there was a problem with the crew. The skipper went into the fish room to find one crew member laying down and the other two conscious but not alert. Emergency services were called and the crew removed. The crew were administered oxygen by the emergency services with one crew member taken to hospital and observed overnight.

Short_Description: Bulk carrier ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: Bulk carrier ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. Ladder secured with ropes, but those ropes were synthetic cargo strops, not suitable for gripping ladder.

Short_Description: Container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: Ladder was not rigged per current SOLAS regulations. The rigging of the pilot ladder was not checked, or the embarkation and/or disembarkation of the pilot was not supervised by a watch keeping deck officer. A tripping line was fitted to the bottom of the ladder, or was rigged not in accordance with IMO Resolution A.1045(27) 2.1.5.

Short_Description: Cruise ship crew member sustained a finger injury while securing aft tender pontoon.
Description: A cruise ship crew member sustained a finger injury while securing aft tender pontoon. They picked up the fender to secure it and their hand got caught between the fender and the frame. No fractures were sustained but the crew member was signed off work over 72 hours.

Short_Description: LPG tanker's crew used two weighted heaving lines during berthing operations.
Description: LPG tanker's crew used two weighted heaving lines during berthing operations. Heaving lines reported as painted monkeys fist with weight inside.

Short_Description: Cruise ship passenger tripped on a mat and sustained a fracture injury.
Description: A cruise ship passenger was walking across a restaurant area carrying a plate in both hands. As the passenger exited through sliding doors, they tripped on a mat placed just outside the sliding doors. The passenger fell forwards but did not extend their arms to break the fall. The passenger did not attend the medical centre until later in the day where they were treated for a fracture to the right shoulder. The area was inspected and no defects or deficiencies were found. The area was well lit by natural light.

Short_Description: A container vessel had an inadequate pilot ladder arrangement.
Description: A container vessel had an inadequate pilot ladder arrangement due to the fact that the pilot ladder was in poor condition. Side ropes frayed. Master agreed to replace ladder immediately.

Short_Description: A sail training vessel grounded after dragging anchor.
Description: A sail training vessel was at anchor close to the coast when it began to drag anchor and grounded approximately 10m from the shore. The crew broadcast a mayday and the local lifeboat service dispatched a vessel to assist. Before the lifeboat arrived, the sail training vessel refloated and the crew were able to get it back underway. The lifeboat escorted the sail training vessel back to a nearby marina but did not need to supply a tow. There was no injuries or damage. There was no pollution, but the sailing vessel crew buoyed off their anchor and left it for collection at a later date.

Short_Description: Fishing vessel had a small fire from its exhaust with a lifeboat tasked but no further assistance required.
Description: A fishing potter had a small fire from the exhaust which was out when the lifeboat arrived. The fishing vessel required no further assistance. The vessel's intention was to assess the damage once alongside.

Short_Description: An offshore tug's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: Ladder side ropes secured by shackles, rigged between the paired side ropes. Potentially stressing the aluminium clips.

Short_Description: A utility vessel crew member slipped and broke their arm.
Description: A utility vessel crew member was walking on deck when they tripped after stepping on a greased wire. They put their hands out to cushion their fall and in the process sustained a broken wrist. The nature of the work of the vessel meant that it was necessary and common to have various tripping hazards such as wires on deck that varied in location depending on the operation. Therefore the accident was attributed to lack of vigilance on the part of the crewmember as it was understood as a necessary part of movement on the working deck to be vigilant about the tripping hazards. The crew member went to hospital and was signed off the vessel and sent home to recover.

Short_Description: Chemical tanker's spring line parted resulting in no injuries.
Description: Chemical tanker's spring line parted resulting in no injuries.

Short_Description: A ro-pax vessel appeared to have a fire on one of the vehicles that was loaded
Description: A ro-pax vessel was loading vehicles when smoke was noticed from an articulated lorry. The crew initiated fire fighting procedures and discharged a dry powder extinguisher in the rear of the cab. After the initial emergency actions had been completed, the crew discovered that the smoke was not from a fire but from the exhaust gas from the cab heater. There were no injuries, pollution or damage from the incident.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel experienced propulsion failure and briefly grounded
Description: A cargo vessel was transiting along a river when it experienced a propulsion failure. The vessel dropped an anchor as it was unable to make it's berth, the vessel's crew were able to repair the engine but as it weighed anchor the engine stopped again and the vessel briefly ran aground on the port quarter. The vessel anchored again to effect repairs and waited for the flood tide to continue to it's berth. No damage to the vessel reported, no injuries to crew.
Damage_Description: PIPES SHEERED, GEAR BOX ISSUE, LOST PROPULSION

Short_Description: Container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: Container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. Pilot ladder seemed custom sized for the particular ballast draught in that the side ropes were led around a hard eye and secured to the deck with a pad eye/shackle arrangement but close to the deck edge. There appeared no means to secure the ladder when loaded via additional ropes with a deck strongpoint for shorter length ladders. The hard eye strongpoints were less than the prescribed 915mm from the deck edge

Short_Description: A cruise ship passenger sustained a fractured arm.
Description: A cruise ship passenger sustained an injury and was medically evacuated. They sustained a fractured humerus and had to be disembarked from the vessel for further treatment.

Short_Description: Near miss between a container vessel and a fishing vessel resulting in no damages
Description: A fishing vessel was hauling pots with day shapes displayed , when a container vessel  on their port side passing east to west got within 300m of  the vessel and gear. The fishing vessel had contacted the container vessel to tell them to turn to port. The container vessel stated they were already altering course before the fishing vessel contacted them.

Short_Description: Near miss between a container vessel and a fishing vessel resulting in no damages
Description: A fishing vessel was hauling pots with day shapes displayed , when a container vessel  on their port side passing east to west got within 300m of  the vessel and gear. The fishing vessel had contacted the container vessel to tell them to turn to port. The container vessel stated they were already altering course before the fishing vessel contacted them.

Short_Description: A cruise ship passenger fell during a tour of the engine room and fractured their pelvis.
Description: A cruise ship passenger was taking part in a behind the scenes tour, when they tripped over a bollard on the main working deck and fell to the deck. They were diagnosed with a fractured pelvis as a result of the fall. There were no defects in the area, the bollard was painted white and was designed to prevent damage to fire screen doors during forklift operations. The passenger reported that they were blind in one eye and the incident reportedly occurred due to lack of attention.

Short_Description: A private motor yacht experienced a steering failure as a result of a power short on a generator.
Description: A motor yacht had just departed from port when a low pressure hose ruptured on one of the main engines. This rupture reportedly occurred because a service technician had left a valve closed on the return fuel line. The engine was shut down so a repair could be carried out. However, once the vessel resumed passage, it experienced an electrical blackout because the generator main circuit breaker tripped. The other generator did not start because it was out of service. The problem was isolated to one of the phases of the generator. The vessel returned to the berth and hooked up to shore power and troubleshooted the issue. It was found to be a neutral that had detached and arced against the L1 phase causing a power surge. There was damage found on various systems due to the power surge. The failure of the fuel line was reported to be due to insufficient preparation for departure and the power surge was because the neutral connection was missing a lock nut, which caused it to vibrate free.
Damage_Description: Damage to ancillary systems affecting the steering gear.

Short_Description: A container vessel used an incorrectly weighted heaving line
Description: A cargo vessel was entering a port, the crew onboard passed a weighted heaving line weighing 316g and containing metal. A replacement gravel/bean bag was issued to the vessel.

Short_Description: A tanker had an inadequate pilot ladder arrangement.
Description: A tanker had an inadequate pilot ladder arrangement due to the fact that it was secured with insufficiently sized rope tails and there were not any suitable deck strong points welded.

Short_Description: Buoy-laying vessel crewmember suffered a back injury whilst moving a cylinder head.
Description: A Buoy-laying vessel was alongside with cylinder heads being moved from a lorry to the vessel. The heads were delivered by wooden pallet and as such, could not be lifted by slinging the pallet on main crane and instead were to be lifted individually by crane using bolt on lifting tool. While waiting for the main crane to become available to move the heads a crewmember decided to move each head individually to the side of the lorry where two deck crew were able to lower them off the lorry onto the pier. During this process, the crewmember felt a twinge in their lower back. The casualty felt some discomfort in their back over the next two days but was still able to continue work. Three days after the incident the crewmember bent down to change the biogreen chemical in the galley and felt a sudden pain in their lower back which intensified overnight and left them struggling to get out of bed in the morning. They reported the incident the next day and has been medically disembarked for treatment at home.

Short_Description: Cruise ship's passenger fell resulting in a hip injury
Description: Cruise ship's passenger fell onto the floor and hit their left hip.

Short_Description: General cargo vessel was not using the appropriate traffic lane, no accident has occurred.
Description: General cargo vessel was not using the appropriate traffic lane, no accident has occurred.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel lost a lifeboat that was found was ashore
Description: The vessel was seen navigating within 0.2nm, believed to be attempting to retrieve a lifeboat that the vessel had lost earlier in the day. The vessel was contacted several times by VHF and agent called and advised to navigate away from islands. The lifeboat has washed ashore and an attempt to recover/salvage will be made.

Short_Description: See MAIB investigation report, when available
Description: See MAIB investigation report, when available
Damage_Description: See MAIB investigation report, when available

Short_Description: Fishing vessel lost propulsion power resulting in towage back to safety.
Description: Fishing vessel lost propulsion power resulting in towage back to safety. Fouled her propellor. The tow was completed to port with no additional assistance required.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel was conducting training when a crew member went overboard.
Description: A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was conducting training when the helm proceeded to do a tight turn to port and a crew member went overboard. The helm immediately turned to starboard to avoid striking the crew. No injury/damages reported.

Short_Description: A ro-pax vessel experienced a fire on the emergency generator.
Description: A ro-pax vessel was alongside when one of it's auxiliary engines experienced an oil mist alarm. The crew started the emergency generator to provide power whilst that engine was offline. The emergency generator then began to emit sparks from the area of the turbo charger. The crew started fire fighting measures, isolating the space and commencing boundary cooling and activating the fixed CO2 fire extinguishing system. The vessel was alongside at the time, so shore side fire services also attended to ensure there was no further risk to the vessel or people. There were no passengers on board at the time and all crew were accounted for and uninjured. Emergency generator and emergency switchboard damaged. Fire damage to the emergency generator compartment: lights, insulation etc
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship
Damage_Description: Emergency generator and emergency switchboard damaged. Fire damage to the emergency generator compartment: lights, insulation etc

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel had an inadequate pilot ladder arrangement.
Description: A general cargo vessel had an inadequate pilot ladder arrangement due to the deck stanchions being too far apart (108cm) and the loose ladder was in poor condition. There was damage to lower wooden steps, the bottom rubber step was bent and there were several loose chocks. The vessel crew was informed of these defects.
Damage_Description: None - but loose ladder was in poor condition.

Short_Description: A cruise ship passenger overbalanced on a staircase and sustained a ligament injury.
Description: A cruise ship passenger was walking down a staircase when their knee buckled and they lost their balance but didn't fall, sustaining a ligament/tendon rupture to their upper right leg. The passenger was able and had no previous injuries or ailments and did not use glasses. They had purchased 11 alcoholic drinks on the day of the accident. The lighting in the area of the incident was artificial and the visibility was good. The surface of the staircase was carpeted and in good condition. The incident was reported to be potentially linked to the influence of alcohol.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel crew member fell over board whilst the vessel was alongside.
Description: A search and rescue vessel crew member was carrying outboard engine fresh water flushing on the mother vessel's tender whilst alongside. The tender was brought around to the stern of the mother vessel where it was positioned stern to stern so that the outboard engine of the tender could be accessed more easily. When the crewmember was leaning over to connect the engine muffs to the tender engine, they slipped on the wet flooring of the boat, causing the connection of the muffs to break free and the crew member to fall into the water. The crew member was wearing a life jacket which inflated and they were able to self recover via the escape ladder. The crew member did not sustain any injuries. In the future the crew of the rescue vessel decided that they should assign two people to this task to assist in attaching the muffs and to raise the alarm if anything went wrong.

Short_Description: Cruise ship's crew member fell from a ladder which resulted in a sprained back.
Description: A cruise ship crew member was standing on the last step of a ladder, fixing cables when the ladder broke and the crew member fell. The crew member briefly lost consciousness and once conscious had extreme back pain and could not move. The crew member was transported to the medical centre for an assessment and x-ray. The crew member was later sent to hospital for further checks. The area where the accident took place was later inspected and found that the rod of the ladder was broken.

Short_Description: Hopper dredger suffered a fire as a result of a failed fuel injector.
Description: Hopper dredger suffered a fire as a result of a failed fuel injector and manifold gasket. The flames were approximately 2-3 inches high and the fire was immediately extinguished using the nearest foam portable fire extinguisher. No injuries were sustained on board. The injector and manifold gasket were both replaced.

Short_Description: Dredger made contact with a tug resulting in damage to the dredgers bow
Description: A survey vessel was manoeuvring within a lock, it passed astern of a service vessel that increased power on it's pods to keep pushed alongside a wall. The power put through the water column subsequently pushed the survey vessel which then made contact with a tug. The survey vessel reported a hole in the starboard bow above the waterline and no other vessel was damaged.

Short_Description: Dredger made contact with a tug resulting in damage to the dredgers bow
Description: A survey vessel was manoeuvring within a lock, it passed astern of a service vessel that increased power on it's pods to keep pushed alongside a wall. The power put through the water column subsequently pushed the survey vessel which then made contact with a tug. The survey vessel reported a hole in the starboard bow above the waterline and no other vessel was damaged.
Damage_Description: Starboard Bow holed above water line

Short_Description: Container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: Container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. Ladder directly onto a reel, leading under a platform. No rope lashings evident.

Short_Description: A shore worker on board a ro-pax vessel was injured after they fell.
Description: A ro-pax vessel shore contract cleaner was working in a cabin, fitting a bed sheet to a top bunk when they lost their balance and scraped their back against a rail fitting. The contractor sustained an abrasion to their back. It is possible to stow the top bunks in the upright position, and the bunk that the contractor fell back against should have been stowed to prevent injury from falling onto it.

Short_Description: A ro-pax vessel experienced loss of propulsion and loss of electrical power
Description: A ro-pax vessel experienced a loss of propulsion from main engine no.2 and three port shafts and a loss of electrical power from the port shaft alternator. Power and propulsion restore after twenty minutes and the vessel continued on its way.

Short_Description: Sailing yacht crew member fell overboard into water during berthing operations
Description: A crew member was attempting to berth their vessel when they fell overboard into the water and, was recovered from the water uninjured.

Short_Description: A cruise ship passenger tripped on a threshold and fractured their knee.
Description: A cruise sip passenger tripped over the threshold when entering the toilet and fell to the floor, resulting in a fractured knee. The passenger was taking medication for some illnesses and had not consumed alcohol at the time of the accident. The area was inspected and no defects were found. Notices to 'Watch Your Step' were also posted in the area.

Short_Description: A SAR vessels crew member injured their knee whilst standing up.
Description: A SAR vessels crew member injured there knee whilst standing up. Whilst preparing the deck for departure from the berth for an afloat exercise, a crewmember took a kneeling position to ready the stern line for release. Following release of the line and on standing the crewmember felt an issue in the knee.

Short_Description: A deck cargo pontoon experienced a fire in the engine room.
Description: A deck cargo pontoon experienced a fire in the engine room. The crew were alerted by a warning light and a spike in temperature on a gauge. They inspected and found an engine room fire. The crew secured the hatches to stop the spread and came back alongside, where the local fire brigade attended and checked that the vessel was safe and the fire was out. The fire appeared to be caused by an electrical fault on an alternator. The fire rendered the vessel unfit to proceed; there were no injuries or pollution.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship

Short_Description: A passenger ship's crew member injured their knee while being on duty, resulting in a necessary surgery.
Description: A crew member on a passenger ship was providing resuscitation to a guest while their knee was bent over 40 minutes as they had nowhere to move. The crew member felt some discomfort however, after dealing with the senior doctor they continued working without any issues. The crew member took part in a crew tug war competition which resulted in them feeling pain in the knee the day after. They attended an MRI scan to which they were advised that the meniscus was torn and would require surgery. The security attended all areas where the individual could have possibly injured themselves and reported no defects.

Short_Description: Pilot fell overboard while transferring to another vessel.
Description: Pilot fell overboard while transferring to a cargo vessel. The pilot was recovered from the water after 3 minutes with no injuries and the tasked lifeboat was stood down.

Short_Description: Pilot fell overboard while transferring to another vessel.
Description: Pilot fell overboard while transferring to a cargo vessel. The pilot was recovered from the water after 3 minutes with no injuries and the tasked lifeboat was stood down.

Short_Description: Passenger ship's guest tripped and injured their wrist.
Description: Passenger ship's guest was walking in the open deck area towards the indoors where they stumbled and fell forward. They managed to cause a closed bone fracture to their wrist. The individual was holding a drink in one hand and some papers in the other, making it hard to catch themselves with both hands. The guest is due to be disembarked for further medical assistance.

Short_Description: Fishing vessel suffered water ingress and was towed by lifeboat
Description: The vessel crew members had noticed that water ingress was seen in the engine room, so they contacted the coastguard in order to get assistance. The reason for the water ingress is unknown, all of the crew members were transferred off the vessel and onto another vessel. None of the crew members required any  medical attention and there was no pollution
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting marine infrastructure or other ship

Short_Description: USV released survey equipment onto the seabed as a procedure.
Description: USV winch payed out as per design and disconnected. All release of survey equipment onto the seabed was controlled and part of a procedure.

Short_Description: Fishing vessel grounded and then capsized with 2 crew onboard
Description: A fishing vessel was outbound from port in a narrow channel when it grounded and then started to list and take on water. The engine was damaged by flooding. The two occupants were rescued. The crew reported that the channel was narrow and the strong tidal flow may have caused the channel markers to move out of position.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship
Pollution_Result: Minor. Quantity not known to MAIB but described as minimal.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel grounded whilst responding to an emergency call
Description: A search and rescue vessel was responding to an emergency to recover a casualty from the water when they ran into rock whilst trying to veer towards the casualty. The propellor was damaged but the vessel was able to complete the recovery and return to their station. The grounding reportedly occurred because the job necessitated the vessel to operate in shallow water. The damage occurred whilst the vessel was operating at low speed and the propeller was replaced once the vessel returned to the station.
Damage_Description: Damage to propellor that did not prevent the vessel from returning to the lifeboat station under its own power.

Short_Description: A tug experienced main engine failure on multiple occasions.
Description: A tug experienced propulsion failure on both of its main engines. At first it was able to return to a berth on its own but later on the engines failed again, and the vessel needed to be towed back to its berth by another tug. There were no injuries, damages or pollution.

Short_Description: Pleasure craft collided with RIB resulting in no damage or injuries.
Description: Pleasure sailing craft collided with pleasure RIB resulting in no damage or injuries.

Short_Description: Pleasure craft collided with RIB resulting in no damage or injuries.
Description: Pleasure sailing craft collided with pleasure RIB resulting in no damage or injuries.

Short_Description: A tanker struck the quay side whilst approaching a jetty.
Description: An edible oil tanker was berthing in high winds when it struck the jetty with its bow.  The crew and pilot of the vessel commenced a starboard turn towards the lock entrance of the port, when the strong force 7 winds caught the stern of the vessel increasing the turning speed of the vessel. Despite the efforts of the crew to curtail the turn, the vessel struck the fendering at the dock entrance. The fendering of the lock was splintered and broken. The vessel was also damaged above the waterline on the bulwark of the forecastle including dents, cracks and a hole at the centreline of the ship, above the forecastle deck. The incident reportedly occurred because the pilot misjudged the turn, taking it too early.
Damage_Description: Hole in the bow and the jetty was damaged so that it could not be used because of a piece of protruding metal.

Short_Description: Container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. Stanchions more than 80cm apart. Additional handholds welded on the outboard side, over the deck, but had a large gap between the bottom of them and the deck-edge. As such, too awkward to use safely. Side ropes severely frayed in places - only visible on way down ladder.

Short_Description: A research vessel crew member was struck by a winch handle whilst recovering an anchor
Description: A research vessel crew member was recovering the anchor using the electric winch. A winch handle was in place but not used, this struck the crew member on the leg causing a large amount of bruising as was diagnosed at the hospital when the vessel returned to harbour.

Short_Description: A recreational motor vessel experienced engine failure and was at risk of running aground
Description: A recreational motor vessel experienced engine failure and was at risk of grounding on a breakwater. A search and rescue vessel was tasked to assist the vessel . The search and rescue vessel towed the motor vessel to a mooring. No injuries to crew. No water ingress or pollution seen.

Short_Description: Chemical tanker experienced propulsion failure and was towed until the engines were restarted.
Description: A chemical tanker was departing a port under pilotage when there was a leak from the main air supply for the main engine. The pilot onboard requested tug assistance to tow the vessel out of a fairway. The crew carried out the repair. the engine was tested and confirmed satisfactory. The vessel then resumed it's passage.

Short_Description: A cruise ship crew member sustained a traumatic amputation from a galley equipment lid falling on their finger.
Description: A cruise ship crewmember was working in the galley area disposing of food waste into a bio-digester. The crew member opened the lid of the bio-digester before turning to assist the other crewmember who was working with them. When they turned, the lid fell and struck the crewmember's hand resulting in a traumatic amputation of their finger. The lid of the bio-digester is not fitted with any restraints and has no designed mechanism to control its rate of closure. The crew member was medically disembarked.

Short_Description: A sailing yacht crew member slipped resulting in a superficial injury to their knee
Description: A sailing yacht crew member slipped and cut their knee when a gust caused the yacht to heel. The crew member had their knee treated once ashore and later went to hospital for stitches.

Short_Description: A turn table ferry partially grounded and sustained damage to the rudder requiring a tow.
Description: A turn table ferry partially ran aground during departure manoeuvring resulting in the rudder stock being bent and the vessel sustaining steering failure. The skipper of the ferry made the vessel fast to a nearby buoy before a fishing vessel rendered assistance and towed the ferry back to the berth. The vessel was intentionally beached to carry out repairs and was out of service for a day. There were no injuries or pollution.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship
Damage_Description: Damage to the rudder stock which was bent and meant the vessel sustained steering failure.

Short_Description: A cruise ship passenger fell and fractured their lower limb.
Description: A cruise ship passenger was walking to use the toilet in their cabin during inclement weather when they overbalanced and fell, sustaining a lower limb fracture. The incident was due the the weather and the fact that the passenger was not using their walking cane.

Short_Description: A ro-pax catamaran made contact with a fender that had a sharp edge causing penetrating damage to the vessel's hull.
Description: A ro-pax catamaran was berthing under PEC direction when a section of a fender sheared off, leaving an exposed sharp metal corner. The corner then damaged the hull of the vessel resulting in cuts and scrapes to the hull including a penetrating damage into a void space. The incident was reportedly due to the extension pieces on the fenders are not the same strength as the main fender and are prone to breaking. There were no injuries or pollution as a result of the incident. The damage was 5m above the water line.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting structural integrity of the ship
Damage_Description: No1  0.4m x 0.15m cut under the belting in  Port Fwd Void No 4, between frames 15-16, 5m above waterline No 2  0.5m x 0.75m cut under the belting in port void No 6, between frames 24-25, 5m above waterline No 3 0.5m x 1.5m cut under the belting in port void No 6, between frames 25-26, 5m above waterline No 4 0.5m x 1.5m cut under the belting in port void No 6, between frames 26-27, 5m above waterline No 5 0.5m x 1.5m cut under the belting in port void No 6, between frames 27-28, 5m above waterline

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel had an inadequate pilot ladder arrangement.
Description: A general cargo vessel had an inadequate pilot ladder arrangement due to the fact that the spreader was resting against the rails to support the weight of the ladder.

Short_Description: A cruise ship crewmember took a misstep and sprained their ankle.
Description: A cruise ship crew member was carrying a box with both hands whilst descending a stair case when as they stepped off the last step they twisted their right ankle. The crew member's supervisor called for medical help and the injured crew member was taken to the medical center on board. The crew member was declared unfit for duty. The area of the accident was inspected and found to have no defects and the incident was attributed to a lack of care on the part of the crew member.

Short_Description: Fishing vessel crew member injured hand after getting caught when hauling gear resulting in near amputation to finger
Description: A male crew member was hauling gear when he caught his hand, which injured his finger. This resulted in the knuckle downwards which was affected and the finger was still attached. The crew member was taken off the vessel with a rescue helicopter and then took him to a local hospital for further treatment

Short_Description: Cargo vessel had a near miss with a pier.
Description: On arrival to port, a cargo vessel came close to contacting the pier. No damage was reported.

Short_Description: Chemical tanker pilot ladder construction did not meet current SOLAS standards
Description: Chemical tanker pilot ladder construction did not meet current SOLAS standards due to the fact that the gap between the stanchion and railings was too small to wrap fingers around for a firm grip.

Short_Description: See MAIB investigation report, when available
Description: See MAIB investigation report, when available
Damage_Description: See MAIB investigation report, when available

Short_Description: A search and rescue hovercraft made contact with a moored vessel
Description: A search and rescue (SAR) hovercraft was on a training exercise, the craft left a slipway and proceeded along a river with moored vessels. A camber present in the mud was observed to late and the hovercraft began to side slip down the camber towards a moored vessel. A call was made for an immediate stop hoping that the removal of the air cushion would bring the hovercraft to a stop before the moored vessel, however the hovercraft made contact with the moored vessel resulting in minor damage to the yacht’s gelcoat and transfer of paint. The SAR craft sustained damage to the fan's protective cage. No injuries to crew.

Short_Description: A search and rescue hovercraft made contact with a moored vessel
Description: A search and rescue (SAR) hovercraft was on a training exercise, the craft left a slipway and proceeded along a river with moored vessels. A camber present in the mud was observed to late and the hovercraft began to side slip down the camber towards a moored vessel. A call was made for an immediate stop hoping that the removal of the air cushion would bring the hovercraft to a stop before the moored vessel, however the hovercraft made contact with the moored vessel resulting in minor damage to the yacht’s gelcoat and transfer of paint. The SAR craft sustained damage to the fan's protective cage. No injuries to crew.
Damage_Description: 8mm deflection at point of contact on fan protection cage. Paintwork chipped at protective cage mount onto hull. Weld cracked on protective cage mount.

Short_Description: Service vessel's crew member suffered injury to finger resulting in partial amputation.
Description: Service vessel's crew member suffered injury to finger resulting in partial amputation. Crew member sustained a laceration injury to their hand/lower arm which resulted in the partial amputation of their little finger.

Short_Description: Passenger Ro-Ro fire in the gally from oven, resulting in no damage.
Description: Passenger Ro-Ro fire in the gally from oven, resulting in no damage. Fire detector activated in mess room alleyway, on investigation there was heavy smoke coming from the convection oven unit in the galley. Fire doors were closed. The fire was contained within the oven unit, crew member used a fire blanked inside to smother the flames.

Short_Description: Cargo ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: Cargo ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. Ladder secured with shackles around side ropes. There appeared to be no means of securing the Pilot ladder safely to the deck.

Short_Description: Cargo vessel experienced a cargo explosion, no damage and no injuries reported.
Description: Cargo vessel experienced a cargo explosion, no damage and no injuries reported.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel suffered engine failure.
Description: A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was being moved when the engine cut out and the vessel started to drift. The vessel was then anchored between moorings and it was found the fuel to be contaminated with water. An investigation is in progress.

Short_Description: A sail training vessel grounded.
Description: A sail training vessel was being navigated close to shallow water, following the 10m contour using the echo sounder. The task was to follow the contour and then turn to port once the echo sounder reading fell below 10 meters. There was one student below deck monitoring the echo sounder and one on the helm. The supervisor was talking to the student on the helm when the student who was monitoring the echo sounder noticed that the water was becoming shallow rapidly. They rushed to tell the helm but the boat was already aground. The student at the helm could not reduce the speed or steer away in time to prevent the grounding. The vessel remained aground until the wash of another passing power vessel lifted it free. There were no injuries, damage or pollution. The incident reportedly happened due to a lapse in concentration of the crew and the helm being distracted.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel experienced steering failure when the rudder fell off.
Description: A fishing vessel experienced steering failure after the rudder fell off. It was reportedly due to a welding defect following repair after an earlier grounding. The vessel was towed back to port and repairs were carried out and the rudder design was improved to prevent reoccurrence. There were no injuries or pollution.

Short_Description: A passenger vessel crewmember sustained an injury during mooring operations.
Description: A passenger vessel crewmember had scratches on their face and a shoulder pain after falling over when handling a chain block.

Short_Description: A ro-pax vessel reported that its fire alarm had triggered after faulty heater had overheated.
Description: A ro-pax vessel reported a fire alarm had triggered the activation of the fixed fire fighting spray system. The activation was because of heat, there were no smoke or flames.  After investigation,  the cause was found to be a faulty heater which had overheated. There were no passengers on board at the time.

Short_Description: A standby vessel crewmember fell overboard during a drill,
Description: A standby vessel was launching its fast rescue craft (FRC) as a test. The crew boarded the FRC, the davit deployed the vessel but the spooling winch also started causing the FRC to tilt. One crewmember was tossed into the water and was recovered by the FRC once it was in the water. The crewmember was wearing a lifejacket and sustained no injuries.  A valve within the davit launch system was found to have not operated correctly.

Short_Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged to SOLAS regulations. The side ropes were secured using shackles.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser collided with an unknown object on a river requiring the crew to be rescued and the vessel to sink.
Description: A motor cruiser with four people on board hit an object mid-river in the dark and took on water and started to sink, eventually listing and settling on the river bottom. All four persons were rescued by the emergency services. What had caused the flooding was unclear but floating debris in the river was believed to have damaged the propeller shaft leading to flooding.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting structural integrity of the ship
Damage_Description: Vessel took in water and was partially submerged sitting on the river bottom.

Short_Description: A recreational motor vessel experienced steering failure and required towing.
Description: A motor vessel reported steering failure and was seen drifting towards rocks. The two crew were unable to anchor as the anchor had broken. A passing vessel passed a towline to the stricken vessel but was unable to tow due to the size of the stricken vessel.  A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was deployed and towed the vessel to safety. No crew injuries were reported.

Short_Description: A yacht had an engine fire which was extinguished and vessel was escorted to its mooring.
Description: A sailing vessel had an engine fire and sent a mayday. A lifeboat and fireboat were tasked and it was confirmed that the fire was extinguished and that there was no water ingress. The vessel proceeded under sail with the lifeboat escorting them back to their mooring with one fire and rescue service crewmember on board. There were no injuries.
Damage_Description: Potential engine fire, only minor damage.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser started taking on water and was beached.
Description: A motor cruiser with two crew on board grounded on the beach after taking on water and not being able to bail quick enough.

Short_Description: A recreational vessel started taking on water and required assistance.
Description: A recreational vessel started taking on water and required assistance.  The six people on board were taken off the vessel and recovered to shore.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel ran aground but managed to re-float.
Description: A fishing vessel ran aground but managed to re-float and a search and rescue vessel escorted them back to port.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel got plastic buoys caught round the bow thruster.
Description: A fishing vessel got plastic buoy caught round the bow thruster and assistance was needed to cut the rope. Another vessel offered assistance.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. The pilot ladder was secured using two shackles connected together, then onto an eye on deck. The eyes on deck are located close to the deck edge. They need to be moved further onto the deck to allow adequate lead of a securing rope.

Short_Description: A passenger on board passenger ro-ro reported near miss incident.
Description: A wheelchair user passenger and their family was left in a potentially dangerous situation after the lifts were broken. There were no crew members available to help.

Short_Description: A passenger vessel hit a rock after a navigational error.
Description: A passenger vessel was on passage when due to a navigational error it briefly grounded. The starboard skeg clipped a rock but there was no apparent damage and no passengers were hurt. The crew and skipper checked the bilges and engine room for any water ingress. The vessel arrived at its destination safely and it was later was dried out and inspected by a marine engineer at low tide alongside the quay. No work was required to the vessel.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel grounded, but was able to refloat whilst the lifeboat crew were assembling.
Description: A fishing vessel grounded, but were able to refloat whilst the lifeboat crew were assembling. There was no reported damage or injuries.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigger as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigger as per SOLAS regulations. Access to deck was obstructed by the presence of mooring bits. A lifebuoy present, however it had no self-igniting light . The pilot declined to embark the vessel.

Short_Description: A commercial RIB crewmember sustained a lower back injury.
Description: A commercial RIB (rigid inflatable boat) crewmember sustained a lower back injury when the RIB they were travelling in hit the wake of another vessel. The impact caused the crewmember to be lifted out of their seated position and fall back down, against the corner of the seat, twice. The crewmember impacted the seat with their coccyx and lower back.

Short_Description: A dive support vessel had an engine failure and was towed by a lifeboat to safety.
Description: A small commercial dive vessel with two crew had an engine failure following battery problems.  A lifeboat agreed to provide a tow to harbour despite there being no immediate danger to the casualty.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel capsized in the surf.
Description: A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was on a training exercise for a new crewmember in surf conditions (approximately 2-3 feet). The crewmember mistakenly crossed a wave broadside to the conditions, a wave hit the sponson and then capsized the vessel. The vessel was righted and then returned to shore. No injuries to crew or damage to vessel reported.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser had a sheared gearbox and was towed to safety.
Description: A motor cruiser with two people on board had a sheared gearbox and was towed to safety by another vessel.

Short_Description: A Ro-Ro passenger ferry crewmember tripped and fell resulting in a fractured elbow.
Description: A Ro-ro passenger ferry crewmember tripped over the sill of a doorway causing them to fall forward landing on their elbow. After travelling to the hospital it was discovered that they had fractured their elbow.

Short_Description: A highspeed-RIB passenger sustained a back injury
Description: A highspeed-RIB passenger had a back injury when the craft left the top of a wave and came back down to the surface. The impact with the water caused the passenger to be thrown from their position and struck a seat on the craft.

Short_Description: A container vessel crewmember sustained a crush injury to their thumb after trapping it.
Description: A container vessel crewmember sustained a crush injury to their thumb after trapping it in the piston they were changing.  The crewmember was disembarked and taken to hospital to seek medical treatment and then returned to the ship.

Short_Description: Sailing yacht had engine failure and drifted close to shipwreck.
Description: The sailing yacht had engine failure resulting in the vessel drifting close to a shipwreck. The vessel was unable to use sail power to navigate to a safe location and was towed by a search and rescue vessel back to port.

Short_Description: A recreational motor vessel ran aground on rocks and was towed to safety.
Description: A recreational motor vessel went aground on rocks and sustained minor damage. The three crew onboard were unable to get the vessel clear of the rocks. A nearby RIB (rigid inflatable boat) towed the vessel clear of the rocks, a search and rescue(SAR) vessel took over the tow and towed the stricken vessel to a marina. No injuries to the crew were reported.
Damage_Description: Boss log suggests there was minor damage, but nothing more specific.

Short_Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel made contact with some rails.
Description: A vessel made contact with rails on the shore side of a lock.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel crewmember slipped down the stairs sustaining a fracture.
Description: A cargo vessel crewmember slipped down the stairs sustaining a fracture.  A few days later the crewmember was still in pain so visited the doctor and was diagnosed with a tail bone fracture. They were signed off work.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel reported engine failure and was towed back into port.
Description: A fishing vessel reported engine failure and was towed back into port.

Short_Description: A power boat was towed to safety  after a water intake pipe failed.
Description: A motorboat with two people on board wearing lifejackets had a broken cooling water intake pipe which resulted in some flooding. The water ingress was stemmed and a lifeboat assisted the vessel back to safety. There were no injuries.
Damage_Description: Water intake pipe had broken which resulted in progressive flooding.

Short_Description: A recreational motor boat had a fire which was extinguished and the vessel was towed back to harbour.
Description: A recreational motor boat had a fire which was extinguished and the vessel was towed back to harbour. A lifeboat attended and offered a tow but the skipper insisted on a friend towing them back. There were six people onboard the casualty vessel, four of whom were transferred from the vessel for the tow whilst two remained onboard.

Short_Description: A ro-pax ferry had a fire in motorhome on a car deck.
Description: A ro-pax ferry had a fire in a motorhome on a car deck. The fire was caused by a fridge that set fire to a vent and then to the awning. The ship's crew extinguished the fire. Once the ship arrived at its destination. The fire crew confirmed that a fire had occurred and it was extinguished safely.

Short_Description: A motor yacht foundered. All persons onboard were rescued successfully.
Description: Non-commercial leisure motor yacht on a deep water passage foundered after noise was heard below by the crew. On investigation by the vessel's engineer, the compartments below were found to be filling rapidly so the captain decided to abandon ship. All crew and passengers onboard escaped to vessel's rib or other craft or life rafts and were rescued successfully.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. The ladder was secured under a platform with shackles over the side ropes near the top of the shell door.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel made contact with a moored vessel whilst departing from its berth.
Description: A cargo vessel was departing its berth. After some lines had been let go, the master started the main engine. The ship moved  forward and was not prevented from moving by the springs which flew off the bollards. It made contact with an offshore supply ship which was moored ahead . There was minor damage sustained to the bow of the cargo ship. The vessel was returned to its previous position and moored. There were no injuries.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel made contact with a moored vessel whilst departing from its berth.
Description: A cargo vessel was departing its berth. After some lines had been let go, the master started the main engine. The ship moved  forward and was not prevented from moving by the springs which flew off the bollards. It made contact with an offshore supply ship which was moored ahead . There was minor damage sustained to the bow of the cargo ship. The vessel was returned to its previous position and moored. There were no injuries.

Short_Description: A yacht collided with a chain ferry mid-crossing.
Description: A yacht was pinned alongside a chain ferry as it was mid-way across the channel. The yacht with two crew onboard was towed off by another vessel and continued to its mooring. There was no damage sustained to the ferry or the yacht. There were no injuries or pollution. The yacht made its way back to its berth under own power.

Short_Description: A yacht collided with a chain ferry mid-crossing.
Description: A yacht was pinned alongside a chain ferry as it was mid-way across the channel. The yacht with two crew onboard was towed off by another vessel and continued to its mooring. There was no damage sustained to the ferry or the yacht. There were no injuries or pollution. The yacht made its way back to its berth under own power.

Short_Description: A passenger ferry damaged its mooring wires whilst trialling alternative mooring arrangements.
Description: A passenger ferry's crew were trialling alternative mooring arrangements, due to magnetic moorings not working, when the master attempted to depart the birth prior to confirming that the moorings had been released. No persons were injured but the mooring lines were stretched and damaged and had to be replaced.
Damage_Description: Shore mooring wires stretched and damaged.

Short_Description: A yacht had water ingress and was assisted by a lifeboat into port.
Description: The vessel had started to take on water during heavy weather conditions, it was also running low on fuel and was on passage to a port at the time.  Because of the worsening weather conditions, it was decided to choose a different port that was closer to where the vessel was at the time. No specific damage was reported and no towage was provided. The vessel was escorted by a lifeboat.

Short_Description: A cruise ship lost its starboard anchor due to a link failure.
Description: A cruise ship was at anchor, the vessel was swinging on its anchor, with one main engine and two bow thrusters on line to alleviate the swing. One of the links in the anchor chain broke resulting in the loss of the port anchor and approximately one cable of chain. The vessel maintained position as the main engine and two bow thrusters were still online at the time of incident. There was no damage to vessel or injuries to the crew reported.

Short_Description: A hire boat grounded and was towed to the marina by a lifeboat.
Description: A day hire boat with three people on board grounded outside the markers on an inland waterway and a search and rescue vessel was tasked. A member of the hire company boarded the vessel to assist with the re-floating. Once afloat there was some engine vibration so the lifeboat towed the vessel to the marina for further examination.

Short_Description: A passenger ship had contaminated fuel, causing it to need a tow back to its berth.
Description: A passenger ship had made contact with a dockside and another vessel. The authorities made contact with the skipper who denied any contact or collision with the dock or another vessel and suggested there was fuel contamination resulting in loss of the engine. The vessel was towed back to a berth.

Short_Description: A ro-ro vessel crewmember fell down the stairs.
Description: A ro-ro vessel crewmember fell down the stairs and had bruising to their left side below their rib cage and on their left hand.

Short_Description: An oil tanker dropped a dangerously weighted heaving line to a tug vessel, which narrowly missed a crew member.
Description: An oil tanker dropped heaving line onto the tug's deck. It landed 2-3 metres from the tug crewmember and there was a loud thump and when it was picked up, it was felt to be a significant weight. The tug crew cut the weighted section off and replaced it with a sandbag. Dissection showed a rigid bag stuffed with sand, gravel and a steel nut.

Short_Description: A ro-ro vessel grounded. It managed to berth without further incident.
Description: A ro-ro vessel grounded outside the navigable area of the channel. The vessel berthed without further incident.

Short_Description: A yacht started taking on water, necessitating a tow.
Description: An EPIRB signal was detected. A  sailing yacht was taking on water. Arrangements were made with the nearest rescue authority to tow the yacht back to safety. No injuries reported.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting structural integrity of the ship

Short_Description: A hire cruiser struck a bridge and became wedged. The vessel was freed with no injuries to the crew.
Description: A hire cruiser with four crew struck a bridge and became wedged underneath. All persons were safe and well. The engineers from the hire company released the vessel from beneath the bridge. The hirer had tried to pass under the wrong arch of the bridge.

Short_Description: A passenger vessel experienced an engine fire.
Description: A passenger vessel was about to manoeuvre out of a lock when the fire alarm sounded in the starboard engine room. The crew checked the engine room CCTV (closed circuit television) and no smoke was seen. A crewmember was instructed to check the engine room via an inspection hatch. A small amount of white smoke, believed to be turbo lagging vapour being burnt off following an engine refit, was observed.  The vessel continued on them passage and a short time later the fire alarm sounded again and smoke was now visible on CCTV. The master instructed the crew to make their way to a nearby mooring and monitor the CCTV for flames. As the vessel made way, flames became visible on the engine room CCTV and black smoke was now emitting from the starboard engine space vent. The crew began shutting the engine down and readied the fixed CO2 suppression system. The master radioed ashore and requested local fire service assistance to be ready for their arrival.  The CO2 suppression system was deployed and the passenger  cabin doors were closed. On arrival, the fire brigade boarded the vessel, requested the master and crew disembark as the aft deck and cabin began to fill with smoke. The fire brigade then brought the fire under control and, once safe to do so, the crew then boarded again to secure the vessel and shut down electronics.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship

Short_Description: A sailing vessel capsized. The vessel and all occupants were recovered to safety.
Description: A sailing vessel capsized. The vessel and all occupants were recovered to safety by a lifeboat. There were no reported injuries.

Short_Description: A cargo ship's pilot ladder was not rigged in compliance with SOLAS guidance.
Description: The pilot ladder was not rigged as per current SOLAS regulations. The heaving line was not available for immediate use and a tripping line was fitted to the bottom of the ladder, or was rigged not in accordance with IMO Resolution A.1045(27) 2.1.5. The ladder was secured by shackles around the side ropes.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel had an engine malfunction resulting in one crew injury.
