Description: A general cargo ship crewmember sustained an injury after a possible explosion in the engine room or from a generator whilst the vessel was alongside. The crewmember was taken by the ambulance service and was conscious.

Short_Description: An oil tanker's pilot ladder construction did not meet SOLAS standards.
Description: An oil tanker's pilot ladder construction did not meet SOLAS standards. The side rope was parted and was hanging by one rope not two. The continuous loop was broken.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel grounded resulting in a crewmember being injured.
Description: A fishing vessel was approaching harbour, the skipper tried contacting shore staff to find out if there was enough water depth for the vessel to enter but the shore staff could not see the tide stick due to the fog. The skipper contacted another vessel and then proceeded to the breakwater where the vessel started to touch the seabed and then became grounded. The skipper asked shore staff to help with getting a line ashore but due to a gate being locked was unable to. The crew threw a grapple hook to the pier to stop the vessel from drifting on to the beach as the tide came in.  After half an hour the grapple hook parted under tension from the pier and hit a crewmember in the face, causing facial injuries. Once the vessel was afloat, the crewmember was transferred to shore and passed into the care of the ambulance service

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel experienced an engine failure whilst on service.
Description: A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was in shallow water to recover casualties from the shore. Once the task was completed the SAR vessel's outboard engine cut out and there was no longer a water jet from the engine. The engine was checked and found that the water intakes were blocked with kelp. The SAR vessel was towed to shore to investigate if any permanent damage had occurred. No lasting damage was identified and it was concluded that the engine lost power after overheating due to the starvation of cooling water.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per current SOLAS regulations. A tripping line was fitted to the bottom of the ladder.

Short_Description: A motor Cruiser took on water and was escorted back to safety.
Description: A cruising catamaran with two crew started flooding through one of the stern drives. The bilge pumps coped with the flooding and a lifeboat escorted the vessel back to port.

Short_Description: A RIB lost engine power and was drifting towards a chain ferry. They were towed to safety by another vessel.
Description: A RIB (rigid inflatable boat) with one person on board lost engine power and was drifting towards a chain ferry. The casualty was towed to safety by another vessel that was nearby.

Short_Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel grounded during berthing operations.
Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel grounded during berthing operations.

Short_Description: A tug lost control, making heavy contact with a lock side.
Description: A tug lost control, making heavy contact with a lock side.

Short_Description: An offshore supply ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: An offshore supply ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. The handholds were not securely fastened to the ship's bulwarks to enable the pilot to step safely and comfortably from the top of the ladder on to the ship's deck.

Short_Description: A sail training vessel had minor flooding.
Description: A sail training vessel was at anchor with all crew on deck when the bilge alarm sounded, water ingress was discovered in the access hatch through to the upper level deck plates, there was around twenty centimetres of water.  The water was bailed out with an emergency fire pump and the source of the water ingress was discovered to be a broken pipe in the air conditioning system.

Short_Description: A motor vessel experienced engine failure and had to be towed to safety.
Description: A motor vessel experienced engine failure. It required a tow as there were concerns that it could drift into a shipping lane. A search and rescue vessel towed the vessel to safety. There were no injures.

Short_Description: A lifeboat ran aground causing minor damage to the propeller.
Description: A lifeboat ran aground on a sandbank and refloated after ten minutes. There was minor damage to the propellers.
Damage_Description: Only known damage to propeller.  Full survey to be conducted.

Short_Description: A person fell overboard from a recreational vessel.
Description: A person fell overboard from a punt boat. The casualty was recovered by another vessel and assist ashore. They received triage by the ambulance service and were allowed to carry on with their day.

Short_Description: A passenger ferry passenger slipped on deck and sustained a head injury.
Description: A Passenger onboard ferry slipped and fell on the deck and had a head injury. The casualty was taken to hospital for further treatment. Prior to the fall the passenger had consumed alcohol.

Short_Description: An offshore supply vessel made contact with a lock gate causing damage to the timber upright fendering.
Description: An offshore supply vessel made contact with an inner lock gate which caused damage to the timber upright fendering. There was no reported damage to the vessel or injuries to people.

Short_Description: A passenger vessel experienced mechanical problems and was towed in order for an engineer to assess the situation.
Description: A small passenger vessel experienced problems with propeller pitch and lost propulsion. Another vessel offered assistance and a tow to safety, where the vessel was moored awaiting an engineer to arrive.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel was conducting training when a crew member went overboard
Description: A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was conducting training with a trainer and helm. The helm went to turn to starboard into a wave, but the turn was initiated late and the wave had broken. This action pushed the SAR vessel to port and caused the helm to fall off the sponson. The helm was using foot straps as required. The trainer took control and recovered the helm. No injury was sustained, no vessel damage.

Short_Description: A dingy capsized resulting in two people falling overboard.
Description: Two people were in a dingy on their way out to a moored motor cruiser when the boat capsized and they fell overboard. One person swam to shore to  get help whilst the other clung onto the boat. The person holding the boat was in the water for 15-20 minutes before being rescued and taken to hospital.

Short_Description: An angling vessel grounded.
Description: An angling vessel grounded. All three persons onboard were taken to shore and the owners were left to arrange recovery.

Short_Description: A search and rescue craft had fuel issues.
Description: A search and rescue vessel had a fuel leak from its port engine and was escorted by a lifeboat to safety.

Short_Description: Investigated by another state
Description: Investigated by another state
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship

Short_Description: Investigated by another state
Description: Investigated by another state
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel experienced water ingress from a seawater cooling system.
Description: A search and rescue vessel was assisting with an emergency when the bilge alarm sounded. A crewmember went to investigate and they noticed a large volume of water in the engine room bilge. The port engine was stopped immediately and the source of water ingress came from the seawater cooling system. A flexible section of the main seawater hose was incorrectly fitted without sufficient overlap on the solid pipe outlet to which it was attached . Both of the jubilee clips on the engine side of the hose were found to be slack. The flexible hose was repositioned by sliding the hose up, all jubilee clips were secured and all of the water pumped out. The vessel returned back into service.

Short_Description: A roro vessel's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS.
Description: A roro vessel's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS. It was secured with shackles.

Short_Description: A recreational vessel grounded on rocks and was assisted.
Description: A RIB (rigid inflatable boat) with two people on board encountered engine failure and drifted onto rocks. The two people onboard manually activated their EPIRB and abandoned the vessel. Upon arrival, the search and rescue assets established there were no injuries and that although damaged, the vessel was still structurally sound. The weather was improving all the time and it became possible to pull the vessel from the rocks and tow it to safety.

Short_Description: A cruise ship passenger fell out of bed and injured their head.
Description: A cruise ship passenger fell out of bed in the early hours of the morning. The casualty mobility issues but unsure of the reasons why they fell out of bed. The casualty sustained a head injury when falling from bed and was taken to hospital for further treatment.

Short_Description: A wildlife survey cruise vessel sustained water ingress whilst alongside.
Description: A wildlife survey cruise vessel had water ingress whilst alongside. The crew and passengers were evacuated and the local fire service attended to assist in pumping the water out of the vessel.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier pilot ladder was slightly damaged and not rigged as per current SOLAS regulations.
Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged as per current SOLAS regulations. The left-hand side rope was damaged and frayed almost to the point of parting. The ladder also secured with shackles.
Damage_Description: Left hand side rope was damaged and frayed almost to the point of parting. Not visible till near top. Ladder also secured with shackles

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel had an allision with a sailing yacht whilst on service
Description: A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was tasked to assist a disable yacht. Following an assessment of the situation, it was decided to put a crew member onboard to assist the two yacht crew as they were physically tired and wet. The SAR vessel approached the yacht at slow speed, but the sea state made the approach tricky due to the motion of both vessels. When the SAR vessel was within five metres of the yacht the SAR vessel was struck by a wave, the helm engaged astern propulsion but struck the yacht's port side. There was minimal damage to both vessels. A second attempt was made to transfer a crew member aboard the yacht that was successful.
Damage_Description: A crack approximately 300mm in length in the hull midships above the waterline.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel had an allision with a sailing yacht whilst on service
Description: A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was tasked to assist a disable yacht. Following an assessment of the situation, it was decided to put a crew member onboard to assist the two yacht crew as they were physically tired and wet. The SAR vessel approached the yacht at slow speed, but the sea state made the approach tricky due to the motion of both vessels. When the SAR vessel was within five metres of the yacht the SAR vessel was struck by a wave, the helm engaged astern propulsion but struck the yacht's port side. There was minimal damage to both vessels. A second attempt was made to transfer a crew member aboard the yacht that was successful.
Damage_Description: Minor damage to the bow beneath sponson.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel's crew used a dangerously weighted heaving line.
Description: A cargo vessel's crew used a dangerously weighted heaving line. The vessel used a weighted monkey's fist when sending a heaving line ashore in the lock upon arrival.

Short_Description: A pilot preparing to disembark a cargo vessel sustained an ankle injury.
Description: A pilot was preparing to disembark a cargo vessel. Prior to stepping onto the ladder the pilot put their foot on a steel step that was available in front of the ladder. As they put their right foot on the step it disintegrated causing the pilot to become unbalanced and twist their ankle. The pilot took two days off to rest their ankle.

Short_Description: A ro-pax vessel and a sailing yacht had a close quarters situation.
Description: A ro-pax vessel was outbound proceeding along a channel, a sailing yacht ahead was mid-channel proceeding in the same direction with two crew onboard. The ro-pax vessel was increasing speed and starting to catch up to the yacht. There was a discussion to keep an eye on the yacht, there was room to overtake so the ro-pax vessel continued along the starboard side of the channel leaving the yacht to port who was still roughly in the middle of the channel. When the yacht was approximately fifty metres ahead, the yacht came around 90 degrees to starboard and started to come across the bow of the ro-pax vessel. The ro-pax vessel was immediately slowed and stopped whilst sounding five short and rapid blasts, the yacht passed clear by approximately ten metres.

Short_Description: A ro-pax vessel and a sailing yacht had a close quarters situation.
Description: A ro-pax vessel was outbound proceeding along a channel, a sailing yacht ahead was mid-channel proceeding in the same direction with two crew onboard. The ro-pax vessel was increasing speed and starting to catch up to the yacht. There was a discussion to keep an eye on the yacht, there was room to overtake so the ro-pax vessel continued along the starboard side of the channel leaving the yacht to port who was still roughly in the middle of the channel. When the yacht was approximately fifty metres ahead, the yacht came around 90 degrees to starboard and started to come across the bow of the ro-pax vessel. The ro-pax vessel was immediately slowed and stopped whilst sounding five short and rapid blasts, the yacht passed clear by approximately ten metres.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel had an engine fire and a hull leak.
Description: A sailing vessel with one person on board had an engine fire. The skipper managed to put the fire out but the vessel had a hull leak resulting in water ingress. The lifeboat was tasked to rescue the casualty from the vessel and was passed into the care of the ambulance staff who treated them for smoke inhalation. The casualty decided not to go to hospital despite being advised to do so as the staff could not check their CO2 levels. A work boat went out to check the casualty vessel to ensure the fire did not reignite.
Damage_Description: There was an engine fire and slight hull leak.

Short_Description: A commercial diving vessel grounded and required a tow back to shore
Description: A commercial diving vessel grounded on a reef and the engine had also shut down which meant that a tow from another vessel was needed. The vessel was taken under tow into a port safely and no damage or injuries to any persons were confirmed.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had a fault with the main engine propulsion and was towed back to port.
Description: A fishing vessel had a fault with the main engine propulsion. The vessel still had electrical power and had requested a tow. Another fishing vessel was proceeding to the stricken fishing vessel which was drifting but safe. The stricken fishing vessel had set up regular communication check-ins and was under tow. The vessel was then towed back to port. No injuries to crew or damage to vessel was reported.

Short_Description: A pilot boat was alongside when the crew saw smoke from the engine room.
Description: A pilot boat was moored alongside when two crew, not on the vessel, saw smoke coming from the engine room. Initial investigations state that there was no damage and no signs of ignition and that the FirePro system's activation caused the smoke and the smell.
Damage_Description: Smoke and smell came from the engine room. Firepro system activated. Initial investigation states there was no sign of damage or signs of ignition in the engine room. Firepro had activated which would have caused the smoke and smell.

Short_Description: An inland waterway vessel made contact with a shore object resulting in significant damage to the wheelhouse.
Description: An inland waterway vessel made contact with a shore object resulting in significant damage to the wheelhouse.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship
Damage_Description: Contact was made with the upper section of the telescopic wheelhouse causing significant damage that resulted in damage to the mast, radar, satellite dome, 5 or 6 windows, wheelhouse door and the upper wheelhouse structure where the force of impact caused the upper section to shift forward.

Short_Description: A motor vessel ran aground and had to be towed off the mud.
Description: A RIB (rigid inflatable boat) had to be towed off the mud by a lifeboat after grounding at a river entrance. There was no danger to life and no damage to the RIB.

Short_Description: A crew member fell overboard during mooring operations.
Description: At mooring, injured person was standing on the front of the boat to moor up and fell between the boat and the mooring.

Short_Description: A dinghy capsized in surf leading to a support boat capsizing. All three people on board self rescued to shore.
Description: A dinghy capsized in the surf, breaking its mast. The sailing club support boat with two people on board went to assist and was capsized by a large wave while attempting to recover the person in the water. The three persons in the water all self rescued and made their way to shore and there were no injuries. A search and rescue vessel recovered the dingy and support boat.
Damage_Description: Vessel capsized in the surf and recovered ashore.

Short_Description: A dinghy capsized in surf leading to a support boat capsizing. All three people on board self rescued to shore.
Description: A dinghy capsized in the surf, breaking its mast. The sailing club support boat with two people on board went to assist and was capsized by a large wave while attempting to recover the person in the water. The three persons in the water all self rescued and made their way to shore and there were no injuries. A search and rescue vessel recovered the dingy and support boat.

Short_Description: A chemical tanker's pilot ladder didn't conform to SOLAS.
Description: A chemical tanker's pilot ladder didn't conform to SOLAS. The pilot's first attempt at boarding noted that ladder was secured using shackles below a step. They discussed the problem with the master over the radio and requested that ladder rope tails were properly secured to a strongpoint and the shackles removed. The master subsequently advised that the ladder was now correctly rigged so the pilot made a second attempt at boarding. They noted that the rope tails were now leading across sharp edges and secured to thin railings. The pilot refused to board.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser capsized resulting in one death.
Description: A recreational motor vessel with two people onboard had left port to go fishing, while heading to the destination the vessel encountered waves which caused the bow to lift and crash down resulting in water immediately submerging the stern of the vessel and flooding the engine. One crewmember grabbed two lifejackets that were still in sealed bags, passed one to the other crewmember and then jumped off the vessel by the stern. This caused the vessel to capsize and the other crewmember ended up in the water. The life jackets did not inflate automatically or when the manual pull cord was used. One crewmember was able to manually inflate their lifejacket using the oral tube. Search and rescue assets were tasked to the scene and recovered two people with one being pronounced deceased.

Short_Description: A service vessel grounded whilst manoeuvring a barge.
Description: A service vessel was tasked to manoeuvre a barge from alongside a dredger. The service vessel let the barge go and started to turn the vessel 90 degrees to take it away from the dredger but the wind & tide caught the vessel and barge resulting in it being pushed onto the rock breakwater. Minor damage was sustained to the service vessel, no crew injuries were reported.
Damage_Description: Damage to supporting stay for Kort nozzle

Short_Description: A motor vessel fouled its propellers on rocks and required assistance.
Description: A recreational motor cruiser with three people on board fouled/damaged its propellers on rocks. The skipper tried to anchor but lost the anchor in the process. The lifeboat was called and towed the vessel back to harbour.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel struck a sandbar at the entrance to a harbour and began taking on water. The fire service managed to pump out the water.
Description: While entering a port a fishing vessel grounded on a sandbar after its skipper miscalculated the tidal height. The vessel began taking water at a faster rate than the pumps could manage. With a lifeboat providing safety cover, the vessel was able to berth alongside and the fire service pumped out the water. The vessel was subsequently lifted out of the water and a sprung plank was refastened before it was refloated. There were no injuries.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting structural integrity of the ship

Short_Description: A tug made contact with a ro-pax vessel during an attempt to make fast.
Description: A passenger vessel was heading towards the dock for repairs. The first tug was already made fast with a bridle on the stern and as the passenger vessel was approaching a buoy, the forward second tug was coming in to make fast on a bridle on the bow. The second tug was sent up the port sideline but as they went over to the starboard bow to send up the starboard line, the vessel got out of position and lost control causing the tug to be pulled by the already made fast port line stern first until they collided with the passenger vessel. The passenger vessel was quickly pulled to a stop using the first tug and the second tug was able to get back in the correct position and continue making fast the bridle. The speed of the passenger vessel was 4.2 knots which was agreed between the pilot and tug master prior to making fast. A contributing factor to the incident was that the port tow line was caught on a stern bollard of the second tug making the gog line useless and the pulling force right aft.

Short_Description: A tug made contact with a ro-pax vessel during an attempt to make fast.
Description: A passenger vessel was heading towards the dock for repairs. The first tug was already made fast with a bridle on the stern and as the passenger vessel was approaching a buoy, the forward second tug was coming in to make fast on a bridle on the bow. The second tug was sent up the port sideline but as they went over to the starboard bow to send up the starboard line, the vessel got out of position and lost control causing the tug to be pulled by the already made fast port line stern first until they collided with the passenger vessel. The passenger vessel was quickly pulled to a stop using the first tug and the second tug was able to get back in the correct position and continue making fast the bridle. The speed of the passenger vessel was 4.2 knots which was agreed between the pilot and tug master prior to making fast. A contributing factor to the incident was that the port tow line was caught on a stern bollard of the second tug making the gog line useless and the pulling force right aft.

Short_Description: A cruise liner passenger fell in their cabin and dislocated their hip.
Description: The passenger was moving around their cabin. They lost their balance and fell, dislocating their artificial hip joint. No one witnessed the event. Their spouse found them less than 5 minutes later. The passenger had a history of mobility issues and had limited feeling in their legs.

Short_Description: General cargo vessel made contact with lock with minor damage.
Description: General cargo vessel made contact with lock with minor damage. A lock's gates closed as the ship was passing through, causing contact damage.
Damage_Description: Damage to shell plating (dent). One 10 cm split in plating above waterline.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel crewmember injured their hand whilst rope handling during the vessel's berthing.
Description: A crewmember on a cargo vessel injured their hand whilst rope handling during a vessel's cold move along berth. They were operating the winch when their right hand became trapped. This caused a cut to the area between the thumb and forefinger and suspected fractures to of two fingers of their right hand. They were treated at the scene by first aiders and conveyed to hospital. They were unable to return to work and repatriation was arranged.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel's standby battery exploded during testing of the emergency generator.
Description: A cargo vessel's standby battery exploded during testing of the emergency generator. The explosion was due to a build up of gases and a faulty battery. The batteries were replaced and tested weekly.

Short_Description: A cruise ship crewmember had a fracture after a crane failure.
Description: A cruise ship crewmember had a fractured metatarsal after a crane failure. The vessel was drifting, hoisting a cylinder liner when the hoisting wire of the crane snapped. The liner fell and hit the left foot of a crewmember. They had a fracture to the left second metatarsal and were escorted to hospital.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel fouled their propeller and was towed by another fishing vessel to its mooring.
Description: A fishing vessel fouled their propeller and drifted in a harbour. Another fishing vessel provided assistance and towed the casualty vessel back to its moorings.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel nearly made contact with the quayside.
Description: Whilst a general cargo vessel was undertaking birthing operations the vessel came close to making contact with the quayside. The anchor was quickly deployed and the bow thrusters were used to avoid making contact with the quayside.

Short_Description: An offshore supply vessel made minor contact with a bridge abutment.
Description: A offshore supply vessel made minor contact with a bridge abutment during inward transit resulting in cosmetic damage to the ship.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger vessel made contact with a fender pile whilst manoeuvring alongside resulting in hull damage.
Description: A ro-ro passenger vessel's stern on the starboard side made contact with the outboard fender pile as the vessel was manoeuvring alongside. This resulted in the walkway between the fender pile and the main stern ramp structure being pushed back out of alignment. The vessel sustained hull damage caused by a steel box section that was part of the fender support frame. No persons were injured.
Damage_Description: The vessel sustained damage causing a 2ft sq hole caused by a steel box section that was part of fender support frame being sheered.

Short_Description: A cruise ship had a fuel leak that was contained onboard.
Description: A cruise ship diesel generator had a fuel leak on the main fuel supply line. The spill was contained within the pipe insulation, all leaked fuel was then directed into the bilge, approximately 200 litres. On investigation it was the small adapter insert in the valve that failed in both cases.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel collided with a moored cargo vessel.
Description: A cargo vessel with a pilot on board was proceeding to its berth when it collided with a moored cargo vessel. The starboard quarter of the berthing vessel made contact with the port bow of the moored vessel. Both vessels had superficial damage. The pilot misjudged the strength of the current.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel collided with a moored cargo vessel.
Description: A cargo vessel with a pilot on board was proceeding to its berth when it collided with a moored cargo vessel. The starboard quarter of the berthing vessel made contact with the port bow of the moored vessel. Both vessels had superficial damage. The pilot misjudged the strength of the current.

Short_Description: A yacht had water ingress after making contact with a container.
Description: A yacht had water ingress after making contact with a container resulting in a 0.3 metre gash in the port side (forward) of the vessel. The yacht made its way to port where the skipper attempted to bail the water using the on board pump. This was unsuccessful and a fire crew were called bringing an extra pump, this also failed to control the water ingress. The vessel was lifted out of the water to repair damage. The container was located by the port authority and removed as to not pose as a future navigational hazard.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting marine infrastructure or other ship

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged to SOLAS regulations.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged to SOLAS regulations. The ladder had a trap door arrangement.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel crewmember went overboard whilst hauling nets.
Description: A fishing vessel was hauling its nets, the cod end was heaved aboard but it was not sat correctly in the reception hopper. A crewmember went to correct the problem at which point, as they pulled on the net, the net mesh gave way and they stumbled, fell backwards and went overboard. The crewmember was not wearing a lifejacket but was quickly recovered by the fishing vessel's other crew, a search and rescue (SAR) vessel was deployed to assess the crewmember due to location of vessel. The SAR crewmember requested an ambulance to meet the fishing vessel once returned to harbour. Once ashore the crewmember was passed into the care of the ambulance service.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. Choke shackles were used over the side ropes at the top of the pilot ladder.

Short_Description: A passenger vessel had an overheating engine, but made its own way back to port.
Description: A passenger vessel had an overheating engine, but made its own way back to port.  A patrol vessel escorted the vessel back.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel struck a submerged object and lost propulsion.
Description: A sailing vessel struck an unidentified, submerged object as it was proceeding through a marked channel whilst returning to port. As a result of the contact, the vessel lost propulsion. The two person crew reported a speed of less than one knot and dark smoke emitting from the stern, following the contact.
Damage_Description: Minor damage, smoke seen following grounding.

Short_Description: A research vessel crewmember injured their shoulder whilst climbing a ladder.
Description: A crewmember was climbing a vertical ladder to move from the container lobby to the hangar top one deck above. While part way up the ladder, the crewmember felt a popping sensation in their right shoulder. The crewmember was able to move their shoulder with a good range of movement and with only minor pain so continued to work. The following day, the crewmember climbed a small vertical ladder from the lifeboat embarkation point. While climbing this ladder, crewmember felt another popping sensation and significant shoulder pain, which left them feeling physically sick. They reported their injury and medical treatment ashore was arranged.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged in compliance with SOLAS guidance.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged in compliance with SOLAS guidance. The pilot ladder was secured with a chain.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel fouled its gear, but managed to retrieve gear and no assistance was required.
Description: A fishing vessel fouled its gear, but managed to retrieve gear and no assistance was required.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel had an engine fire
Description: A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was idling at a harbour entrance when an alarm activation was noted by a crew member. The alarm was due to a flame detector activation over the starboard engine. CCTV was checked and indicated a flickering of a flame at the aft end of the starboard engine. A crewmember looked through the engine room door glass and confirmed a fire, then entered with a CO2 extinguisher. The CO2 extinguisher extinguished the fire. The port engine remained running to enable manoeuvring and the decision was made to beach the SAR vessel. After beaching, the fire service attended to confirm the fire was extinguished.
Damage_Description: Smoke damage around the turbo and lagging

Short_Description: A cruise ship discharged untreated waste within the twelve nautical mile limit.
Description: A cruise ship discharged approximately ten cubic metres of sea water contaminated with untreated sewage during a flushing operation. This occurred within the twelve nautical mile zone from the shore.

Short_Description: A yacht broke free of its moorings and was towed.
Description: A yacht with two people on board broke free of its moorings. The vessel was unable to make way with the engine and was being pushed onto rocks. A lifeboat was tasked to rescue it and return it to a mooring.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser skipper fell and had a suspected fractured ankle.
Description: A lone skipper onboard a moored motor cruiser fell and sustained a suspected fractured ankle. An ambulance was called and on arrival assessed the skipper. The skipper decided they did not want to go to hospital. The skipper wanted to stay onboard overnight and decide the following morning if they wanted to go to hospital.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser fouled its propeller and was towed back to port.
Description: A motor cruiser fouled its propeller and was towed back to port by a search and rescue vessel.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel was entering a harbour and grounded on a sandbar.
Description: A fishing vessel was entering a harbour and grounded on a sandbar, the tide was ebbing resulting in the vessel listing heavily. Once the tide was on the flood, the vessel came off the sandbar and safely into the harbour. The previous week had been easterly winds and it is a known issue that following easterlies the sandbank moves and often increases in size. There were no indications of damage to the vessel but it was put onto a slipway and inspected.

Short_Description: A motor vessel was towed by a lifeboat after a fire which was extinguished.
Description: Two search and rescue vessels were tasked to a motor vessel with three people on board that had reported having a fire. On arrival the fire appeared extinguished, but the lifeboat towed the vessel to harbour were the fire and rescue service assessed the vessel and declared it safe. One casualty was treated for smoke inhalation.

Short_Description: A search and rescue craft made contact with a casualty vessel
Description: A search and rescue craft was effecting a rescue to a casualty vessel when a wave caught the search and rescue craft, causing it to collide with the casualty vessel. The damage sustained to the search and rescue craft was minor to no damage and the damage sustained by the casualty vessel was some bent hand rails and paint transfer to the hull.

Short_Description: A multi-purpose service vessel broke down and was drifting and arranged a tow.
Description: A multi-purpose service ship broke down and was drifting. The vessel had to arrange a tow. No injuries or damage were reported.

Short_Description: A general cargo ship crewmember fell down the stairs and sustained a head injury.
Description: A general cargo crewmember fell coming down the stairs. The casualty fell from around two meters height and sustained a head injury.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. The ladder was secured by a deck tongue and shackles.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser collided with a chain ferry.
Description: The chain ferry had just reached its destination when a recreational motor cruiser hit the back of the ferry and carried on without stopping. The skipper of the motor cruiser had misjudged the course of the vessel and the tide. No major damage or injuries were sustained.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser collided with a chain ferry.
Description: The chain ferry had just reached its destination when a recreational motor cruiser hit the back of the ferry and carried on without stopping. The skipper of the motor cruiser had misjudged the course of the vessel and the tide. No major damage or injuries were sustained.

Short_Description: A vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per current SOLAS regulations.
Description: A vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per current SOLAS regulations. The ladder was secured by a deck tongue, an attempt was made to use the side ropes but they were of insufficient size and all the weight was on the ladder step.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier had a fire in one of the cargo holds which was extinguished.
Description: There was a fire in a cargo hold of a bulk carrier that was quickly extinguished. No emergency services were required.

Short_Description: A tanker crewmember cut off their finger with a knife.
Description: A tanker crewmember severed the top half of their fourth finger on their right hand with a knife in the galley. The casualty was taken to hospital.

Short_Description: A general cargo's pilot ladder was not rigged in compliance with SOLAS guidance.
Description: A general cargo's pilot ladder was not rigged in compliance with SOLAS guidance.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel under tow had a near miss after the tow line parted.
Description: A disabled fishing vessel was being towed back to harbour by another fishing vessel when the towline parted. The fishing vessel started to drift towards a breakwater where there was a significant risk of grounding. A search and rescue vessel was deployed and towed the vessel back to harbour.

Short_Description: An oil tanker's mooring line parted whilst under tension.
Description: An oil tanker was preparing to depart a lock when the forward spring mooring line parted whilst under tension. No injuries to crew or shore operatives occurred.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had engine failure and was towed.
Description: A fishing vessel had engine failure. The engine's water pump had stopped working. An anchor was deployed but the vessel started to drift as the anchor was not holding. Due to the proximity to the shoreline, a search and rescue vessel was tasked to tow the vessel to a harbour.

Short_Description: A ro-pax vessel that was alongside broke a mooring bollard during high winds.
Description: A ro-pax vessel was alongside, overnight there were winds gusting up to 25 knots. It was noticed by the shore staff that the vessel was slightly off the berth and it was discovered that the vessel's morning line had pulled the bollard almost off the dockside. The vessel's mooring line was moved to another bollard.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel experienced engine failure and was towed to an anchorage.
Description: A fishing vessel experienced engine failure and was towed to an anchorage position.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. On disembarking the vessel, the pilot noticed that the pilot ladder was showing signs of ageing and the lashings were old.

Short_Description: Duplicate of 4036/2021
Description: Duplicate of 4036/2021

Short_Description: Duplicate of 4040/2021.
Description: Duplicate of 4040/2021.

Short_Description: A sail training vessel lost propulsion and there was no wind so a tow back to its mooring was arranged.
Description: A sailing training yacht engine failed in a precautionary area and the yacht started to drift in the tide. Another company vessel was nearby so a tow was arranged back to its mooring near by.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel began taking on water and required supplementary pumps in order to remain afloat.
Description: A sailing vessel began taking on water and required supplementary pumps in order to remain afloat. They were they towed back to harbour by SAR (search and rescue) craft.

Short_Description: A cruise ship crewmember fell backwards off a kitchen counter injuring their back.
Description: The crewmember was cleaning the ceiling in the pot wash area of the crew galley. In order to clean the ceiling they were standing on top of the basin unit. The crewmember slipped while performing the task and as they fell backwards they grabbed hold of a commercial rinse faucet which broke and they landed on top of the basin unit injuring their lower back.

Short_Description: A passenger vessel crewmember slipped on deck and fell overboard. No injuries were sustained.
Description: A crewmember was working on board a passenger vessel whilst it was alongside when they slipped on the deck and fell overboard. Help was provided by a nearby vessel also alongside. The crewmember was not wearing a lifejacket and they were recovered uninjured.

Short_Description: A yacht ran aground and one person was rescued.
Description: A yacht ran aground and the one person on board was rescued.

Short_Description: A yacht grounded.
Description: A yacht grounded and was escorted to port by a lifeboat.

Short_Description: An angling vessel crewmember severed their finger after their hand got stuck in a winch.
Description: Crew member on a single handed angling vessel severed their finger after getting their hand stuck in a winch. A search and rescue vessel met the vessel and brought the casualty on board and towed the vessel back to port where they were met by an ambulance.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser owner spilt diesel on the engine causing it to smoke. It was towed to safety.
Description: A motor cruiser with two people on board was towed to safety after a report of a fire. However, it transpired that the owner over-filled the fuel tank and diesel spilt onto the engine which produced lots of smoke when the engine warmed up . There was no fire damage or injuries.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel fouled their propeller and was towed to safety due to its close proximity to rocks.
Description: A sailing vessel with three people on board fouled their propeller on a pot or buoy. A lifeboat was tasked due to the dangerous nature of the area and they were close to rocks. An angling vessel also assisted and the casualty vessel was taken to safety. There were no reports of damage to the vessel.

Short_Description: A passenger vessel ran aground.
Description: A passenger ship ran aground. The skipper attempted to manoeuvre the vessel off rocks, but was unable to do so. A passenger called for help and assistance was provided from the local lifeboat. The passengers were transferred to the lifeboat whilst the skipper remained on the vessel to make the tow back to port. The vessel was taken ashore and the extent of the damage was assessed as rendering the vessel unable to proceed.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship
Damage_Description: Damage to the rudder, propeller, and stern of vessel

Short_Description: A private hire boat made contact with the underside of a bridge when navigating a rising lock and partially flooded.
Description: A private hire boat was navigating a  river, through a lock. As the water level in the lock rose, the vessel made contact with the underside of a swing-bridge (that needed to be raised prior to filling the lock) and partially flooded. Assistance was given by nearby members of the public and the boat was re-floated. The lock in question was beyond the designated route boundary as set out by the hire company. The hirers either ignored the boundary or did not know they had exceeded it and either did not see or pay attention to signage relating to the swing-bridge at the lock.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship

Short_Description: A child boarding a passenger vessel fell between the vessel and the pontoon and was recovered.
Description: A child was boarding a passenger vessel unassisted when they fell between the vessel and the pontoon. The crew left the vessel and grabbed the child's right arm and lifted them from the water. Apart from being wet and distressed, the child was uninjured.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel experienced propulsion failure after the shaft become detached from its housing.
Description: A search and rescue vessel experienced propulsion failure when its outboard engine's propeller dropped off. The vessel was rescued by another search and rescue vessel.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel made contact with a lock.
Description: A general cargo vessel was passing through a lock when the portside mid rails came into contact with the edge of the lock. No damage was reported to vessel or lock.

Short_Description: A SAR Hovercraft grounded and became stuck due to ballasting by the stern.
Description: A SAR (search and rescue) hovercraft was searching for a missing person. They were stood down and while flying overland on return to the lifeboat station, the craft lost its ability to make way and became bogged down. The craft was made safe while the team waited for the tide to come in. Investigation found the ballast in the craft had all been set to the stern of the craft. This meant they were flying rear heavy and collected mud and sand in the skirts resulting in the craft losing lift.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged to SOLAS regulations.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged to SOLAS regulations. The ladder was running from the deck not in a straight line and then shackled underneath the combination ladder platform. The crew were told vessel to re-rig the ladder using two ropes on the ladder to strong point on deck. The pilot advised the master to remove the shackles and use the ladder rigged from the deck and magnets in combination.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. The inward pilot boarded using a trapdoor arrangement. It wasn’t until they were at the platform that they noticed the arrangement was noncompliant and the safest option was to continue rather than go down the ladder. The trap door arrangement has been modified but consisted of two ladders - one was hung from below the platform and the second was supported in an A-frame above the platform. There were no designated strongpoints to secure the ladder. The ladder was lashed using a number of different knots around a piece of angle iron supporting a fire hydrant. The ladder was not secured to the ship's side at a point 1.5m above the lower platform but at platform level. The accommodation ladder wasn’t secured to the ships side.

Short_Description: An offshore supply ship nearly veered outside the navigable channel whilst under pilotage.
Description: An offshore supply vessel was under pilotage and at the request of the pilot, the vessel was on manual steering. The vessel veered to starboard and the master immediately noted this and stopped the engines, applying a stern motion using the vessel's port bow thruster to reposition the vessel. The ship remained in the navigable channel in the harbour, avoided grounding and continued on passage.

Short_Description: An offshore supply ship was having its tank cleaned when a shore side worker fell and injured their leg.
Description: An offshore supply ship was having its tank cleaned by a shore side worker. The worker slipped, fell and caught their leg causing them to fracture their leg. Their supervisor above spotted the casualty lying on the deck and raised the alarm. The casualty was recovered by fire and rescue personnel and passed into the care of the ambulance service.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel hit rocks and was a total loss.
Description: Fishing vessel was proceeding under auto-helm at approximately eight knots. The skipper did not appear to have seen that the vessel was heading towards rocks and subsequently grounded. The vessel was a constructive total loss.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger vessel crewmember strained their back whilst heaving in a line.
Description: A crewmember on a ro-ro ferry strained their back whilst heaving in a line during departure from its mooring resulting in them being signed off work.

Short_Description: A leisure fishing vessel grounded and was towed by search and rescue services.
Description: A leisure fishing vessel ran aground and was towed by search and rescue services. They ran aground after experiencing engine failure. There was no damage to the vessel or injuries to the crew.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel's various lines parted during discharge.
Description: During discharge the breast-line aft parted, both anchors were deployed to assist. Also a headline and aft spring parted and vessel stern slid another  five meters to thirty metres from the quay.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel crewmember sustained a finger injury after it was caught between a rope and a railing.
Description: A fishing vessel was hauling nets and a crewmember was connecting ropes when they got their finger trapped between a rope that went tight and a rail resulting in a fractured finger. The crewmember went to hospital where the affected part of the finger was removed.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel had a small fire in trim plane motor.
Description: A search and rescue vessel was exiting a harbour for a boat handling course. The boat's trim plane was used, the control button stayed on and would not turn back off. Attempts were made to reset the unit but it did not work. A smoke alarm was heard within the jet space of the boat. The alarm was acknowledged and investigated using the boat's CCTV (closed circuit television). Smoke was noticed so the crew members isolated the systems and went down to see if it was possible to extinguish the fire with a portable fire extinguisher. It was then confirmed that a small fire had been seen and  Co2 was used to put it out. Once the fire was confirmed to be out, the space was vented and the unit was inspected. Isolation was continued and monitored as the vessel made its way back into port.

Short_Description: A tug crewmember descended stairs from the bridge to the deck and slipped resulting in multiple injuries.
Description: A crewmember was in the process of descending stairs from the bridge to the deck when they slipped and fell 2.5 meters bruising their back, toes and sustaining a right shoulder ligament strain. They where taken to a fracture clinic where they were checked over and signed off work for three weeks.

Short_Description: An offshore supply vessel made contact with the quay during berthing operations.
Description: An offshore supply vessel was approaching the berth. When it was close to its final position, the vessel then sheered slowly away from the intended quay. The pilot advised the master to stop the sheer. The master then over compensated and the vessel swung violently back towards the berth and contacted it with its starboard quarter. The pilot thought the master went the wrong way on the controls and had problems adjusting the power. The master admitted it was their first time docking alone. The pilot mentioned that the vessel is hard to steer due to its design. The vessel had a CPP (controllable pitch propeller) and two bow thrusters. There was a scrape to the side of the vessel.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier's pilot later was in poor condition and without a certificate.
Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder had no certificate for one of the ladders. The other was impregnated with scrap shards inside ropes.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel briefly grounded on rocks whilst launching
Description: A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was tasked to an incident, whilst launching the engine's skeg and propeller briefly grounded on rocks due to the swell. This resulted in minor damage to the propeller and skeg but it did not impact the operations at the time and no crew were injured.

Short_Description: A survey vessel contractor broke a bone after falling.
Description: Contractor broke a bone is their left foot as a result of a fall. They were leaving the vessel by the starboard forward door from the laboratory to the hanger deck. They stepped onto the edge between the wooden decking and the steel deck and fell onto the wooden deck. They were not wearing protective footwear.

Short_Description: A lifeboat's tow rail parted during a rescue operation, injuring a crewmember's knee.
Description: A lifeboat was carrying out an alongside tow, securing spring rope attached from the lifeboat to the casualty vessel, when the casualty vessel rolled onto the lifeboat, causing tow rail to part and injure a crewmember.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged to SOLAS regulations.

Short_Description: A catamaran grounded and took on water. A lifeboat towed the vessel to harbour with no injuries.
Description: A catamaran with two people on board ran aground and started to flood as one of the hulls was breached. A sailing vessel stood by the casualty until the lifeboat arrived and towed them to harbour after installing pumps. There were no injuries.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting structural integrity of the ship
Damage_Description: One of the hulls was breached.

Short_Description: A passenger ship experienced a small fire in a waste silo.
Description: Waste disposal operators on board a passenger ship discovered a small fire within the waste silo. The vessels incinerator had been shutdown the morning prior and consequently meant that no damage had been caused to the silo - as far as could be seen on a visual inspection. The crew discharged a water and CO2 extinguishers as well as the silo's water mist system.

Short_Description: A tug crewmember twisted their ankle in the accommodation.
Description: A tug crewmember twisted their ankle after trying to go to the bathroom in the dark. They misjudged the bathroom step resulting in a twisted ankle. The crewmember had five days off work as a result of the injury.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel with water was ingress towed to shore.
Description: A fishing vessel experienced water ingress and was keeping it under control with an onboard pump but later required a tow from to get back to port.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship
Damage_Description: Failed stern seal. Water ingress greater that vessel's pumping capacity.

Short_Description: An oil tanker's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS standards.
Description: An oil tanker's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS standards. It was a combination ladder. Access from the straight ladder to the accommodation ladder was via a trapdoor. The pilot ladder stopped at platform level , rather than extending to the accommodation ladder handrail level. The pilots had to lean back to grab a hand hold and then step up from ladder to the access the platform rather than simply stepping across. A crewmember was required to assist the pilots at the bottom of the accommodation ladder.

Short_Description: A sailing yacht fouled its propeller and was towed back to port.
Description: A sailing yacht fouled its propeller and was towed back to port by a search and rescue vessel.

Short_Description: A motorboat grounded, refloated and was towed by a lifeboat.
Description: A motorboat grounded, managed to refloat successfully with assistance from a lifeboat and was towed to a marina. There was no water ingress.

Short_Description: A SAR craft reported a grounding causing minor damage to the propeller.
Description: A SAR (search and rescue) vessel conducted a net recovery onto its carriage on completion of a scheduled exercise. During the recovery in a confused sea the port propeller made contact with the carriage. Both aft springs were on and the engines were running astern.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel fouled its propeller and was towed back to port.
Description: A fishing vessel with one person on board fouled its propeller on a pot marker and a lifeboat attended, freed the pot marker, then towed the vessel back to port. The tow was transferred from the initial lifeboat to another lifeboat for operational reasons.

Short_Description: A training ship crewmember was injured after winch failure.
Description: A sail training vessel crewmember was evacuated from the vessel via helicopter after injuring their hand and head after a winch failure. The block parted under load and struck the casualty.

Short_Description: A service ship's mechanical component overheated, causing smoke to be emitted and fire alarms to sound.
Description: After departure from port, en-route to an offshore survey site, a fire alarm was triggered from the steering room and tween deck of a service ship. Some smoke was also sighted at this time near the controlled pitch propeller (CPP). Upon inspection, it was observed that the smoke was coming from CPP housing following which the engine was stopped immediately for further assessment. Upon inspection, it was found that the aft bearing on CPP housing had overheated and got damaged. At this time vessel was clear from all traffic with no injuries or any risk of pollution. Vessel safely anchored for further assessment and assistance from their ship management office.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel fouled its propeller and was towed back to port by another vessel.
Description: A fishing vessel fouled its propeller and was towed back to port by another vessel.

Short_Description: A RIB went aground and then sank at high tide. All persons were rescued with no injuries.
Description: A RIB (rigid inflatable boat) with three people on board grounded on mud. The lifeboat extracted a child from the vessel whilst the two remaining people on board waited to refloat. As the vessel refloated, the vessel started to sink and the two people were rescued by the lifeboat.

Short_Description: A yacht hit unknown object and required a tow.
Description: A yacht hit an unknown object in the water and started drifting.  A privately owned vessel towed the yacht to a nearby buoy and a rescue vessel towed the yacht to its final destination. No damage was confirmed.

Short_Description: A racing powerboat crashed into the water at speed after a steering failure resulting in damage and crew injuries.
Description: A racing powerboat crashed into the water at speed after a steering failure resulting in damage and crew injuries.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting structural integrity of the ship

Short_Description: An oil tanker's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS.
Description: An oil tanker's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: A cargo vessel's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. The pilot ladder was rigged incorrectly. The spreader was across the inside of the gate posts with no lashings.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had engine failure and was towed back to port
Description: A fishing vessel had engine failure after their fuel became contaminated. The vessel with the two crew was towed back to port by a lifeboat.

Short_Description: A general cargo made contact with the breakwater whilst approaching a harbour entrance.
Description: A general cargo vessel was approaching the harbour entrance when the ship did not respond with a port swing required to approach to the channel. It was as a result of gusting wind. The bow came into contact with the breakwater. No persons were injured and no damage was reported.
Damage_Description: Vessel sustained damage over a length of around 8-9m along the starboard bow above the uppermost continuous deck at the apron and down into the forecastle store area. Indentations of approximately 3-5cm maximum between frames over a height of around 30-45 cm with heavy scuffing. No frames tripped, no cracks and no buckling. Vessel sailed on completion of cargo with no requirements from class.

Short_Description: Investigated by another state
Description: Investigated by another state
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting structural integrity of the ship

Short_Description: A tug reported a fire in its starboard engine during tug operations.
Description: Whilst a tug was pushing up on a vessel, fire alarms were set off in the engine room. The crew were mustered investigated. A fire was reported on the starboard engine. Emergency shutdown on the starboard engine was initiated immediately. Fuel came into contact with a hot surface and ignited. The fire was started because the lay of a low-pressure fuel hose was rubbing on a corner of the engine cover. Although the fuel hose is specified for fuel, the way the hose was clipped to other pipework meant it had contact with a small piece of steel sticking up and over time this cut into the hose causing a leak. The flames from the fire then melted the hose (for the pressure gauge on the end of the inlet manifold) which then allowed pressurised air to fan the flames.

Short_Description: A yacht reported a broken mast and was towed to shore.
Description: A yacht reported a broken mast and was towed to shore.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel's engine failed and a tow was arranged with another fishing vessel.
Description: A beam trawler with four people on board had engine failure. The skipper arranged a tow from another fishing vessel. Both vessels arrived back safely in port the next day.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser's engine overheated, resulting in a tow.
Description: A recreational motor boat with six people on board lost propulsion after their engine overheated and stopped, necessitating a tow from another vessel.
Damage_Description: Overheated engine leading to engine seizure

Short_Description: A sailing yacht collided with another yacht during a race, resulting in material damage and a minor injury.
Description: A sailing vessel with three crew was taking part in a race when another sailing vessel collided with them amidships. The casualty vessel's hull was penetrated resulting in minimal water ingress and bruised ribs for one crewmember. The other vessel left the scene. The casualty vessel was taken to harbour and inspected for further damage.

Short_Description: A sailing yacht collided with another yacht during a race, resulting in material damage and a minor injury.
Description: A sailing vessel with three crew was taking part in a race when another sailing vessel collided with them amidships. The casualty vessel's hull was penetrated resulting in minimal water ingress and bruised ribs for one crewmember. The other vessel left the scene. The casualty vessel was taken to harbour and inspected for further damage.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting structural integrity of the ship
Damage_Description: Hit midships and there was penetration of the hull. Minimal water ingress and the vessel will be inspected thoroughly.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel was dismasted and one person sustained a head and hand injury.
Description: A sailing vessel with two people on board was dismasted with one crewmember sustaining a head and a hand injury. First responders provided initial care before handing the casualty to the ambulance team. The vessel was escorted into the harbour and the mast cleared from the tiller to enable the vessel to steer back to its berth.

Short_Description: A vehicle carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A vehicle carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.

Short_Description: A commercial yacht had a fire in the saloon.
Description: A commercial sailing yacht experienced a fire in the galley, underneath the grill that holds pots and pans above the ring burner. The fire was not from the ring burner. The crew used a fire blanket but were unable to get an air tight seal and deployed a powder extinguisher which put the fire out but filled the cabin space with powder and smoke.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel briefly grounded whilst being recovered
Description: A lifeboat was returning to a slipway for boat house recovery when the rudder stock made contact with the slipway structure. A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was returning to the slipway for recovery when the rudder stock briefly grounded on the slipway structure before the keel located itself in to the keel way on the slipway. The rudder stock sustained damage, no reported crew injuries.

Short_Description: A sailing yacht had water ingress from the propeller shaft
Description: A sailing yacht started taking on water, the onboard pump was not able to cope with the water ingress. The lone skipper radioed for assistance, a search and rescue (SAR) vessel was tasked to assist. The SAR vessel pumped out the water and found the ingress was coming from the propeller shaft. The ingress stopped when the engine was not used. The skipper was happy to continue their passage under sail and then required assistance to a berth upon arrival..

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS.

Short_Description: A product tanker's crew threw weighted heaving line.
Description: A product tanker's crew threw weighted heaving line.

Short_Description: A yacht crewmember fell and injured their arm.
Description: A crewmember had a fall on-board a yacht which resulted in a puncture wound to their arm.

Short_Description: A sailing yacht lost its rudder and required towage.
Description: A sailing yacht lost its rudder and required towage.

Short_Description: A recreational fishing vessel had water ingress and foundered.
Description: The vessel had started to take on water, a tow was attempted however it sank with all four persons evacuated safely off and no injuries were confirmed to any crew members.

Short_Description: General cargo ship crewmember was hit by a winch after a mooring line got caught in the propeller and ripped the fitting from the deck.
Description: A crewmember threw the heaving line ashore, the shore worker began to heave the line ashore, however, the heaving line came away from the mooring line. This resulted in the line falling into the dock. It then got caught around the propeller pulling on the rope and breaking the winch off its fittings. The winch subsequently hit a crew member's thigh before falling in the dock. The crewmember was taken away to the hospital for further treatment for a suspected broken femur.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel collided with an anchored yacht.
Description: A fishing vessel collided with an anchored yacht whilst sorting out its fishing gear. There was damage to the yacht which had to start bailing to reduce the water ingress. A lifeboat was requested to assist. The fishing vessel towed the yacht to the marina where it was placed on a slipway. There were no injuries sustained.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting marine infrastructure or other ship
Damage_Description: Damage caused water ingress and had to be assisted with pumping.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel collided with an anchored yacht.
Description: A fishing vessel collided with an anchored yacht whilst sorting out its fishing gear. There was damage to the yacht which had to start bailing to reduce the water ingress. A lifeboat was requested to assist. The fishing vessel towed the yacht to the marina where it was placed on a slipway. There were no injuries sustained.

Short_Description: A sailing yacht grounded.
Description: A sailing yacht grounded at the entrance to a harbour and was towed free.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser crewmember fell and injured their head.
Description: Whilst mooring a motor cruiser, one of the crew members slipped and fell into the hold resulting in a minor head injury.

Short_Description: A passenger ship crewmember sustained a concussion after hitting their head on the upper frame of a walk in freezer.
Description: A ro-ro passenger vessel crewmember hit their head on the upper door frame as they exited a walk-in freezer. The casualty did not report the incident at the time but later experienced headaches and vomiting. They were diagnosed with concussion and signed off work.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel could not start their engine and was towed by another fishing vessel.
Description: A fishing vessel was at anchor and could not restart their engine due to a flat battery. Another fishing vessel provided a tow to harbour where a new battery was fitted.

Short_Description: An oil tanker's pilot ladder was not rigged in compliance with SOLAS guidance.
Description: An oil tanker's pilot ladder was not rigged in compliance with SOLAS guidance.

Short_Description: An inland waterway vessel had a crewmember overboard who sustained minor graze on their forehead.
Description: A tug's crewmembers were preparing to board empty barges that were being towed from the tug's stern. One crewmember slipped from stern fender and entered water between the tug and barge. The crewmember was recovered from the water. There was a superficial injury to the crewmember's head. A search and rescue vessel was tasked to the tug to assess the crewmember who then went to hospital for further checks after the immersion. The crewmember was wearing a lifejacket.
Lat_Long_Unknown: River Thames near Grosvenor Railway bridge

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel hit a piece of driftwood during a training exercise.
Description: A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was on a training exercise with three crew on board. Whilst proceeding at 20 knots, the vessel struck a submerged object. Once the vessel stopped the crew looked behind and saw it was a submerged piece of driftwood. The crew had not noticed it before as it was not visible on the surface before the vessel struck it. The outboard engine cowling came off, but was retrieved and refitted. No other damage to the vessel or injuries to the crew were reported.
Damage_Description: Outboard engine cowling came off but was retrieved and refitted.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: A cargo vessel's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. The pilot ladder's securing ropes, made fast to the cleats on deck, resulted in it being impossible to safely position the steps, without a significant gap between the access steps and the ship's bulwark. The pilot had advised vessel on two previous recent occasions. The master was asked to resolve this issue prior to the vessel's return.

Short_Description: A service ship crewmember's fingers became trapped in a mooring rope.
Description: During mooring operations, a crewmember's finger became trapped between the eye of the mooring rope and the barge bollard. As the rope tightened on the bollard , the crewmember's fingers became trapped until slack could be given and their fingers freed.

Short_Description: A speed boat occupant on ring had leg injuries from a propeller and was taken to hospital.
Description: An occupant of a speedboat with three people on board was in an inflatable ring being towed behind the speedboat when they fell into the water. The driver of the boat passed to check the occupant, when they put the throttle astern inadvertently while untangling the kill cord. The throttle was put into neutral immediately but the boat reversed up to the occupant in the water and caught their legs in the still turning propeller causing deep lacerations to both legs and ankle. The casualty was recovered and taken to hospital.

Short_Description: A RIB passenger fell in the water whilst disembarking the boat. They were recovered uninjured.
Description: A passenger on a commercial RIB (Rigid Inflatable Boat) ride was exiting the vessel when they fell into the water. They ascended some steps fitted in the bow but as they stepped down onto the pontoon their trailing leg caught the RIB tube and they lost their balance and fell into the water. Their lifejacket inflated and they were recovered from the water and passed into the care of an ambulance team who discharged them with no injuries.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel crewmember sustained injuries to their arm and hand.
Description: A fishing vessel crewmember sustained injuries to their fingers and arm when the cod end of their nets were lowered and the crewmember had not let go of a line attached to the cod end. The momentum of the cod end being lowered pulled the crewmember's hand over the vessels side rail, hitting it on its way past.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel experienced steering failure and was towed back to its mooring.
Description: A fishing vessel experienced steering failure. A search and rescue vessel was tasked to tow the vessel back to its mooring where the three crew on board were transferred from the vessel to the shore.

Short_Description: A tug grounded.
Description: A tug grounded whilst assisting a vessel leaving a berth.

Short_Description: A charter vessel had flooding to its port engine room due to the propeller shaft seal failing.
Description: A charter vessel had flooding in the port engine room. The port engine room bilge alarm sounded and it was pumped dry but flooded again. The flooding was traced to the port propeller shaft seal. The vessel diverted to port for repair.
Damage_Description: Flooding to port engine room as cutlass bearing failed

Short_Description: An oil tanker's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: An oil tanker's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. The accommodation platform was less than five metres above the water. Due to the vessel's partially loaded condition the crew could not adjust the length. The ladder was not secured to strong points and instead was tied to hand rails.

Short_Description: A cruise ship crewmember slipped over and has a suspected fracture in the neck.
Description: The crewmember was preparing vegetables and when storing them, whilst coming out of the area, they slipped injuring themselves. The crewmember had a suspected neck fracture and was taken to hospital for further check ups as the x-ray on board the cruise ship was inconclusive.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel had damage to the propeller and skeg after hitting a shipwreck.
Description: A search and rescue vessel was on a training exercise when it struck the remains of a historic ship's boiler resulting in damaging the outboard engine's propellers and skeg. No pollution reported and no injuries to crew.

Short_Description: A mussel farm catamaran had a fire in the starboard engine room.
Description: A mussel farm catamaran detected smoke in the starboard engine room. The vessel made its own way to harbour on the port engine after closing the starboard engine space down and was met by the fire and rescue service (FRS). The FRS remained on site as safety cover until the smoke dissipated. The fire was believed to be electric in nature. No persons were injured.

Short_Description: Pilot vessel had water ingress and was towed by a lifeboat.
Description: The vessel became holed which resulted in water ingress and it was beached at the entrance of a harbour with lifeboat crews bringing pumps on board in order to assist.  All of the vessel's compartments were checked, they were deemed to be dry and afterwards, it was towed by a lifeboat into a harbour. The extent of the damage that was confirmed was a 70cm by 10cm gash.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting structural integrity of the ship

Short_Description: A sailing vessel grounded and crew had to be rescued with boat abandoned.
Description: A sailing vessel ran aground. A lifeboat was tasked but the boat was inaccessible. The two people on board were rescued and the vessel was abandoned until it could be refloated by the owner at a later date.

Short_Description: Investigated by another state
Description: Investigated by another state

Short_Description: A fishing vessel crewmember had burns after a boiling steam pot top blew off.
Description: A fishing vessel crewmember had second degree burns after the lid blew off a boiling pot and the contents inside spilled over the crewmember's upper torso. The vessel was escorted by the to calmer waters where the crewmember was then airlifted to hospital.

Short_Description: A workboat / fish carrier experienced propulsion failure, the anchor wouldn't hold and it was escorted back to harbour.
Description: The vessel was returning to port after harvesting salmon from a fish farm when the engine stopped unexpectedly. The vessel crew were unable to restart the engine and dropped the anchor. The anchor didn't hold and the vessel crew continued to try to restart the engine. The vessel was one nautical mile away from shore when the engine restarted. A lifeboat arrived on scene and escorted the vessel back into port.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel's propulsion failed resulting in a tow to port in order to conduct repairs.
Description: A general cargo vessel's propeller shaft failed after leaving port and the ship anchored to assess the damage. It could not be repaired on board. The ship remained at anchor for several days until a tow was arranged to port for repairs.

Short_Description: A tug grounded in a river.
Description: A tug grounded  in a river. No damage was reported and vessel continued on passage.

Short_Description: A yacht fouled its propeller and was assisted with clearing it.
Description: A sailing vessel with two crewmembers on board fouled its propeller. A local lifeboat provided a tow to port where a rope attached to two buoys was removed from the propeller. There were no injuries or damage.

Short_Description: A vehicle carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
