Description: A vehicle carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. There was a platform over the ladder, choke shackles over the side ropes and the spreader was against the stanchions. The ladder was in poor to average condition.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS. The pilot ladder was secured with a metal tongue and a locking bar underneath the platform. No side ropes were being used.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser experienced engine failure and was towed back to port.
Description: A motor cruiser experienced engine failure and was towed back to port.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel alongside experienced an engine fire. No reported casualties.
Description: A cargo vessel has had a small fire in a workshop, which was extinguished by the crew. There was minimal damage.
Damage_Description: Fire in the engine room. No more details as yet.

Short_Description: A fishing Vessel had multiple engine failures and was assisted to harbour by another vessel.
Description: A fishing vessel with two crewmembers on board had engine failure. A lifeboat was ready, but the fishing vessel managed to restart the engine. The engine failed again as they entered the harbour and they were assisted by another vessel back to their mooring.

Short_Description: A leisure fishing vessel required a tow due to an electrical failure.
Description: A leisure fishing vessel had electrical failure and the engine would not start. The lifeboat service decided that a tow was necessary as the vessel was dragging their anchor. There were two people on board who were uninjured and there was no damage to the vessel.

Short_Description: A RIB capsized and the crew managed to self recover.
Description: A RIB (rigid inflatable boat) with three people on board capsized. The boat was righted and all three persons were able to self recover into the boat. The kill cord for the engine was lost in the capsize and they had to paddle towards the slipway they had launched from. The alarm was raised and a lifeboat which was on exercise towed the boat back to the slipway. There were no injuries except for one occupant who was provided a blanket as they were cold.

Short_Description: A sailing yacht collided with an offshore supply vessel.
Description: A yacht and an offshore support vessel collided in a pilotage area. The interaction of the two vessels passing close to one another reportedly caused the collision.

Short_Description: A sailing yacht collided with an offshore supply vessel.
Description: A yacht and an offshore support vessel collided in a pilotage area. The interaction of the two vessels passing close to one another reportedly caused the collision.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had engine failure and was towed back to port.
Description: A fishing vessel had engine failure and was towed back to port.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. The rigging of the pilot ladder was not checked, or the embarkation and/or disembarkation of the pilot was not supervised by a watch keeping deck officer.

Short_Description: A vessel's pilot ladder was non-compliant with SOLAS
Description: During boarding two pilots onto the vessel, a large swell was running with a fresh 25 knot wind. The vessel had rigged a compliant ladder which was near the maximum nine metre length. The vessel was rolling in the swell causing the bottom five steps to land on the pilot boat deck. The specialist pilot boarded first without incident. During second pilot boarding, the swell caused them to move away taking the ladder with it. There was no damage or injury to the pilot.

Short_Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel's slackened spring line fell in the water close to an operating thruster.
Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel's forward spring line entered the water when the end of the rope, on shore, had become tangled. Whilst the shore workers where trying to untangle the rope, the vessel's crew kept feeding the rope not realising that the rope had slackened and was now in the water. This resulted in the spring line entering the water where there was a potential for it to get caught in the bow thruster.

Short_Description: A motor vessel's battery went flat and it was towed to safety.
Description: A motor vessel's battery went flat and it was towed to safety.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier had a collision with a cargo vessel.
Description: A bulk carrier with a pilot onboard was making the final approach to its berth. Once in the berthing area the master took the controls and began to slow the vessel. On passing a moored cargo vessel, the bulk carrier's speed was approximately 1.5knts, the bow thruster was full to starboard but having little effect. The rudder was put hard to starboard in an attempt to bring the bow out, the master then pressed the override button for main engine control. The bulk carrier's stern made contact with the starboard bow of the moored vessel and the carrier's bow then made heavy contact with a fender on a berth. The top section of the wooden fender splintered. Both vessels sustained minor damage.
Damage_Description: Superficial denting and scratching to the bow and anchor housing area

Short_Description: A bulk carrier had a collision with a cargo vessel.
Description: A bulk carrier with a pilot onboard was making the final approach to its berth. Once in the berthing area the master took the controls and began to slow the vessel. On passing a moored cargo vessel, the bulk carrier's speed was approximately 1.5knts, the bow thruster was full to starboard but having little effect. The rudder was put hard to starboard in an attempt to bring the bow out, the master then pressed the override button for main engine control. The bulk carrier's stern made contact with the starboard bow of the moored vessel and the carrier's bow then made heavy contact with a fender on a berth. The top section of the wooden fender splintered. Both vessels sustained minor damage.
Damage_Description: Damage to the port bow, port side stern guard rails, safety boat and safety boat cradle.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. Handholds were not securely fastened to the ship's bulwarks to enable the pilot to step safely and comfortably from the top of the ladder on to the ship's deck.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had engine failure and was towed back to port.
Description: A fishing vessel with three people on board had engine failure and was towed back to port by a lifeboat. The engine failure was attributed to a water pump issue.

Short_Description: A passenger vessel crewmember was nearly hit by a tractor.
Description: A small ro-pax vessel crewmember was nearly hit by a tractor with a defective handbrake. According to the crew this was the third incident of this type. In the previous two incidents the crewmember was in-between the tractor and the hitched trailer when the tractor moved.

Short_Description: A rubber dinghy capsized and two persons went overboard.
Description: A rubber dinghy capsized with two crew members ending up in the water who were recovered by lifeboat. They were both intoxicated and not wearing personal floatation devices.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel ran aground and was taking on water.
Description: A catamaran yacht ran aground on a rock and was holed in the right hull. The engine then failed as a result.  The crew issued a MAYDAY call and a lifeboat provided pumps and a tow to a local boatyard for repairs.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting structural integrity of the ship
Damage_Description: There was some water ingress on their right hull.

Short_Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. On disembarkation, the pilot ladder was secured using a deck tongue on the main deck.

Short_Description: A SAR vessel fouled its propeller resulting in a grounding on rocks.
Description: A SAR (search and rescue) vessel was attempting to tow a grounded vessel off the rocks of a harbour arm when its propeller became fouled in the towing line and it experienced propulsion failure. The crew of the SAR vessel raised the two outboard engines from the water and were blown onto the rocks of the harbour arm. The crew managed to free the fouled rope from the propellers and make their way to safe water. There were no injuries and the propellers were not damaged. There was cosmetic damage to the hull of the vessel, but no penetrating damage.

Short_Description: A hopper barge lost directional control and was towed.
Description: A hopper dredger experienced steering failure. A tug was put on standby to assist with a lifeboat on scene which towed the casualty to deeper water. It was decided to tow the vessel into port and was secured safely alongside.

Short_Description: An oil tanker's pilot ladder was not rigged in compliance with SOLAS guidance.
Description: An oil tanker's pilot ladder was not rigged in compliance with SOLAS guidance. The pilot ladder was not made fast with mechanical fastening.

Short_Description: A single handed skipper went overboard but was rescued
Description: A fishing vessel was preparing to shoot its nets, the lone skipper went inside the wheelhouse and removed their lifejacket and waterproofs. Before going on deck they put redressed but forgot to put their lifejacket on. The skipper shot the net and moved down the vessel, a rope whipped over the deck and caught the skippers leg. The skipper was taken overboard with the vessel still in gear. The skipper swam to a float to hold on and called the emergency services. Search and rescue (SAR) assets were tasked to the scene where the skipper was recovered.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel grounded during unberthing operations.
Description: A general cargo vessel grounded during unberthing operations.

Short_Description: A pilot vessel made contact with a light float.
Description: A pilot vessel was waiting for the next vessel when the tide caught the vessel and set it onto a light float. The vessel touched the float with its quarter. There was no damage to the pilot vessel or the light float.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger ferry davit failed when lifting the fast rescue craft.
Description: During the recovery of the FRC (fast rescue craft) following a drill, with one crewmember onboard, the wire drum free fall break on the davit  failed and started lowering the boat back to sea level. This was from approximately one metre high. The crewmember exited the FRC at sea level via the embarkation door . The brake was tested several times and intermittently failed to hold the FRC in a suspended position. The failure resulted in the FRC being lowered back to the water line.

Short_Description: A recreational fishing boat fouled its propeller and required assistance.
Description: A leisure craft with seven people onboard fouled its propeller on a lobster pot. The lifeboat crew tried to untangle the propeller with no success and so the vessel was towed back to port.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A pilot reported a general cargo vessel's pilot ladder was rigged incorrectly. The ladder was made good before pilots boarded.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel snagged its propeller and was towed by a lifeboat.
Description: A fishing vessel with three crewmembers snagged their propeller with a rope. A lifeboat was tasked and towed the vessel to safety. There was no reported damage or injuries.

Short_Description: A tug towing a barge reported a fouled propeller, but maintained slow speed into port
Description: A tug towing a barge reported a fouled propeller, but maintained slow speed into port using one engine.

Short_Description: A tug's towline parted during mooring operations.
Description: A tug's towline parted during mooring operations.

Short_Description: A dredger had a fire in the engine.
Description: On a dredger an engine room fire alarm was activated. The crew discovered that the fire was caused by the starboard clutch bearing. The crew were unable to declutch the vessel. The crew extinguished the fire using a fire extinguisher and there was only minor damage.
Damage_Description: Shaft alternator bearing damage, electrical power limitations. Propulsion and manoeuvring equipment unaffected.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations
Description: A cargo vessel's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. The pilot ladder was in poor condition.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. The pilot reported both ladders onboard were more than three years old and not load tested, both requiring replacement prior to departure.

Short_Description: A motorboat crewmember severed the top of their finger whilst attempting to fix an anchor chain issue.
Description: A motorboat crewmember severed the top of their little finger whilst attempting to fix an anchor chain issue. The casualty was taken ashore for medical treatment.

Short_Description: A small fishing vessel grounded after getting caught out by tide.
Description: A creel fishing vessel grounded on a rock after getting caught out by the tide. They managed to refloat with the tide and returned to port safely without any assistance. No damage was sustained.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser had a fire on board
Description: A motor cruiser had a fire on board. The three people on board transferred on to another boat nearby and the fire was extinguished. The vessel was towed back to its mooring by a search and rescue vessel.

Short_Description: A passenger vessel had a hull fracture and took on water.
Description: During a passenger vessel's regular passage, part of the metal bilge keel struck an underwater obstruction, and the bilge keel penetrated the hull leading to a minor fracture. It slowly took on water. The skipper did not alert the passengers to the water ingress and instead transferred the eleven passengers to a sister taxi boat operating nearby. There were no injuries. The skipper called for assistance and the local lifeboat service despatched a vessel to assist the skipper to ground the boat on a nearby beach to inspect the hull. The local lifeboat service pumped out the water and then transferred the boat to a slipway. A temporary repair was made and the vessel was moved to a local boatyard for permanent repairs.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting structural integrity of the ship

Short_Description: A fishing vessel crewmember was intending to wash down the deck with a chemical acid, the vessel rolled and the container fell over splashing acid in to their eyes.
Description: A fishing vessel crewmember was intending to clean the deck while the vessel was on passage and poured a chemical acid (Hypochlorite) into a container. The vessel rolled spilling the acid from the container and splashing it in to their eye. The crewmember immediately got into the shower and was then transported to hospital for treatment to flush out the acid.

Short_Description: A dredger crewmember sustained a minor head injury in the engine room whilst fixing a dredge pump.
Description: A dredger crewmember sustained a minor head injury in the engine room whilst fixing a dredge pump. The casualty sustained superficial wounds to their scalp after they stood up and caught their head on a pipe. The casualty only required minor first aid.

Short_Description: A container ship crewmember sustained deep laceration to their finger after catching their finger on angle bar.
Description: A crewmember had a deep laceration on their ring finger when their wedding ring was trapped during a fall.

Short_Description: A cruise ship lost its port anchor due to a link failure.
Description: The incident occurred while the vessel was lying to its port anchor in 35 to 40 knots of wind. One of the links in the anchor chain broke resulting in the loss of the anchor and three cables of chain. The anchor and chain were recovered at a later date.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. It was a combination ladder with a trapdoor arrangement. The ladder did not extend 1.5 metres above platform (it was about 70 cm) and the accommodation ladder was not secured to the hull.

Short_Description: A person fell over board from a yacht.
Description: A crewmember was manoeuvring their vessel when they fell into the water and were hit by a boat. The accident resulted in crush injuries.

Short_Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per current SOLAS regulations. The pilot ladder was not secured at all and the vessel had not heeded previous warnings.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel reported that their alternator was not working and were escorted back to port.
Description: A fishing vessel with two people on board reported that their alternator was not working. They initially requested a tow but managed to get to safety under their own power while being escorted.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel collided with a pole at the harbour entrance whilst towing another sailing vessel.
Description: A sailing vessel was providing another sailing vessel with a tow when they struck a pole at a harbour entrance, resulting in minor damage.  The towed vessel then collided with the towing vessel and the tow rope became wrapped around the propeller. The yachts anchored and awaited assistance form a local lifeboat. No injuries were sustained and there was only minor damage to one vessel.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel collided with a pole at the harbour entrance whilst towing another sailing vessel.
Description: A sailing vessel was providing another sailing vessel with a tow when they struck a pole at a harbour entrance, resulting in minor damage.  The towed vessel then collided with the towing vessel and the tow rope became wrapped around the propeller. The yachts anchored and awaited assistance form a local lifeboat. No injuries were sustained and there was only minor damage to one vessel.
Damage_Description: Described as some damage. Coastguard stated there was no water ingress.

Short_Description: A pilot vessel had a heavy impact whilst coming alongside.
Description: A pilot boat was conducting boarding trials with a ro-ro ferry after fitting new fendering. The pilot boat came alongside with a hard impact which resulted in a dent to the pilot boat's starboard bow section. Initially, the damage appeared to be minor, but on further inspection, the vessel was removed from service as there was impact damage on several welded seams, between two watertight compartments and on each side of the bulkhead. However the hull was not breached and there were no injuries.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel was blown by wind onto a moored barge, causing a puncture to the hull above the waterline.
Description: A general cargo vessel was leaving port and approaching a swing bridge. As the vessel rounded a corner, it became apparent that the bridge would not be open in time. The pilot applied full astern helm to try and reduce the impact but the vessel made contact with a moored barge and one other vessel. The general cargo vessel was holed above the waterline and was returned to the port awaiting a surveyor. The moored barge was also damaged but the extent was not severe.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel was blown by wind onto a moored barge, causing a puncture to the hull above the waterline.
Description: A general cargo vessel was leaving port and approaching a swing bridge. As the vessel rounded a corner, it became apparent that the bridge would not be open in time. The pilot applied full astern helm to try and reduce the impact but the vessel made contact with a moored barge and one other vessel. The general cargo vessel was holed above the waterline and was returned to the port awaiting a surveyor. The moored barge was also damaged but the extent was not severe.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel was blown by wind onto a moored barge, causing a puncture to the hull above the waterline.
Description: A general cargo vessel was leaving port and approaching a swing bridge. As the vessel rounded a corner, it became apparent that the bridge would not be open in time. The pilot applied full astern helm to try and reduce the impact but the vessel made contact with a moored barge and one other vessel. The general cargo vessel was holed above the waterline and was returned to the port awaiting a surveyor. The moored barge was also damaged but the extent was not severe.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting structural integrity of the ship

Short_Description: A container vessel's pilot ladder was non-compliant.
Description: The pilot embarkation point on the deck was not free from obstructions. The deck was cluttered with the pilot ladder and the deck boarding light was rigged facing aft toward the pilot boat. The duty officer on deck was notified.

Short_Description: A chartered fishing vessel had hydraulic failure whilst hoisting the anchor. Assistance was received from an another vessel.
Description: A chartered fishing vessel had hydraulic failure whilst attempting to hoist the anchor.  Another vessel assisted with repairs and the casualty vessel made their own way back to port.

Short_Description: A yacht crewmember slipped backwards whilst attempting to hoist the main sail and injured their lower back.
Description: A crewmember was working on the foredeck helping to hoist the mainsail when they slipped and fell backwards onto a metal protective railing over a deck vent, falling heavily and was in immediate pain. The crewmember was helped back into the cockpit and monitored for ten minutes. There was no reduction of pain, which was severe, it was decided to arrange for an ambulance. The crewmember was taken to hospital and discharged the following day.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel caught a kayak's anchor and dragged it along.
Description: The kayak was anchored up and was fishing at the time. A fishing vessel had been sailing some distance away when they altered their course and sailed very close to the kayak. In doing so the fishing vessel caught the anchor in the vessel's nets. The kayak was then dragged for about a mile until the fishing vessel finally lifted its nets and freed the kayak's anchor. The skipper was aware that the kayak had being dragged but did not make any attempt to stop immediately. Fortunately realizing the danger of the fishing vessel coming that close, the kayaker had unclipped the anchor from the back of the kayak. There was a high risk of the kayak capsizing.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel caught a kayak's anchor and dragged it along.
Description: The kayak was anchored up and was fishing at the time. A fishing vessel had been sailing some distance away when they altered their course and sailed very close to the kayak. In doing so the fishing vessel caught the anchor in the vessel's nets. The kayak was then dragged for about a mile until the fishing vessel finally lifted its nets and freed the kayak's anchor. The skipper was aware that the kayak had being dragged but did not make any attempt to stop immediately. Fortunately realizing the danger of the fishing vessel coming that close, the kayaker had unclipped the anchor from the back of the kayak. There was a high risk of the kayak capsizing.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel had a main engine failure on approach to harbour.
Description: A general cargo vessel had a main engine failure on approach to harbour. The engine was back online quickly and the anchor was heaved up and the vessel continued without further issue.
Damage_Description: Main engine loss for a short period of time.

Short_Description: A motorboat was swamped near a harbour entrance. There were no injuries and the vessel was recovered at low water.
Description: A low freeboard motorboat left a harbour with two crew on board, one of whom was wearing a lifejacket.  The boat was powered by a main outboard but also had an auxiliary outboard mounted on the stern. As the boat passed the eastern breakwater a fishing line from an angler became caught around the outboard propeller. The two crew moved towards the stern to try and untangle the outboard. The weight distribution pushed the stern below the water and the boat started to flood and sank. The two crew were rescued by a passing vessel and taken ashore uninjured. The boat was recovered at low water and refloated without hull damaged but with the engines experiencing issues from submersion in sea water.

Short_Description: A motor vessel grounded.
Description: A motor vessel grounded and was towed by a lifeboat.

Short_Description: A vessel's davit collapsed when load testing.
Description: A boat davit collapsed when carrying out a load test on a workboat davit. No pollution occurred.  There was structural damage to the starboard workboat aft davit arm.

Short_Description: A yacht fouled its propeller and was towed to a marina.
Description: A yacht fouled its propeller on a mooring buoy line. The lifeboat was tasked to assist and they cut the line as they were unable to free the propeller. The vessel was then towed to a marina to enable the line to be cleared.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel crewmember had neck and back injuries after a fall from height while repairing machinery at sea and was airlifted to hospital.
Description: On the way to fishing grounds, machinery was being fixed at a height of 1.5 metres by a crew member. On completion of the maintenance the crewmember stood and lost their balance falling on the back of their head and neck against the deck below. They lost consciousness for a significant amount of time and were airlifted to hospital.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. The rigging of the pilot ladder was not checked, or the embarkation and/or disembarkation of the pilot was not supervised by a watch keeping deck officer. - A tripping line was fitted to the bottom of the ladder, or was rigged not in accordance with IMO Resolution A.1045(27) 2.1.5.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser had engine failure and drifted close to shore.
Description: A motor cruiser had engine failure close to shore. The vessel had eleven people on board. A lifeboat was tasked to the vessel where they removed nine of the passengers from the vessel and two stayed on board. The vessel was towed back to safety.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS.

Short_Description: A supply vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A supply vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. The stanchions only 50cm high.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged in compliance with SOLAS guidance.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged in compliance with SOLAS guidance. The pilot ladder was suspended from the main deck all the way down the ship's side adjacent to a shell door. The pilot needed to do a big step across in order to get access to the shell door opening without any platform to step on. Distance from the bottom of the shell door to the water level was 3.95m as per the pilot card and 3.3m as per the calculation provided on board.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged in compliance with SOLAS guidance.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged in compliance with SOLAS guidance.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel required assistance due to engine difficulties.
Description: A fishing vessel required assistance due to engine difficulties. The fishing vessel was drifting towards a breakwater. The fishing vessel was taken back alongside safely by a search and rescue (SAR) vessel.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel experienced a fire.
Description: A lifeboat was on passage back to its station when the flame detector and smoke alarm automatically activated. An investigation of the engine room was carried out and smoke and small flames were seen on the starboard engine turbo. The starboard engine was shut down and the flames went out, no fire extinguishers were used. The vessel returned to the departure port using just the port engine. Upon investigation it appeared that the turbo heat shield and exhaust lagging were incorrectly fitted resulting in the lagging catching fire.

Short_Description: A chemical tanker crewmember threw a weighted heaving line.
Description: A chemical tanker crewmember threw a weighted heaving line.

Short_Description: A crew transfer vessel was tied off to a wind turbine when it made contact, causing the port tank to flood.
Description: A crew transfer vessel was tied off to a wind turbine with the engines shut down. The master, who was on the bridge looking at the chart table, noticed the vessel drifting toward the turbine and started the engines. In the time it took to start the engines, contact was made with the wind turbine and the vessel's port side. An external inspection of the hull on the port side was carried out, from deck level, and showed no apparent damage. The vessel remained tied off with engines in low astern for a little over two hours. Upon making their return to base-port the vessel began listing to port and the high and low level alarms in the port tank sounded. The master went to inspect the port tank space and on opening the hatch found the tank to be completely filled to the top. The emergency bilge pump was rigged to supplement the pumps already in use.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship
Damage_Description: Flooded Port Tank Space Full extent of damage is unknown, pending an assessment

Short_Description: A vessel's pilot ladder was not compliant with SOLAS.
Description: A pilot reported that the pilot ladder on a vessel was not compliant with SOLAS. The steps were not horizontal and were covered in oil. The vessel turned away from port and the crew rigged a new ladder.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS.
Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS.

Short_Description: A passenger ship crewmember injured their back whilst lowering a life raft from a cradle.
Description: The crewmember was involved in the removal of a Means of Recovery (MOR) life raft, from its cradle. The life raft was lowered onto a Fast Rescue Boat (FRB) and was then to be lowered to deck level. As weight was induced, the crewmember, who was stood upright with arms out, experienced pain in their lower back. They were incapacitated for less than 72 hours

Short_Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per current SOLAS regulations.
Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per current SOLAS regulations. On disembarkation, the pilot ladder was secured using a deck tongue bar arrangement.

Short_Description: A speedboat experienced engine failure.
Description: A vessel experienced machinery failure and became stuck in mud. All persons were taken ashore and the vessel was towed to a marina.

Short_Description: A SAR vessel grounded during a rescue operation.
Description: A search and rescue (SAR) vessel grounded whilst looking for a casualty along a beach. There was no damage to the vessel and it continued on the rescue operation without further incident.

Short_Description: A service vessel crewmember slipped down a set of stairs and sustained a head injury.
Description: A service vessel crewmember was staying onboard overnight and was woken by an alarm sounding in the engine room. The crewmember went to investigate the alarm which involved crossing an open wet deck to access the stairs to the engine room. The crewmember was descending the stairs with their back to the stairs and both hands on the handrail when they slipped and hit their head on the handrail resulting in concussion and a cut to the forehead. The crewmember was taken to hospital to have the wound glued together and the crewmember was signed off work to recover.

Short_Description: A chemical tanker's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A chemical tanker's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. The ladder was secured with choke shackles over the side ropes, jammed against the wedges and the step.

Short_Description: A single handed yacht crewmember had a head injury after being hit by the boom. They were taken ashore for treatment.
Description: A single handed yacht crewmember had a head injury after being struck by the boom while on passage. They sailed into a nearby harbour and anchored but struggled to stop the bleeding so called for assistance. The local lifeboat attended and recovered the skipper ashore, passing them into the  care of the ambulance crew who then took the casualty to the minor injuries unit at the local hospital.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger ferry had water ingress.
Description: A vessel was on a routine passage when the local steering gear bilge alarm sounded. The crew investigated and found around 230 litres of water in the steering gear bilge, with salt water emitting from the skeg breather pipe. The vessel continued on passage and successfully berthed, following which it was placed out of service. The suspected cause of the ingress was a crack in a weld on the skeg, but the vessel was due to go into drydock to investigate further.

Short_Description: A crew member on board a passenger vessel fell through a hatch and sustained a dislocated shoulder.
Description: A crew member on board a passenger vessel fell through a hatch and sustained a dislocated shoulder.

Short_Description: A ro-pax vessel had a non-operational bow thruster.
Description: A ro-pax vessel had a non-operational bow thruster mid-passage. The vessel reported the failure and the authorities monitored the vessel.

Short_Description: A cruise ship crewmember trapped their finger between a door and a frame.
Description: A crewmember sustained a partial amputation of their right index finger when transiting a fire sliding door during a drill. They opened the door by the handle and their finger was trapped between the door and its frame once the door was in fully open position.

Short_Description: A motorboat ran aground and reported minor water ingress from the rudder.
Description: A motorboat lost steering and ran aground resulting in minor water ingress through the rudder. The vessel was a fin keel boat and waited for the incoming tide before re-floating. No assistance was required.

Short_Description: A sailing yacht lost its rudder and had water ingress.
Description: A sailing yacht lost its rudder and had water ingress. The vessel was towed back to port by a lifeboat to make repairs.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship
Damage_Description: Lost rudder. Other damage is unknown

Short_Description: A roro vessel's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS.
Description: A roro vessel's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel grounded after passing through a harbour entrance.
Description: A general cargo vessel grounded on the side of a channel just after passing through the harbour entrance. The pilot and master managed to manoeuvre vessel off the bank and continued to the berth. The vessel was undamaged.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel's gear got caught on the seabed.
Description: A fishing vessel's fishing gear got caught on the bottom of the seabed but the crew managed to retrieve all the gear. The vessel did not require any assistance.

Short_Description: A passenger vessel lost power to their engines and had to be towed back to safety.
Description: A passenger vessel with three people on board had electrical problems and lost both engines. The vessel was towed back the to harbour for repair.

Short_Description: A RIB's steering failed and threw the helm and two passengers into the water. The people were recovered and the vessel was towed back to safety.
Description: A RIB (rigid inflatable boat) was returning to its home port when it suddenly slowed as the steering failed resulting in three people being thrown into the water, and three remaining in the rib. No lifejackets were being worn. A kill cord was in use and the RIB stopped as the helm was thrown overboard. All those thrown into the water were recovered to the RIB and another vessel assisted the RIB back to port. Later examination found the morse steering cable had snapped, with no obvious signs of wear or corrosion. The RIB was regularly serviced. The owner intended to fit hydraulic steering and always wear lifejackets in future.
Damage_Description: Steering cable broke which threw 3 of those on board into the water. Boat had been maintained. Steering morse cable suddenly failed, no obvious sign of corrosion.

Short_Description: A tanker's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: A tanker's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. There were broken strands on the side ropes throughout the length of the ladder. There was no officer at pilot boarding station.

Short_Description: A chemical tanker's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A chemical tanker's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. The ladder was secured using shackles below a step. The ladder shifted as the pilot stepped on it.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had a small fire on an electrical switchboard.
Description: A fishing vessel had a switchboard electrical fire 2.5 nautical miles from shore. The crew extinguished the fire at first but it reignited before being extinguished for a second time. There was minimal damage to the vessel and no injuries to the three crew on board. The vessel was escorted back to port by a search and rescue vessel and met by the fire service to make sure the fire was out.

Short_Description: A cruise ship crewmember set off the deep fat fryer fire protection mist by accident.
Description: A cruise ship was at anchorage carrying out an annual inspection on various systems. During the inspection, the fixed fire fighting system for the deep fat fryer was accidentally activated by a crewmember. The vessel did not have any spare nitrogen bottles on board so the system was out of action until a new bottle was received on board. There were no injuries, damage or pollution.

Short_Description: A personal watercraft user sustained lacerations to their foot and was taken to hospital by their family.
Description: A personal watercraft user sustained severe lacerations to their right foot. This occurred as they were trying to tow somebody behind the jet ski and the tow rope became caught on their foot. The wound was deep. The casualty was given first aid ashore, but an ambulance was not available so the casualty was taken to hospital by their family with the first responders escorting them.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.

Short_Description: An offshore supply vessel's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS.
Description: An offshore supply vessel's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had a close quarters situation with a cargo vessel.
Description: A fishing vessel was towing their gear and displaying symbols for fishing although the visibility was poor. The crew noticed a cargo vessel approaching from the vessel's stern but did not call the cargo vessel. The cargo vessel altered course to port and passed within one-thousand meters when it saw the fishing vessel. The fishing vessel did not transmit on AIS (Automatic Identification System) until after the close quarters situation.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had a close quarters situation with a cargo vessel.
Description: A fishing vessel was towing their gear and displaying symbols for fishing although the visibility was poor. The crew noticed a cargo vessel approaching from the vessel's stern but did not call the cargo vessel. The cargo vessel altered course to port and passed within one-thousand meters when it saw the fishing vessel. The fishing vessel did not transmit on AIS (Automatic Identification System) until after the close quarters situation.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had engine failure and was towed by a lifeboat.
Description: A fishing vessel had gearbox failure and was towed by a lifeboat to port.

Short_Description: A capsized sit-on kayak trapped a paddler on a white water section of a river resulting in a fatality.
Description: A two person sit on kayak capsized on a white water section of the river with one paddler on board. The casualty became trapped under the kayak, the paddle and got their legs tangled in the webbing and leg leash leaving their head under the water. The victim was declared deceased by the doctor on the scene. They were wearing a personal flotation device at the time.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser had a damaged rudder and requested assistance.
Description: A motor cruiser reported that it had lost or damaged it's rudder, the two crew onboard had not fitted a temporary rudder but they were able to manoeuvre using the bow thrusters. The crew requested assistance as the vessel was not making much headway, a search and rescue (SAR) vessel deployed and towed the vessel to a mooring.

Short_Description: A replenishment tanker crewmember sustained multiple injuries whilst on a training drill.
Description: A replenishment tanker crew were carrying out coming alongside drills on a fast rescue craft (FRC), several successful approaches had been made. On the next approach, the FRC missed picking up the painter and it manoeuvred away from the tanker’s side. As it did so, the FRC rode across a wave and a crewmember who was in the bow walking back to their seat lost their footing and fell. As they fell they hit their head, fell unconscious and sustained an injury to both shoulders and one ankle. First aid was administered onboard, once the FRC was recovered, the crewmember was evacuated by helicopter and taken to hospital for further assessment and treatment.

Short_Description: A replenishment tanker reported a fire due to an exhaust fan overheating.
Description: A replenishment tanker was alongside when a crewmember entered the cargo pump motor room to start an exhaust fan. The contactor for the overload protection circuit overheated and a small electrical fire started. The crewmember extinguished the fire with a CO2 extinguisher. The incident was reported and the crew went to their muster stations. Primary and secondary electrical isolations were confirmed complete and crew stood down from emergency stations. There was evidence of heat damage to wiring and some of the wiring terminals appeared to be loose, no other damage was reported. No injuries to crew were reported.
Damage_Description: Localised heat damage to contactor and terminal wiring.  No smoke and or heat damage to any other assets.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel grounded whilst attempting to berth.
Description: A cargo vessel grounded whilst attempting to berth. The vessel's engines were running astern and proceeding at 1.7knots. During the manoeuvre, the master noticed a very slight list to port and the speed reduced, eventually to 0.0knots. The pilot aboard the vessel made contact with the pilot cutter and requested assistance in re-floating. The cutter pushed the cargo vessel clear of the obstruction. The vessel amended its plans to berth and shortly after being clear of the obstruction, berthed successfully.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had a fouled propeller and was towed back to port.
Description: A fishing vessel had a fouled propeller engine and was initially towed back to port by a nearby fishing vessel and then by a lifeboat .

Short_Description: A sea safari rib passenger had back pain after vessel hit wave.
Description: A sea safari trip passenger had a back injury after the vessel slammed into a wave. The skipper decide to return to port where they were met by a doctor who determined that the passenger didn't suffer any injures and was given paracetamol.

Short_Description: A lifeboat made contact with the harbour wall while departing port resulting in bow damage.
Description: The lifeboat was proceeding from port at night in rough weather when it made contact with the harbour wall resulting in damage to the port bow above the waterline. The lifeboat was taken off service. The position of the lifeboat relative to the harbour wall was confused due to harbour lights, car lights and other torches being used along the harbour wall due to a missing persons search that was being conducted in the area.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser had engine failure and was being pushed onto rocks.
Description: A motor cruiser had engine failure and was being pushed onto rocks. The local lifeboat service were tasked to tow the vessel.

Short_Description: A sailing yacht grounded on a rock ledge.
Description: A sailing yacht with five crew onboard grounded on a rock ledge. The crew lowered the sails and made to secure the yacht as the yacht was unable to be towed off due to the falling tide. All crew onboard were wearing lifejackets, two crew entered the water and were recovered by a passing boat. The remaining crew were recovered by a search and rescue (SAR) vessel and taken ashore. No injuries to crew were reported, the damage to the yacht was unknown. The crew planned to recover the vessel on the flood tide.

Short_Description: A person fell overboard from a dinghy whilst attempting to moor it to a buoy.
Description: A person fell overboard from their dinghy whilst attempting to moor it to a buoy . They were wearing a life jacket. The casualty was picked up by a safety boat, the boat was recovered by a lifeboat and taken to its mooring. No injuries were sustained.

Short_Description: A suction dredger's stern line parted at the drum end.
Description: A suction dredger's stern line parted and caused a snap back. No crew members were injured but they were made aware of the hazard and made aware to stand clear of snap back zones.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel experienced engine failure.
Description: A general cargo vessel experienced engine failure. Repairs were conducted and the vessel resumed passage.

Short_Description: A chemical tanker lost power and was towed out of the channel. The vessel rectified the issue and went underway.
Description: A cargo vessel lost power during pilotage and was assisted by two tugs until the power was restored.

Short_Description: A mooring vessel crewmember crushed their finger between a mooring line and a bollard.
Description: Whilst mooring a vessel alongside the crewmember of a mooring vessel had the 3rd finger on their right hand crushed between the rope and the bollard.

Short_Description: A utility vessel ran aground at the entrance to harbour.
Description: When departing the harbour whilst towing a salmon feed barge the utility vessel ran aground after misjudging the tide. The barge it was towing drifted into the back of the vessel but there was no damage to the vessel or the barge. The vessel used the thrusters to push its self off the seabed and continued without further incident.

Short_Description: A RIB started taking on water and was towed by a search and rescue vessel.
Description: An anchored RIB (rigid inflatable boat) with nine people and two dogs onboard had a fouled propeller and was taking on water. Apart from three crew, everyone else managed to get ashore on a paddleboard. A search and rescue vessel was deployed and towed the vessel to a harbour.

Short_Description: A sailing yacht required assistance after it became stuck on an underwater obstruction.
Description: A sailing yacht was sailing when it became stuck on an underwater obstruction. The yacht was still afloat but unable to move and the lone skipper was unable to see what they were stuck on. The skipper lowered the sails and requested assistance as the yacht was broadside to the wind. A search and rescue (SAR) vessel assisted the yacht off the obstruction and then towed it to a marina. There were no reported injuries to the skipper.

Short_Description: A recreational angling vessel reported an engine failure and was towed back to shore.
Description: A recreational angling vessel with four crew onboard reported an engine failure. The four crew were wearing lifejackets and had deployed an anchor. A passing vessel towed the stricken vessel back to shore, no damage reported and no injuries to crew.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. A tripping line was fitted to the bottom of the ladder.

Short_Description: A pilot boat made contact with bitts on the pontoon after making fast to pontoon resulting in two dents to the hull.
Description: After the vessel had completed sea trials it was making fast to a pontoon when it impacted the bitts on the ponton causing damage to the port side with two dents to the hull.

Short_Description: A hopper dredger had a small engine fire after an oil leak.
Description: A hopper dredger had a small engine fire after the starboard engine gearbox blew out spraying the engine room in oil. The fire was extinguished using a foam trolley extinguisher. The vessel anchored overnight and arranged to head to port for repair. No persons were injured.

Short_Description: A tug had an engine failure during sea trials.
Description: A tug had a main propulsion failure to its starboard main engine during sea trials. The tug returned to port on the port engine and was taken out of service to investigate and effect repairs.  The engine had just been repaired when it had a piston liner failure and expulsion from the engine.
Damage_Description: Damage to starboard engine, piston liner failure and expulsion from engine. Major repairs required.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel made contact with a breakwater.
Description: A general cargo vessel made contact with a port breakwater on departure. There was only minor damage to the vessel, scraping and a dent to the starboard shoulder.
Damage_Description: Light scraping and a small dent on starboard shoulder.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel crewmember was injured whilst on service.
Description: A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was carrying out a search for a missing person, crew members were located on the foredeck. A potential target was located at the base of the cliff, the helm manoeuvred closer to the shoreline for a better look using searchlights. As the vessel was being manoeuvred, a crewmember on the foredeck with a searchlight was thrown against the Sampson post resulting in heavy bruising to their right hip, ribs and shoulder.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger vessel had a fire as a result of a fire blanket falling behind a compressor unit.
Description: A ro-ro passenger ship was alongside. Two shore contractors were replacing steel pipework near the deckhead in the compressor room. Shortly after the contractors left the area for a break, the ship's company were alerted by fixed smoke detectors. The fire party discharged a nearby fire extinguisher on a smouldering fire blanket which had fallen behind the compressor unit. The blanket had originally been placed on top of the compressor to capture sparks during welding. There was no major damage or injuries.

Short_Description: A person went overboard from a privately owned yacht.
Description: A crewmember fell overboard from vessel, they were recovered and had the effects of cold.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged to SOLAS regulations. A tripping line was fitted just above the bottom step. The officer present was not aware of the wheelhouse poster indicating that this was not permitted. There was no overside lighting and the  bridge wing floodlight did not illuminate the ladder.

Short_Description: A crew transfer vessel crewmember injured their back lifting a bag.
Description: A crew transfer vessel windfarm technician injured their back lifting a personal bag awkwardly. The crewmember was met by an ambulance ashore.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per current SOLAS regulations.
Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged per current SOLAS regulations.  After embarking the vessel the ladder was found to be secured with a steel pin while the side ropes were lying on deck.

Short_Description: A general cargo ship made contact with a concrete quayside and sustained material damage.
Description: A general cargo ship made contact with a concrete quayside and sustained material damage.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship
Damage_Description: Deep scoring, large indentation of bow.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel's engine failed and the vessel was towed back to harbour.
Description: A fishing vessel's engine failed and a tow was arranged back to harbour by a lifeboat. The casualty vessel was not in immediate danger and there were no injuries or damage.

Short_Description: A cruise ship crewmember injured their shoulder after pulling a chain.
Description: A cruise ship crewmember was on duty on deck in the evaporator room. At this time they were operating a chain winch that was connected between the chain block hooking point and the sea chest cover assisting other crew members in replacing the sea chest cover. As they did so they started to feel a mild pain in their right shoulder, while holding one of the chain block chains which was a little tight. While pulling the chain they used an excessive amount of force causing a strain to their right shoulder.

Short_Description: An angling  was vessel towed after making contact with rocks.
Description: Three people left port in an angling vessel after being advised not to due to the condition of the vessel. They proceeded and found themselves to be in difficulty and on the rocks where a lifeboat had to tow them back to port.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser had a fire in the engine room.
Description: A motor cruiser had a fire in the engine room.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. The pilot ladder was secured using a deck tongue.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger ferry had issues with its starboard engine but continued to port using its port engine.
Description: After leaving the berth, a ro-ro passenger ferry's shaft generator breaker tripped. This caused a knock-on effect that resulted in the vessel's starboard engine producing a loud mechanical noise. The engineering team activated the emergency shut down and the vessel proceeded using the port main engine only.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel had a loss of directional control after the helm malfunctioned and the vessel made contact with a bank.
Description: The vessel had swung to starboard, when the vessel's helm malfunctioned. It turned hard to port causing the vessel to swing to port towards a bank. All attempts made to turn the helm to starboard were not successful, the engine was stopped immediately and engaged in full astern power. The vessel's port bow landed ashore on a bank. The crew then attempted the restart the steering equipment and following this, the helm appeared to respond normally. The crew then engaged  the engine astern and the bow thruster to attempt to manoeuvre the vessel off the bank, this did not work and a tug was  requested in order to tow the vessel to safety.

Short_Description: A container vessel had a small fire in the scavenge space and as a result had total engine failure.
Description: The vessel had a small contained fire in the scavenge exhaust and was safely anchored. The repairs were rectified and the vessel was allowed to resume its passage to its port of destination.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship

Short_Description: A passenger ro-ro vessel grounded on its final approach to the berth.
Description: A vessel was making its final approach to the berth when the aft starboard skeg make contact with an underwater object on starboard side of the channel. Lack of propulsion available and non-responsive propulsion lead to the vessel entering shallow water. There was a slight scrape to the skeg and a small area of damage to the transverse frame above the skeg.

Short_Description: A cruise ship lost an anchor during severe weather.
Description: A cruise ship parted its anchor cable during heavy weather and started to drift. They recovered the remaining chain and then dropped the other anchor in a different position.

Short_Description: A vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A  vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged per SOLAS regulations. The deficiency was noted on disembarkation, the upper ropes of the ladder were spread either side of the stanchions to secure to deck, which are much wider than the ladder. This caused the ropes to form a Y shape above the ladder as well as fray and the fixing piece to part from the top step.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser grounded and refloated on the high tide.
Description: A motor cruiser grounded after the skipper became distracted. The vessel was later refloated on the high tide.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel went aground and the crew were recovered from the vessel.
Description: A sailing vessel went aground and the two crew were recovered from the vessel back to port.

Short_Description: A tug passed another vessel at speed causing water to enter the yacht.
Description: A yacht was passed by a harbour tug at speed, causing a large wash, some of which entered the yacht through a hatch. There was no reported damage or injuries.

Short_Description: A sailing catamaran went aground.
Description: A sailing catamaran grounded after being caught in bad weather. The vessel began to fill up with rain and grounded on the beach. The crewmember on board dropped the anchor to prevent the vessel from moving and waded to shore, with the plan to return to the vessel at high tide.

Short_Description: A motor vessel used for fishing sunk following a fire. No one was injured.
Description: A small motor vessel with one crewmember was proceeding to sea when the engine suddenly stopped. The skipper went to drop the anchor in which time a fire started near the engine. A lifeboat was launched and the casualty was evacuated by a passing private vessel. The casualty vessel sank and there were no injuries.
Pollution_Result: Vessel sunk with 4 or 5 gallons of fuel onboard.

Short_Description: A hire cruiser passenger fell overboard and was recovered with no serious injuries.
Description: A person that had hired an inland waterway cruiser fell overboard while the vessel was moored alongside. After the alarm was raised, the emergency services assisted with recovery of the casualty who was taken into the care of the ambulance service. The person had injuries to a leg and an arm and was later discharged from hospital.

Short_Description: A cruise ship crewmember was electrocuted after a live wire was touching a metal beam.
Description: A cruise ship crewmember was electrocuted by a loose wire.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. The ladder was in a poor condition with lower steps loose and twisting.

Short_Description: A cruise ship passenger was walking when they tripped on their right foot and fell forwards resulting in a fractured right upper arm.
Description: A passenger was walking, when they tripped on them right foot and fell forwards. The deck in the casino was covered with carpet, there were no obstructions and the area was well illuminated. They could not explain how or why they tripped and blamed themself for not paying attention when walking. They stated that as they were falling forward they landed with their right upper arm and shoulder on the corner of the casino machine. The passenger was checked over at the medical centre where it was confirmed that they had fractured their right upper arm.

Short_Description: A RIB had engine failure and was towed to safety.
Description: A RIB (rigid inflatable boat) had engine failure and was towed to safety.

Short_Description: A hire cruiser ran aground and waited overnight to refloat and to be towed.
Description: A hire cruiser with three crew on board grounded in a river on the mud. They had to wait overnight until they could be assisted in refloating on a higher tide and were towed to port. No reported damage to the vessel.

Short_Description: A passenger ferry had a child fall from the gangway. The child landed in their fenders and was unhurt.
Description: A small child went slightly ahead of their parent on the gangway of a ferry. The crew at the gangway was helping an elderly passenger onto the ship. The child leant backwards in the area without a handrail, but with a safety rope. they were too short for the rope and fell around one and a half metres. The child landed on their feet on the fenders and was recovered unhurt.

Short_Description: A workboat became fouled on a wind float structure and was freed by another vessel.
Description: A workboat, which was moored to a windfarm structure, became unknowingly fouled on the structure as the tide ebbed and the crew were unable to free the vessel. They were eventually freed with the assistance of another workboat. No damage was found to either the structure or the workboat.

Short_Description: A tug crewmember entered hold to dislodge a jammed cargo handling grab sustaining a hand injury in the process.
Description: A crew member was requested by shoreside staff to enter hold and dislodge a jammed cargo handling grab. When the grab opened the crewmember sustained serious injuries to their arm.

Short_Description: A sailing yacht had an electrical fire in the engine room.
Description: A sailing yacht had an engine failure after an electrical fire caused the engine to cut out. The fire was extinguished and the vessel towed back to port.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel grounded during the approach to its berth.
Description: During an operational turn off the berth, the vessel entered a shallow depth of water. The vessel may have lightly grounded.

Short_Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel made contact with a pump house.
Description: A vessel made  contact with a pump house with its port shoulder. The crew reported that the wind caused the vessel to veer uncontrollably.

Short_Description: A passenger vessel crewmember slipped down a ladder and fractured their ankle.
Description: A passenger vessel crewmember lost their grip whilst descending a ladder and fractured their ankle.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. A ladder was secured with twelve millimetre polypropylene rope looped around a step. The deck crew were told to change this to a rope of the same diameter as the side ropes. A crewmember attempted to secure the ladder with a poor condition, frayed piece of rope. Shortly after this the ladder was finally secured with new rope of the correct diameter.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per current SOLAS regulations.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per current SOLAS regulations. The ladder was secured by a deck tongue holding a step. There were no independent side rope lashings to take the weight of the ladder. A retrieval line led forward but was attached below the lower spreader.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel had a fire and subsequently foundered.
Description: The sailing vessel had recently had a new turbocharger fitted which subsequently caused a fire and as a result the vessel foundered. One crewmember that was onboard was taken off by another vessel and a lifeboat stood by the vessel until it foundered.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel discovered a small hole in the sponson during an operation.
Description: A SAR (search and rescue) vessel was launched after which the crew noticed that the port sponson was sagging. After an initial investigation it was observed that there was a small hole in the sponson. At the time the vessel was deemed seaworthy and continued with its rescue operation as it was deployed with another SAR vessel. Once back at base, on further investigation, three black half circular marks could be seen on the sponson in the vicinity of the hole. This marking seemed consistent with the location of the trailer wheel.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel sustained damage after contact with a pier.
Description: A search and rescue vessel's sponson collided with a pier resulting in several punctures during an operation. The vessel was able to complete the rescue mission and return to station and was taken out of service. There were no injuries to persons.

Short_Description: A pilot on board a chemical tanker slipped on the bridge steps whilst disembarking and injured their shoulder.
Description: A pilot on board a chemical tanker slipped on the bridge steps whilst going down to the deck to depart the ship. The pilot had an injury to their shoulder and was taken to hospital once ashore.

Short_Description: A sailing dingy crewmember was struck on the head with a boom.
Description: One instructor and three passengers were out in a sailing dinghy when the passenger steering accidentally gybed the boom which swung around and the hit the instructor on the head. Someone else from the water sports centre came to meet the sailing dingy in a RIB and towed the vessel back. The casualty went to the hospital after and spent the next five days off work as a result of the head injury.

Short_Description: A cruise ship passenger tripped and fell while playing table tennis, resulting in a broken wrist.
Description: A cruise ship guest tripped over their own foot and fell while playing table tennis. The passenger put their hand out in front of them to break their fall and broke their wrist.

Short_Description: A crew transfer vessel grounded inbound into port.
Description: A crew transfer vessel was proceeding back into port. It entered the channel alongside two ferries that were inbound and stayed over to the starboard side to leave them room. The vessel grounded because the crew were unaware of a bank that had shifted into the channel. No damage to vessel or injuries to crew were sustained.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel crewmember got burned due to a hydraulic hose failure on a davit.
Description: A search and rescue vessel launched on routine training and the crew prepared to launch the daughter boat from above the wheelhouse using a crane. They noticed that the crane was not operating correctly.  Once the boat was clear, the mechanic entered the main engine room and attempted to move the crane using manual controls. One of the hydraulic hoses parted, spraying them with hot oil on the side of the face, arm and chest. This led to some scalding and a small abrasion on their chest. They went to hospital and the wound was cleaned and dressed.
Damage_Description: The crane/davit hydraulic hose parted when the engineer tried to move the crane by using manual controls.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel crewmember lost tip of their finger and was airlifted to hospital.
Description: A fishing vessel crewmember lost the tip of their finger after crushing it against a rope and a winch. The crewmember was airlifted to hospital.

Short_Description: A chemical tanker's pilot ladder was not rigged in compliance with SOLAS guidance.
Description: A chemical tanker's pilot ladder was not rigged in compliance with SOLAS guidance. The weight of the ladder was on a spreader against railings and the line used to secure the ladder was too small and of a dissimilar material.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel grounded whilst launching and damaged both propellers
Description: A search and rescue vessel grounded whilst launching from a drive off carriage to a rescue. Immediately after the launch, both outboard engines struck the seabed. The helm maintained steerage and managed to  manoeuvre the vessel back to harbour and then self recovered onto the carriage. Upon inspection, both propellers were damaged and had to be replaced. No persons were injured.
Damage_Description: Both propellers had to be replaced.

Short_Description: A vessel's crewmember injured their shoulder during aircraft refuelling operations.
Description: A crewmember was in the process of securing a fuel hose to a helicopter on the flight deck. As they went to make the connection, the hose became pressurised. The hose kicked and jarred the crewmember's shoulder as they restrained it. The crewmember dislocated their shoulder as a result.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had engine failure and briefly grounded.
Description: A fishing vessel had engine failure resulting in the vessel briefly grounding. The vessel re-floated and returned to its berth before heading back out to sea later. There was no reported damage.

Short_Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel parted a stern morning line.
Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel parted a stern morning line.

Short_Description: A crew member broke a finger and sustained other injuries after becoming trapped in an MES (Mass Evacuation System) chute during a training exercise.
Description: A crewmember was taking part in a training exercise using a mass evacuation system (MES). As they descended the chute their leg got trapped within the inner sock of the MES chute. As a result they were unable to descend the chute to the mother raft. Other crew tried to assist them but the crewmember was stuck. The rescue system was deployed which involved the trapped crewmember donning a safety harness so they could be lifted up. Eventually the injured crewmember was lowered down the chute and they were taken to hospital. The crewmember sustained soft tissue injures as well as a spiral fracture of their right finger during their entrapment. The reason for the crewmember becoming trapped could not be determined for certain but it was believed to be because the crewmember did not put their legs together on entering the chute.

Short_Description: An angling vessel crewmember dislocated their shoulder after hitting a wave awkwardly.
Description: An angling vessel crewmember was injured when the vessel hit a wave causing the crewmember to fall to the deck and dislocate their shoulder.

Short_Description: A yacht ran aground and started taking on water.
Description: A yacht ran aground and started taking on water. It was recovered to a mooring by a lifeboat.

Short_Description: A container vessel's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS.
Description: A container vessel's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS.  On arriving at the vessel, the pilot cutter's crew observed that the pilot ladder was in poor condition with the second from the bottom rubber step broken from the side rope and two other wooden steps split.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had engine failure and was towed back to port.
Description: A fishing vessel had engine failure and was towed back to port by a search and rescue vessel.

Short_Description: A sailing yacht's propeller fell off.
Description: A sailing yacht's propeller dropped off and it was towed back to port by a search and rescue vessel.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel had an engine fire and was towed by a harbour patrol vessel.
Description: A sailing vessel had an engine fire outside of a harbour area but drifted in due to the tide. A harbour patrol vessel picked up the vessel and was towed to floating pontoons. A fire officer boarded the vessel and confirmed it was safe. The vessel sustained smoke damage with some superficial melting of fiberglass in the engine casing.

Short_Description: A container ship's crew sent a heaving line ashore using a weighted monkey's fist.
Description: A container ship's crew sent a heaving line ashore using a weighted monkey's fist.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel crewmember sustained injuries to their hand after getting caught it in a chain.
Description: A fishing vessel with five people on board was preparing to shoot gear when the chain back strap of the starboard door got caught between the hull of the vessel and the trawl door. The door was lowered to free the chain from the hull and as the door was being heaved back up a crewmember's hand got caught on the chain. The crewmember sustained a fractured left hand and the vessel returned to port so that the casualty could be taken to hospital.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel skipper was evacuated after experiencing a severe finger injury.
Description: A fishing vessel skipper was evacuated after experiencing a severely crushed finger.  They were evacuated by local lifeboat to shore where they were met by an ambulance and taken to hospital.  Their finger was crushed in a winch.

Short_Description: A motor Cruiser lost steering and was assisted to safety.
Description: A twin engine recreational motor cruiser with ten people on board lost steering and the owner believed a belt had come off. A lifeboat located the casualty vessel and assisted them to safety.
Damage_Description: Lost steering and owner believed belt may have come off.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel crewmember fell from height onto the quayside experiencing life changing leg injuries.
Description: A general cargo vessel crewmember fell from height onto the quayside experiencing leg injuries.

Short_Description: A racing motor boat had a near miss with divers and a dive vessel.
Description: A racing motorboat passed close to a dive vessel.

Short_Description: A racing motor boat had a near miss with divers and a dive vessel.
Description: A racing motorboat passed close to a dive vessel.

Short_Description: A tug had engine failure possibly due to a fuel issue and lost its anchor.
Description: A tug had engine failure possibly due to a fuel issue and lost its anchor.

Short_Description: A jet-RIB's jets were blocked by debris, causing it to lose propulsion and ground
Description: A search and rescue operation was underway. Whilst crew of the search and rescue craft were attending to the casualty, the jets ingested a significant about of flotsam and jetsam and the rescue craft was unable to reverse power off the foreshore. As a result, the craft grounded as the tide fell away. The craft was afloat again on the flood tide and the debris was cleared from the jets by hand.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel had propulsion issues and made contact with a moored charter fishing vessel.
Description: A cargo vessel was under pilotage, transiting the main river channel to its berth when it had issues with its propulsion system. This was noticed as the vessel was rounding a corner with another vessel moored at a jetty on the starboard side. The engine/gearbox de-clutched and alarm was sounded in the wheelhouse. There was a temporary lack of propulsion meaning the helm orders to check the swing were not having any effect. As the cargo vessel made contact with the moored vessel the propulsion system engaged and steerage was regained. The moored vessel had damage to the hull above the waterline, fibreglass wood gunwale and stainless steel railings. There was also damage sustained to navigational equipment in the wheelhouse. There was no pollution.
Damage_Description: Damage to hull above the waterline.  Gunwhale and stainless steel railings-squashed  Damage to navigational equipment

Short_Description: A cargo vessel had propulsion issues and made contact with a moored charter fishing vessel.
Description: A cargo vessel was under pilotage, transiting the main river channel to its berth when it had issues with its propulsion system. This was noticed as the vessel was rounding a corner with another vessel moored at a jetty on the starboard side. The engine/gearbox de-clutched and alarm was sounded in the wheelhouse. There was a temporary lack of propulsion meaning the helm orders to check the swing were not having any effect. As the cargo vessel made contact with the moored vessel the propulsion system engaged and steerage was regained. The moored vessel had damage to the hull above the waterline, fibreglass wood gunwale and stainless steel railings. There was also damage sustained to navigational equipment in the wheelhouse. There was no pollution.

Short_Description: A yacht crewmember was climbing a ladder and fell back into their boat.
Description: A crewmember on board a yacht fell from a ladder whilst climbing out and fell back into the vessel. They sustained suspected chest injuries.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel grounded and was damaged and needed a tow once it refloated.
Description: A yacht was sailing on a broad reach to return to an anchorage in the lee of an island.  The skipper became distracted from navigation while the sails were lowered and the vessel grounded on a submerged, charted, rock.  The yacht heeled over as the tide ebbed. A lifeboat responded and evacuated the three crew before returning them to the yacht when it re-floated at the next high tide.  The casualty vessel was then towed to a local pier where it was pumped out and allowed to ground for assessment and repair.  The yacht had some internal flooding and possible consequential damage to the electrics and the inboard engine.
Damage_Description: Hull damaged allowing flooding. Consequential flood water damage to electrics and engine

Short_Description: A yacht crewmember had a back injury after falling down a hatch.
