Description: A yacht crewmember fell through a hatch injuring their back during an offshore race. After spending two days in bed they were recovered ashore after the yacht returned to its berth.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had a propeller shaft failure and required a tow.
Description: A vessel had a propeller shaft mechanical failure which resulted in a tow from a lifeboat. No damage was confirmed.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had engine failure and grounded.
Description: A fishing vessel lost engine power and drifted onto rocks. A short time later, the vessel's engine power was restored. The vessel made its own way off the rocks and back to port, undamaged.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. The ladder was not secured effectively.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel lost propulsion and steerage and had to anchor. The vessel was taken under tow to port.
Description: A general cargo vessel had a blackout and lost propulsion and steering. A coupling between the main engine and the gearbox failed and could not be repaired. The ship dropped anchor in a traffic separation scheme and initially the anchored dragged until it then held. A tug arrived the next day and towed the vessel back to port.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship
Damage_Description: Coupling between engine flywheel and gearbox failed.

Short_Description: An ocean rowing boat capsized with four crew onboard
Description: An ocean rowing boat with four crew onboard was out on a training row when the boat capsized in deteriorating weather conditions. A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was tasked to the scene. One crew member had sustained a head injury and was evacuated by helicopter and taken to hospital. The other three crew initially stayed on board whilst the SAR vessel started towing but were later taken off when the rowing boat capsized again. The rowing boat later sunk after it was left to drift.

Short_Description: A container ship's crew used a dangerously weighted heaving line.
Description: A container ship's crew used a dangerously weighted heaving line.

Short_Description: A service vessel crewmember slipped on a step and injured their head.
Description: A service vessel crewmember was transiting down a stairwell when they slipped on a step and fell receiving a 10 centimetre laceration at the back of their head and bruising to their nose.

Short_Description: A small passenger vessel experienced engine failure and subsequently grounded.
Description: A small passenger vessel was on an evening trip when the vessel's two engines failed. The vessel drifted with the wind and ebbing tide, before the anchor could be deployed the vessel was in shallow water and then grounded. The fire service attended and evacuated the nine passengers and one crew member, and two crew remained onboard until the vessel re-floated on the next tide. The vessel proceeded to its mooring without any assistance. No injuries to passengers or crew reported, no damage to vessel.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser had engine failure resulting in the vessel going aground.
Description: A motor cruiser had engine failure with one person on board, as a result of the engine failure the vessel went aground on the mud and was towed free.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder was in poor condition.
Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder was in poor condition as the whippings were loose and frayed.

Short_Description: A tug vessel crewmember fell and sustained a gash to the underside of their forearm
Description: A crewmember was onboard a tug alongside taking some photographs in the engine room. They turned and fell down a step where the level drops in the engine room, as they were distracted looking at the phone. Their forearm made contact with the main engine platform causing a deep tissue wound to the underside of their forearm. The casualty was taken to hospital for treatment.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had engine failure and water ingress.
Description: A fishing vessel had engine failure and water ingress. Three other fishing vessels came to help the casualty vessel with pumps and established a tow.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship

Short_Description: A passenger vessel had engine failure and was towed.
Description: A passenger vessel had engine failure and was towed.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel grounded after a crewmember fell asleep during their watch.
Description: The vessel was engaged in seabed mapping, the watchkeeper was called to start their watch when they fell asleep and the vessel grounded. Damage was sustained to three frames and water ingress was also seen in the fish room and the vessel required repairs to be made to the hull
Damage_Description: Hull damage and three frames damaged

Short_Description: A vehicle carrier vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: Vehicle carrier vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. The bottom rubber rung was damaged.

Short_Description: A RIB passenger fell overboard.
Description: A RIB (rigid inflatable boat) passenger fell over board. They were wearing a life jacket and were rescued from the water and given warm clothes. The boat reportedly hooked causing the passenger to be ejected overboard.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.

Short_Description: A cruise ship passenger lost their balance and fell resulting in a hip fracture.
Description: A cruise ship passenger lost their balance in the restaurant and fell over resulting in a broken hip.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel made contact with a carriage on recovery resulting in minor damage
Description: A search and rescue (SAR)  vessel was returning to shore for a recovery after the completion of an exercise. During the stern recovery onto the carriage, a gust moved the vessel resulting in the starboard propeller getting caught on the trailer. The SAR vessel was recovered and returned to the station. There were no injuries to the crew, the propeller was damaged but there was no other vessel damage.

Short_Description: A remote unmanned survey vessel capsized in large swell
Description: A remote Unmanned Surface Vehicle (USV) was approaching its support vessel when it was manoeuvred broadside onto a large wave. The wave broke and capsized the craft, it remained afloat and the support vessel was able to tow it into harbour.

Short_Description: A dive vessel reported electronic chart failure whilst underway in fog.
Description: A dive vessel reported electronic chart failure whilst underway in fog.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier had a near miss with a lock after a bow thruster malfunction.
Description: On the vessel's approach to a lock, the pilot realised that the bow thruster was having little to no effect and struggled to keep the ship aligned with the lock. Attending tugs were used to manoeuvre the vessel back on course.  No apparent grounding or contact occurred.

Short_Description: A tug grounded during operations.
Description: A tug grounded during port operations. There was no damage to the vessel and the vessel later re-floated on the flood tide.

Short_Description: An offshore supply vessel experienced steering failure and avoided making contact with a quayside.
Description: An offshore supply experienced steering failure and avoided making contact with a quayside.

Short_Description: A chemical tanker's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A chemical tanker's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. The ladder had gaps of approximately 20 to 30 millimetres between the steps and chocks such that steps were not held in place. The crewmember present had not checked the ladder and did not believe that it was their duty to do so.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged in compliance with SOLAS guidance.
Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged in compliance with SOLAS guidance.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel dropped it's anchor to avoid a collision with a bridge
Description: A general cargo vessel was on passage and approaching a bridge, the vessel was turned hard to starboard but the effect of wind and tide did not turn the vessel enough so the vessel was still heading towards the bridge. To avoid a collision with the bridge, an anchor was dropped and with the strong tide, the vessel swung around on the anchor. The  anchor was later recovered and the vessel continued on it's passage. No reported grounding, vessel damage or injuries to crew.

Short_Description: A service ship made contact with a jetty during dredging operations.
Description: A dredger was undertaking harbour dredging operations in close proximity to a ro-ro terminal. When turning the vessel around, the combined strength and effect of the wind and tide were underestimated and the vessel made contact with the ro-ro jetty. Engineering support was required to repair the damage to the dredge gear.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship
Damage_Description: Vessel sustained damage to stbd dredge equipment.  Jetty ladder damaged, pending further investigations by jetty staff. Vessel was unable to continue dredging and the damage sustained required shore assistance to repair.

Short_Description: A ro-ro ferry had a fire on its main car deck.
Description: During routine cargo loading operations on the main car deck of a ro-ro ferry, a refrigerated trailer had been plugged in to the vessels 3 phase 415v system. Within a few minutes of the trailer being plugged in, smoke and flames were seen to be coming from the trailer's reefer unit. The vessel's crew reacted immediately by disconnecting the reefer cable and extinguished the flames using a dry powder extinguisher. The trailer was then removed from the vessel.
Damage_Description: Damage to a trailer within the vessel

Short_Description: An inland waterways vessel sank during towage.
Description: An inland waterways vessel sank whilst being towed. The vessel sank due to being swamped during towage. No damage was noted prior to departure. There was 120 litres of diesel onboard but it did not leak. Salvage was arranged for the vessel.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser was towed due to water ingress.
Description: A motor cruiser was towed due to water ingress.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel's mast collapsed and was taking on water.  The vessel was towed back to port.
Description: A sailing vessel's mast collapsed and was taking on water.  The vessel was towed back to port.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had engine failure and was towed back to port.
Description: A fishing vessel had engine failure and was towed back to port.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel capsized whilst dredging in shallow water
Description: A fishing vessel was dredging for oysters, another fishing vessel was nearby. The lone skipper had deployed the dredge line and bag, increased speed and started towing. The dredge line went taut and the bow came around to starboard. As the skipper stepped out of the wheelhouse, the starboard side dipped under the water and the boat quickly capsized and almost fully submerged despite the shallow water. The skipper, who was wearing a lifejacket, climbed the port side and entered the water. The other fishing vessel quickly recovered the skipper.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had engine issues.
Description: A fishing vessel had engine issues but managed to fix the problems and made their way to port without the need for a tow.

Short_Description: A tug received a weighted heaving line during tug operations.
Description: A tug received a heavily weighted heaving line. It was cut off by the tug crew and found to contain six mild steel ball bearings. The pilot was informed and photos taken and sent to the pilot who informed that the matter would be passed onto the ship's crew.

Short_Description: A sailing yacht had a de-masting and required assistance.
Description: A sailing yacht with a lone skipper onboard had a  de-masting. The mast was still attached but over the side of the yacht and dragging. The skipper requested assistance, a search and rescue (SAR) vessel was tasked to the scene, took the yacht under tow and placed one SAR crewmember onboard with the skipper. The SAR vessel then proceeded to tow the yacht to a port. No injuries to the skipper were reported.

Short_Description: A wind farm support vessel reported a starboard engine fire alarm activation.
Description: A windfarm vessel reported a starboard engine fire alarm activation. The engine was shut down and vents isolated. The vessel maintained position until another support vessel arrived.  The vessel was then escorted back to port. No damage or injuries were sustained.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel was taken under tow after engine failure.
Description: A fishing vessel with one person on board had engine failure and was towed back to port. There was no damage to the vessel or injuries.

Short_Description: A vessel had a non-compliant pilot ladder arrangement.
Description: The rigging of the pilot ladder was not checked, or the embarkation and/or disembarkation of the pilot was not supervised by a watch keeping deck officer.  The pilot station was manned by one crewmember during pilot boarding.

Short_Description: A SAR vessel crewmember dislocated their shoulder after a wave hit the sponson and threw them into the air.
Description: An inflatable SAR (search and rescue) boat was launched to conduct surf rescue training. While manoeuvring out through the waves, a large wave broke just in front of the bow. As the wave hit the bow, a crewmember leaned forwards to stop the vessel from lifting too high at the bow. Their foot came out of the foot strap and the wave hitting the sponson threw them into the air. The crewmember landed on their shoulder resulting in a dislocation.

Short_Description: A tanker made contact with fendering during berthing operations.
Description: The vessel touched the forward of the two-terminal fender during berthing operation and the fender collapsed. The movement speed of the vessel was less than one knot (0.5 metres per second).

Short_Description: A cruise ship passenger fractured their tibia following a fall.
Description: A cruise ship passenger tripped on the threshold between their cabin bathroom and the main cabin area. They subsequently fractured their right ankle

Short_Description: A grab hopper dredger made contact with a pier upon departure.
Description: During departure from a turning basin to proceed to a spoil ground, a dredger made contact with the pier. The wind speed and direction at the time of departure caught the vessel's starboard quarter and accentuated the set towards the pier preventing a normal turn to port. In order to correct the adverse drift direction, power had to be applied with port helm initially and then starboard helm was given. The vessel's speed then made the point of contact stronger. The pier itself was undamaged and only minor damage was sustained to the vessel's rubbing band.

Short_Description: Duplicate of 4037/2021
Description: Duplicate of 4037/2021

Short_Description: A near miss collision occurred between a ferry and a yacht.
Description: The yacht was overtaking, passing down the port side of the ferry as the ferry was in its final approach to the ferry berth in the harbour. The skipper of the yacht thought the ferry was departing, not entering. This put the yacht between the pier and the ferry berth. Yacht was speeding and slowed down in front of the ferry as it approached the ferry berth just north of the harbour entrance, ferry sounded five short blasts on the ships whistle and engaged astern gear. The yacht then continued in to the harbour to berth for the night.

Short_Description: A near miss collision occurred between a ferry and a yacht.
Description: The yacht was overtaking, passing down the port side of the ferry as the ferry was in its final approach to the ferry berth in the harbour. The skipper of the yacht thought the ferry was departing, not entering. This put the yacht between the pier and the ferry berth. Yacht was speeding and slowed down in front of the ferry as it approached the ferry berth just north of the harbour entrance, ferry sounded five short blasts on the ships whistle and engaged astern gear. The yacht then continued in to the harbour to berth for the night.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel capsized and sank.
Description: A traditional sailing fishing boat capsized and sunk in five metres of water. The two people on board who were wearing lifejackets were recovered from the water by a nearby fishing vessel. The vessel was refloated and returned alongside. Neither of the crew were injured.
Damage_Description: The vessel capsized and sunk, but was recovered shortly after

Short_Description: A SAR vessel grounded after fouling propeller on line
Description: A SAR (search and rescue) vessel was launched to assist a RHIB with four persons on board that had had engine failure and was drifting towards sea defence rocks. Just prior to arriving on scene the SAR vessel was informed that the casualty vessel was now aground on the rocks. Three of the persons had managed to scramble from the craft up onto the rocks and onto the concrete walkway above. One person was reported to be unaccounted for and the SAR vessel continued to proceed. The SAR vessel arrived on scene and was informed that all four persons from the casualty craft were now accounted for and in the company of a rescue team who were on the walkway above the craft. The decision was taken to make an attempt to tow the casualty craft off the rocks and take it the short distance round the arm to shelter. The rescue team on shore agreed to assist by passing the rope from the shore to the SAR vessel in the water.  When attempting the tow, the SAR vessel broke down and began to drift onto the rocks. The crew of the SAR vessel lifted the props and found that they had been fouled by the towline. The SAR was then pressed by the wind and the waves onto the rocks of the harbour arm, making heavy contact and experiencing heavy rolling. The crew cleared the fouled propellers and made their way to a safe place to inspect the damage. There were no injures, but the hull had had gouging and deep scratches to the gelcoat. None of the damage was penetrating and there was no visible deformation indicating internal structural damage. Both engines were clear of any visible damage and were not known to have made any contact with the rocks during the grounding.

Short_Description: A cruise ship passenger fell over in the restaurant resulting in a broken shoulder.
Description: A cruise ship passenger was walking in the restaurant area on board when they fell and fractured their shoulder. They used crutches to aid them in walking and one of their crutches hit their foot causing them to overbalance and fall to the floor. They were diagnosed with a fractured shoulder.

Short_Description: The hirer of inland waterway cruiser fell onto jetty resulting in a leg injury.
Description: A person from an inland waterway hire cruiser fell from the vessel onto the wooden jetty and injured their leg. The casualty was assessed by paramedics and transferred to an ambulance.

Short_Description: A tug received a weighted heaving line.
Description: A tug received a weighted heaving line.

Short_Description: A yacht ran aground in soft mud.
Description: A yacht with three people on board ran aground on soft mud. There was no evident damage to the vessel but there was concern around the fin keel and how the yacht would settle.  In the end they decided to wait overnight for the incoming tide and self recovered.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel experienced engine failure and required a tow.
Description: A lifeboat towed the fishing vessel back to port due to engine failure.

Short_Description: An oil tanker's crew used a weighted heaving line.
Description: A crude oil tanker's crew used a weighted heaving line. The weight was cut off by the tug's crew and reported to the harbour authority.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger vessel and a vehicle carrier had a close quarters situation.
Description: A ro-ro passenger vessel and a vehicle carrier experienced a close quarters situation after the vehicle carrier sped up after boarding a pilot, but before the pilot arrived on the bridge. This resulted in the ro-ro passenger vessel doing a round turn to avoid a collision.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger vessel and a vehicle carrier had a close quarters situation.
Description: A ro-ro passenger vessel and a vehicle carrier experienced a close quarters situation after the vehicle carrier sped up after boarding a pilot, but before the pilot arrived on the bridge. This resulted in the ro-ro passenger vessel doing a round turn to avoid a collision.

Short_Description: A leisure fishing vessel had engine failure and a fuel leak which resulted in a tow from a lifeboat.
Description: A leisure fishing vessel had engine failure and fuel leaking into the starboard bilge. The fuel leaked from the injector pump and started to fill the starboard bilge with red diesel. The vessel was towed by a lifeboat into port.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel had propeller damage whilst recovering into a trailer.
Description: The SAR (search and rescue) vessel was on a practice exercise and was being recovered onto its trailer when the propeller made contact with the steel frame, taking the tips off all three blades.
Damage_Description: Damage to tips of propeller of the outboard engine.

Short_Description: A trawling fishing vessel dragged their nets across the anchor and chain of another vessel.
Description: A trawler fishing vessel dragged its net over the anchor of a private fishing vessel. The crewmember onboard the anchored vessel cut their anchor line to avoid being dragged and potentially sustaining damage.

Short_Description: A trawling fishing vessel dragged their nets across the anchor and chain of another vessel.
Description: A trawler fishing vessel dragged its net over the anchor of a private fishing vessel. The crewmember onboard the anchored vessel cut their anchor line to avoid being dragged and potentially sustaining damage.

Short_Description: A tug crewmember lost balance and fell down stairs and sustained a head injury.
Description: A crewmember was carrying out maintenance on a vent, after a review of CCTV footage was made, the crewmember was seen to have fallen from the top of the ladder/stairs to the main deck due to possibly losing their balance. The crewmember had sustained a brain injury in the past and the reason for the incident is still unknown

Short_Description: A container ship crewmember was injured while clearing an accommodation ladder snag
Description: A container ship crewmember was injured while trying to stow the ship's accommodation ladder. While standing on the quay, a shore-side forklift was assisting in lifting the bottom of the accommodation ladder clear of an obstruction when it became snagged. The crewmember was trying to see what was snagging the ladder when it broke free and hit them in the jaw. They were taken to hospital and underwent surgery to their jaw.

Short_Description: A cruise ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A cruise ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. The rigging of the pilot ladder was not checked, or the embarkation and/or disembarkation of the pilot was not supervised by a watch keeping deck officer.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel crewmember fell overboard.
Description: A fishing vessel crewmember was found to be missing when the skipper rose from their bunk. A PLB (personal locator beacon) had been activated and a search and rescue operation was undertaken. The crewmember was found safe and well after approximately 1 hour - 1.5 hours in the water.

Short_Description: A SAR craft's propeller made contact with rock groyne.
Description: A SAR (search and rescue) vessel was attending an emergency of a vessel on fire. It was acting as a cordon at the time and the conditions pushed the vessel close to a rock groyne. The vessel's propeller touched the groyne and then moved away. As a result, the propellers had burred edges and it was filed back down on returning to the station.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder parted whilst the pilot was disembarking.
Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder failed when the pilot was disembarking. The rope parted and the bottom step  fell. The pilot fell about one metre and landed on their ankle.  No damage to the ladder was seen when the pilot was boarding the vessel.
Damage_Description: Pilot ladder rope parted and bottom step fell

Short_Description: A fishing vessel collided with a stationary yacht.
Description: A sailing yacht had broken down and while trying to fix the issue a passing fishing vessel collided with the yacht.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel collided with a stationary yacht.
Description: A sailing yacht had broken down and while trying to fix the issue a passing fishing vessel collided with the yacht.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. The pilot ladder was in a poor state and appeared weathered. The distance spacers were loose on numerous steps, causing the steps to tilt. The ladder was shackled to eyebolts on deck and a man rope was leading aft.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger ferry made contact with a RIB while protecting three dinghies.
Description: A ro-ro passenger ferry had a close quarters situation with three sailing dinghies who were struggling to manoeuvre out of the way of the ferry. The sailing clubs safety RIB (rigid inflatable boat) then placed itself in between the ferry and the dinghies to protect them before helping them out of the way.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger ferry made contact with a RIB while protecting three dinghies.
Description: A ro-ro passenger ferry had a close quarters situation with three sailing dinghies who were struggling to manoeuvre out of the way of the ferry. The sailing clubs safety RIB (rigid inflatable boat) then placed itself in between the ferry and the dinghies to protect them before helping them out of the way.

Short_Description: A SAR craft's two propellers made contact with the seabed during a rescue.
Description: A search and rescue (SAR) craft was assigned to secure a recreational fishing vessel which had lost power and was being blown ashore by onshore winds with three persons onboard. The SAR vessel entered known shallow water to try and make fast a tow line. Whilst trying to conduct the rescue in windy and choppy wave conditions, both outboard engines made contact with the seabed causing damage. Due to complications with trying to tow the casualty vessel to a place of safety in breaking waves, the towline was cut and the casualty vessel left to beach.
Damage_Description: Damage to both propellers. Superficial gel coat damage.

Short_Description: A catamaran capsized and was towed by a fishing vessel.
Description: A catamaran capsized and the two persons on board were recovered by a FRC (fast rescue craft) from a local ferry and found not to require any medical assistance. A fishing boat provided a tow and a local lifeboat also observed the vessel until they reached the harbour safely. No damage was confirmed to the vessel.

Short_Description: A pilot fell overboard after disembarking a vessel during heavy swell.
Description: The pilot was disembarking the vessel when they fell into the water between the ship's starboard side and the pilot boat due to the effects of the swell on the pilot boat. The master put the helm hard to starboard and crew on deck released life buoy with a rope. The pilot managed to grab a securing rope alongside the pilot boat and they were recovered from the water onto the pilot boat.

Short_Description: A motorboat reported a fire on board and was towed back to the marina.
Description: A motorboat reported fire on board and was towed back to the marina. The fire was extinguished and no damage was sustained.

Short_Description: A vehicle carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged as per current SOLAS regulations.
Description: A vehicle carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged as per current SOLAS regulations. A heaving line was not available for immediate use. The ladder was hung from a step pulled over the back of the ladder guide below the air driven spool. The crew were told to unhook and hang the ladder from the spool and secure the side ropes to the deck.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel had an engine failure and collided with an unoccupied vessel
Description: A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was tasked to assist a yacht pinned under an arch of a bridge with its bow facing up-river with a flow estimated at four to six knots. The SAR vessel was in the process of investigating for signs of occupancy and to attach a tow line when the port engine unexpectedly stopped. Due to the river flow the SAR vessel allided and both vessels became entangled. The SAR vessel manoeuvred away with one engine, the yacht passed under the bridge. The ~SAR vessel managed to secure the yacht to a mooring before returning to station. Both vessels sustained damage, no reported crew injuries.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel had an engine failure and collided with an unoccupied vessel
Description: A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was tasked to assist a yacht pinned under an arch of a bridge with its bow facing up-river with a flow estimated at four to six knots. The SAR vessel was in the process of investigating for signs of occupancy and to attach a tow line when the port engine unexpectedly stopped. Due to the river flow the SAR vessel allided and both vessels became entangled. The SAR vessel manoeuvred away with one engine, the yacht passed under the bridge. The ~SAR vessel managed to secure the yacht to a mooring before returning to station. Both vessels sustained damage, no reported crew injuries.
Damage_Description: Top of mast broke away that had the direction finding equipment and blue light.

Short_Description: A suction dredger's forward spring parted and caused a snap-back near miss with two crew members.
Description: A suction dredger's forward spring became caught between the vessel and sharp corner of a fender causing the line to be cut and subsequently part. Two crew members were within the snap-back zone but the rope missed them both.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier made contact with a lock entrance.
Description: A bulk carrier was making its approach to a lock when it made heavy contact with the east outer knuckle, piercing the bulbous bow. An investigation was carried out. No injuries to crew were reported.

Short_Description: A guard vessel made contact with a navigation buoy.
Description: A guard vessel made contact with a navigational buoy which resulted in a cracked hull and water ingress. Search and rescue vessels attended and pumped the water out of the machinery space and the vessel was able to make its own way back to port under its own power for repairs to be carried out. No injuries to crew were reported.
Damage_Description: Crack to the hull that allowed water to ingress.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel passed between two vessels and severed the tow line.
Description: A general cargo vessel passed between two vessels and severed the tow line.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel passed between two vessels and severed the tow line.
Description: A general cargo vessel passed between two vessels and severed the tow line.

Short_Description: A cruise ship at anchor sustained structural damage to the aft boiler trunking. There were no injuries.
Description: A cruise ship crew at anchor heard a loud bang towards the stern. On investigation some structural damage was found to the aft boiler trunking. There was no fire and no injuries.
Damage_Description: Structural damage was found to the aft boiler trunking.

Short_Description: A recreational fishing boat reported gear problems.
Description: A recreational fishing boat reported gear problems and required assistance back into the marina.

Short_Description: A tanker's pilot ladder was SOLAS non-compliant.
Description: A tanker's pilot ladder was not rigged per current SOLAS regulations.  Ladder secured at an intermediate length with shackles over the side ropes.

Short_Description: A SAR craft capsized during a routine exercise after the engine cut out. It self-righted itself and returned to harbour.
Description: A search and rescue (SAR) vessel capsized during a routine training exercise after the engine stalled and the crew were unable to hold the boat head to sea in the surf using the oars alone. The vessel then capsized, managed to self-right itself and made it back into harbour safely. There were no injuries to any persons onboard.

Short_Description: A commercial RIB grounded on a sandbar and was towed by a privately owned vessel.
Description: A RIB (rigid inflatable boat) grounded on a sandbar and another RIB towed them off safely and back into port. No damage was confirmed.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel on a lee shore dragged anchor, but managed to motor into safe water.
Description: A general cargo vessel dragged anchor in adverse weather conditions and was close to grounding. The crew attempted to hold position using the engine but continued to drag closer to shore. Lifeboats and a rescue helicopter were initially tasked but were stood down once the vessel recovered under its own power to safer water. There was no reported damage or injuries.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel was towed by another vessel after experiencing engine failure.
Description: A fishing vessel was towed by another fishing vessel after experiencing engine failure.  During the tow, power was restored and the tow released.

Short_Description: A motor boat fouled its propeller.
Description: A motor boat with one person on board fouled its propeller. The lifeboat was tasked to assist and freed the propeller and then escorted the casualty vessel to its marina.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel's pilot embarkation point was not free of obstructions.
Description: A cargo vessel's pilot embarkation point was not free of obstructions.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel grounded and was towed by a lifeboat.
Description: A fishing vessel fouled its propeller with fishing gear, attempted to anchor and the anchor was lost due to a cable snapping. The vessel grounded on a nearby rocky shore. Search and rescue assets attended and found the crew safe and well. The vessel was re-floated on the next high tide with the assistance of a lifeboat. The vessel was towed into port by the lifeboat.

Short_Description: A container ship's crewmember fell through a hatch.
Description: A container ship's crewmember was checking reefer containers on the cross deck when they fell through a hatch onto the upper platform of the cargo hold. The fall was around 4 meters. The crewmember was found by another crewmember who was returning to close the hatch. They were taken to the medical centre and following medical advice they were sent ashore for further treatment

Short_Description: A chemical tanker's crew threw a weighted heaving line.
Description: A chemical tanker's crew threw a weighted heaving line.

Short_Description: A passenger vessel crewmember sustained scalds to their back following a burst header tank.
Description: A passenger vessel crewmember sustained scalds to their back when hot water burst out of a header tank in the engine room that was under pressure. The affected area of the body immediately blistered and the crewmember then stood under a cold shower for approximately 30 minutes. They were transferred by lifeboat ashore and then on to hospital in a taxi.

Short_Description: A chemical tanker's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A chemical tanker's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. There were no stanchions, it was not secure and the mechanical stopper on ladder reel was not in place, the ladder was held on the brake.  The pilot discussed with the master and provided copy of Pilot Boarding Arrangements Booklet.  The ladder was correctly rigged for disembarking.

Short_Description: A wooden crabber flooded and sank. Both crewmembers were safely rescued.
Description: A wooden crabber with two people on board flooded. Both crewmembers got into their life raft and were recovered and taken into the care of ambulance staff. The casualty vessel sank with reports of debris at the location.
Pollution_Result: Reports of debris floating in the water.

Short_Description: A hire yacht grounded and was towed by a lifeboat.
Description: A vessel grounded. It was found to be on the wrong side of a channel marker and a tow was arranged with a lifeboat to pull it off to safety. The vessel was taken into a harbour, checked over and no damage or any injuries to any persons on board were found.

Short_Description: A pleasure craft  fouled their propeller and drifted towards the shore.
Description: A motor boat with five people on board fouled their propeller on fishing gear and drifted towards the shoreline. The crew were preparing to drop anchor when it was shallow enough. After raising the alarm the vessel was taken under tow by a local lifeboat and then were assisted back to their marina berth.

Short_Description: A ro-pax ferry had a weld defect.
Description: A ro-pax ferry had a pin hole on its main engine's fuel line. This was thought to be caused by weld defect as pipe was not corroded.  The crew were concerned that this hole may lead to split fuel pipe with resulting fuel leakage into vessel bilges.  They stopped the engine in order to isolate the fuel line. The vessel returned to its port of departure for repairs without incident.

Short_Description: A crane barge crewmember fell overboard during a training exercise.
Description: During a training berthing evolution, a trainee deckhand fell overboard after holding onto another vessel rather than passing the berthing line. When the vessels slowly moved apart, they fell in the sea. Their lifejacket inflated and they were quickly recovered out of the water without injury.

Short_Description: A tug's crewmember sustained laceration to the face.
Description: A tug's crewmember had a laceration to their face, the local lifeboat attended but the casualty was able to make their own way to the hospital for further treatment.

Short_Description: A survey vessel made contact at a terminal and was holed above the waterline.
Description: A survey vessel was holed above the waterline after contact with a ro-ro terminal during harbour survey operations.  The aluminium hull was punctured when it struck the link span. The vessel was lifted from the water for repair.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting structural integrity of the ship

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel capsized whilst on service.
Description: A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was tasked to a casualty in the water who had been cut off by the incoming tide. The location of the casualty required the SAR vessel to veer down to achieve a suitable position to recover the casualty.  During this manoeuvre the anchor became dislodged allowing the vessel to turn around into the surf, and possibly the chain caught in the propeller leading to the loss of propulsion. As a result the vessel capsized on the next set of waves. The three crew swam away from the shoreline to deeper water where they were rescued by another SAR vessel. No injuries were sustained to the crew. The vessel was later recovered and there was some damage to the propeller.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel's cargo moved during heavy seas.
Description: A cargo vessel experienced rough seas and the deck cargo shifted. However, the vessel made it safely to harbour.

Short_Description: A sail training vessel reported power loss and went to anchor to await engine repairs.
Description: A sail training vessel reported power loss and went to anchor to await engine repairs, which were scheduled for the next day.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel had flooding in the engine room due to incompatible replacement pipe.
Description: A search and rescue vessel was on a training exercise when the bilge alarm sounded. On inspection of the engine room, it was found that a replacement pipe had come off on one end and water was entering the engine room. The alarm was raised and the vessel brought to a stop. Attempts to  replace the pipe failed. After this, the vessel was rigged for single engine running and any water was pumped out. They returned to the slipway with no further issues and the original pipe was re-fitted. No major damage or injuries were sustained.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder rigging didn't conform to SOLAS.
Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder rigging didn't conform to SOLAS.

Short_Description: A trailer tug unit on a ro-ro passenger vessel had an electrical fire which was extinguished.
Description: A trailer tug unit on a ro-ro passenger vessel was noticed with smoke coming out of the cab. A crewmember turned off the battery isolator as the driver used a wet rag to extinguish the smoke. A foam extinguisher and hose was subsequently rigged as a precautionary measure. The vessel was bunkering at the time and this was immediately stopped. A relay in the cab had shorted and was then repaired by a mechanic. The unit then disembarked from the vehicle deck.

Short_Description: A shore representative fell from a gangway but was uninjured.
Description: A shore representative fell from a gangway but was uninjured.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. The pilot ladder was secured with shackles. The lower spreader and several steps were loose and most chocks on the ladder were loose. The ladder was secured with chocks resting on the edge of the pilot door.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel made contact with a wall as it was entering a lock.
Description: A cargo vessel assisted by to tugs was entering a lock, its bow struck a lock wall and a section of security fencing. There was no reported damage to the vessel but there was damage to the fencing, concrete wall and rubber fendering.

Short_Description: A racing sailing vessel grounded briefly causing one minor injury and damage to the keel bulb.
Description: A yacht with seven people on board that was racing made brief contact with an unidentified submerged object while tacking inshore out of the tide. The sudden stop caused a minor injury to one crewmember. Subsequently, after retiring from the race and returning to port, damage was found to the leading edge of the keel bulb approximately seven centimetres above its bottom.
Damage_Description: Crush damage to the leading edge of the keel bulb approx 3 inches above the bottom.

Short_Description: A tug crewmember fractured their elbow after hitting it on machinery.
Description: A tug crewmember sustained a fractured elbow during a fault finding inspection.

Short_Description: A cruise ship passenger fell down the stairs and broke their hip.
Description: A guest was descending the stairs on a cruise ship when they missed the last step and fell and sustained suspected hip injury.

Short_Description: A passenger on board ro-ro pax vessel fell down the stairs and had suspected fractured leg.
Description: A passenger on board ro-ro pax vessel fell down the stairs and had a suspected fracture.  An ambulance met the vessel in the harbour.

Short_Description: A container ship's anchor winch malfunctioned leading the anchor dragging.
Description: A container ship was anchored with nine shackles deployed. When attempting to retrieve the anchor the windlass would not work when under load. The crew attempted to repair the electric motor then replaced it with a spare one. They heaved two shackles and the windlass stopped again, causing the vessel to drag anchor. The master maintained position by using the engines and the windlass was repaired and the anchor brought home. It was observed that the anchor's fluke was missing. The vessel made it safely into port.
Damage_Description: The crew attempted to repair the electric motor and ultimately, they changed it with a spare one. Two shackles were heaved, and the windlass stopped once more, causing the vessel to drag her anchor. In consultation with the windlass's manufacturer, the crew repaired the windlass, and the anchor was brought home. It was also observed that the port anchor's fluke was missing.

Short_Description: A guard vessel had engine failure whilst towing a fishing vessel.
Description: A guard vessel was towing a fishing vessel back to port when it had engine failure. A search and rescue vessel was tasked to tow the stricken fishing vessel whilst another fishing vessel towed the guard. Both vessels made it safely to port. There was no damage to the vessels or crew injuries reported.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser broke down and was towed.
Description: A motor cruiser lost propulsion and was without an anchor. They ran the risk of running aground as they were being pushed on the shore so a lifeboat launched to conduct a rescue operation and towed vessel to port.

Short_Description: A motorboat fouled its propeller. Minor damage was caused to the propeller and a tow was arranged.
Description: A motorboat fouled its propeller with a plastic bag but the boat managed to moor at a wharf. A passing tug crew managed to clear the plastic bag but some damage was sustained to the propeller.  A tow was arranged to take the vessel back to their car and trailer.

Short_Description: A service ship experienced electrical failure which caused significant damage to many items.
Description: A service vessel had a large electrical surge causing significant damage to many items of critical equipment. The vessel was connected to shore power at time of incident.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship
Damage_Description: Vessel was connected to shore power. Believed surge causing significant electrical failure throughout the vessel. Resulting in critical items unrepairable.

Short_Description: A lifeboat damaged its propeller after hitting submerged rock during training.
Description: A lifeboat damaged its propeller after passing through a narrow passage when the propeller made contact with a submerged rock.

Short_Description: A passenger on commercial rib sustained a minor back injury.
Description: RIB ride passenger reported minor back pain after a high speed ride. The passenger had not followed the skippers instructions to hold on and was using a camera.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel fouled its propeller on its own gear and was towed.
Description: A fishing vessel fouled its propeller on its own gear and was towed.

Short_Description: A tanker reported engine failure during a harbour approach and required assistance to berth.
Description: A tanker with a pilot onboard was approaching a harbour when it experienced engine failure. Two tugs were already in attendance and pushed the vessel to its berth. The engine was tested and restarted.

Short_Description: An anchor handling supply vessel made contact with railings.
Description: The vessel commenced its move from the lock centrally then closed on a gate. Contact was made with the vessel's side fender tyres against the railings and upper timbers of the lock.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel grounded.
Description: During pilotage, the pilot became disorientated with their position and was convinced that they were in a position more south and more east than they were. The pilot admitted that they were confused on passage. The weather was fine and all landmarks were visually available to them.

Short_Description: A yacht crewmember injured their finger after getting it trapped in an anchor chain.
Description: The skipper of a yacht injured their finger after it was caught in an anchor chain. The vessel proceed safely to port where they went on to seek medical attention.

Short_Description: Recreational yachts collided after breaking from moorings during strong weather.
Description: All vessels were moored and during strong winds, the moorings dragged to create a collision. One vessel settled underneath the other with the rigging tangled. A lifeboat assisted in separating the vessels. Damage was sustained to both vessels.

Short_Description: Recreational yachts collided after breaking from moorings during strong weather.
Description: All vessels were moored and during strong winds, the moorings dragged to create a collision. One vessel settled underneath the other with the rigging tangled. A lifeboat assisted in separating the vessels. Damage was sustained to both vessels.

Short_Description: Recreational yachts collided after breaking from moorings during strong weather.
Description: All vessels were moored and during strong winds, the moorings dragged to create a collision. One vessel settled underneath the other with the rigging tangled. A lifeboat assisted in separating the vessels. Damage was sustained to both vessels.

Short_Description: Recreational yachts collided after breaking from moorings during strong weather.
Description: All vessels were moored and during strong winds, the moorings dragged to create a collision. One vessel settled underneath the other with the rigging tangled. A lifeboat assisted in separating the vessels. Damage was sustained to both vessels.

Short_Description: Recreational yachts collided after breaking from moorings during strong weather.
Description: All vessels were moored and during strong winds, the moorings dragged to create a collision. One vessel settled underneath the other with the rigging tangled. A lifeboat assisted in separating the vessels. Damage was sustained to both vessels.

Short_Description: Recreational yachts collided after breaking from moorings during strong weather.
Description: All vessels were moored and during strong winds, the moorings dragged to create a collision. One vessel settled underneath the other with the rigging tangled. A lifeboat assisted in separating the vessels. Damage was sustained to both vessels.

Short_Description: Recreational yachts collided after breaking from moorings during strong weather.
Description: All vessels were moored and during strong winds, the moorings dragged to create a collision. One vessel settled underneath the other with the rigging tangled. A lifeboat assisted in separating the vessels. Damage was sustained to both vessels.

Short_Description: A RIB grounded near the entrance to a harbour
Description: A RIB (rigid inflatable boat) went aground near the entrance of a harbour. The vessel was anchored in situ. A lifeboat was launched to assist the persons onboard. Three crew were recovered from the vessel. No injures or damage to the vessel occurred. The lifeboat later attended with the skipper once the vessel had re-floated and the vessel was recovered.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder rigging was not checked.
Description: The rigging of the pilot ladder was not checked, or the embarkation and/or disembarkation of the pilot was not supervised by a watch keeping deck officer. The pilot embarkation point on the deck was not free from obstructions. There was no officer present and the pilot was not escorted to the bridge. The deck was obstructed by a bunched up ladder and the handholds/stanchions were confusing.

Short_Description: A cruise ship passenger slipped whilst exiting a swimming pool and fractured their hand.
Description: A cruise ship passenger slipped after they stepped out of the swimming pool and were crossing the adjacent deck. Their left hand caught on a sunbed as they fell resulting in a fracture.

Short_Description: An oil tanker fouled its propeller during unberthing operations.
Description: The vessel was along side in heavy weather so extra mooring lines were added to secure the vessel. When unbreathing there was an issue with letting go of the stern lines resulting in three mooring lines in the water. The ebb tide and winds pushed the mooring lines under the vessel and two of them made contact with the starboard propeller. One line was cut and the other fouled the propeller. More lines were sent back ashore and divers were commissioned to free the propeller.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger vessel passenger fell down an internal stairway.
Description: A ro-ro passenger ferry passenger was noted to be unsteady on their feet, they had already fallen once during the passage so the ferry staff had planned to escort them to the car deck upon arrival. The passenger had already attempted to make their own way to the car deck where they had fallen down an internal staircase, fourteen steps, resulting in them being knocked unconscious and bleeding from their mouth and nose. Staff members kept their airways clear and an ambulance was called to meet the passenger at port.

Short_Description: See MAIB investigation report, when available
Description: See MAIB investigation report, when available
Damage_Description: See MAIB investigation report, when available

Short_Description: A RIB ran aground and was towed back to port.
Description: A lifeboat was tasked to recover a RIB (rigid inflatable boat) that had gone aground with one person on board. The vessel was towed back to port.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser grounded, sustaining propeller damage, and had to be refloated and towed by a lifeboat.
Description: A motorboat with two anglers on board grounded on a beach, it appears intentionally. The crew went ashore for food. On trying to depart from the beach on the rising tide it was evident the vessel's propeller was damaged and the vessel had no other means of propulsion. A lifeboat successfully re-floated the vessel and a tow was established to return the vessel to its home port.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship

Short_Description: A fishing vessel began taking on water after a pipe burst.
Description: A fishing vessel started to fill with water after a pipe had burst expelling water into the vessel. The bilge alarms sounded alerting the crew to the water ingress. The bilge pumps where used to expel the water, once the water level was low enough the crew could see that the water was coming from a burst pipe and closed the valve to stop the flow.

Short_Description: A Ro-Ro cargo vessel's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: A Ro-Ro cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged to SOLAS regulations. The ladder's weight was borne by the top step on two hooks (this was not visible from the pilot cutter). A tripping line led aft. A discussion was held with the crew and the ladder was rectified during the passage.

Short_Description: A kayaker capsized and was later found deceased.
Description: A kayaker capsized and was later found deceased.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel grounded and started taking on water.
Description: The vessel grounded resulting in the crew abandoning via lifeboat which was half submerged initially. The vessel owner salvaged the vessel and no injuries or pollution were reported.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting structural integrity of the ship

Short_Description: A vessel's pilot ladder construction did not meet current SOLAS standards.
Description: A vessel's pilot ladder construction did not meet current SOLAS standards. The side ropes of the ladder were in poor condition. The Master was informed and another ladder was rigged. The second ladder was in good condition and was 2 months old.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder rigging didn't conform to SOLAS.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder rigging didn't conform to SOLAS because it used a trap door arrangement.

Short_Description: An inbound tanker lost propulsion, veered from the fairway, then grounded. The vessel was towed to safety by a tug.
Description: An inbound bitumen tanker lost propulsion and sheered out of the channel. The starboard anchor was dropped as the vessel left the channel but the vessel ran aground close to a gas pipeline. The propulsion was restored promptly and the vessel was brought astern and clear of the gas pipeline. The vessel was assisted by a tug as well.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel crewmember was seasick and fell and injured their head. A lifeboat assisted the casualty and vessel to harbour.
Description: A single handed sailing vessel skipper was experiencing sea sickness. There was an engine malfunction and they fell and hit their head when they tried to examine the issue. They made a mayday call and a helicopter and lifeboat were deployed. The lifeboat crew rescued the skipper and brought them ashore. The helicopter was not needed and the lifeboat crew brought the vessel safely into harbour to be reunited with the skipper, who by then felt much better.
Damage_Description: Engine overheated, but vessel was sailed into harbour.

Short_Description: A Fishing vessel lost power and was drifting towards rocks. It was towed back to harbour.
Description: A fishing vessel lost propulsion and was drifting towards rocks. A nearby vessel towed the casualty vessel back to port.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel crewmember had facial injuries after being hit with a metal bar.
Description: A general cargo vessel crewmember evacuated and taken to shore for medical assistance after being hit in the face by a metal pole resulting in damage to the casualties lip and missing teeth.

Short_Description: A suction dredger had a fire.
Description: A fire was discovered by a crewmember at a junction box for the boiler room in the forward machinery space. The fire was extinguished by the crew member, the boiler switched off and the situation monitored to ensure the fire was successfully extinguished.

Short_Description: A port tender had engine failure and had to disengage from mooring operations.
Description: A port tender had a malfunction to its starboard engine. This resulted in it disengaging in mooring operations and had to return to the jetty.
Damage_Description: Malfunctioning starboard engine that forced it to cease mooring operations.

Short_Description: A sailing yacht grounded and required assistance.
Description: A sailing yacht with three crew onboard grounded on a bank and was unable to get the vessel into deeper water. A search and rescue vessel towed the yacht into deeper water and then escorted the yacht until the crew onboard confirmed there was no visible damage or water ingress to the yacht. No injures to the crew were reported.

Short_Description: A commercial RIB passenger had a fractured rib.
Description: A commercial RIB (rigid inflatable boat) passenger injured one of their ribs at the beginning of a trip whilst the boat was weaving. They were squashed on a bench seat and crushed their rib on the arm rest as the weight of the other passengers slid against them. The casualty left the vessel at the end of the trip and did not inform the skipper at the time. The fractured rib was reported retrospectively.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel had an engine fire which was extinguished by crew.
Description: A sailing vessel with two crew had an engine fire which was extinguished by the crew. The vessel sailed back to port but was assisted alongside by the lifeboat where the fire service checked the vessel confirming the fire was out. There were no injures and damage was mainly limited to smoke damage in the cabin.

Short_Description: A chemical tanker ran aground.
Description: A chemical tanker ran aground with 13,000mt of fuel on board. The vessel was re-floated at high water and taken to anchorage. No apparent damage was sustained to the vessel or pollution.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel had a near miss with yacht moorings while swinging in an estuary.
Description: A general cargo vessel had a near miss with yacht moorings while swinging in an estuary.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel fouled it's propeller and was towed to shore.
Description: A fishing vessel fouled it's propeller and was drifting offshore and lost all propulsion. A search and rescue vessel deployed and towed the vessel back to a place of safety.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had a fire onboard that was extinguished by the crew.
Description: A fishing vessel crewmember smelt smoke and sounded the fire alarm. An investigation found that there was a fire in the fish room. All crew assembled and were accounted for, a fire team and medical team were assembled. The vents to accommodation were closed and hoses run out. The fire team went in and the fire was quickly extinguished. The source of the fire was a battery in a fork lift truck. After a consultation it was determined that fire was out and the fish room was vented before heading to port for repair. The fork lift was damaged and fish and packaging was also contaminated.
Damage_Description: Only damage is to the fork lift truck battery and also contamination to the fish in fishroom and packaging

Short_Description: Passenger ship vehicle edging deck panel fell from the deck head. No one was injured.
Description: Passenger ship vehicle deck edging panel fell from the deck head and landed on the vehicle deck. This panel was 1.2m long weighed 2.7kg and fell from a height of 2.6m. At the time, the vehicle deck was clear of all passengers, crew and vehicles. The fixings had failed. The panel was reattached and all others were checked.
Damage_Description: Vehicle deck edging panel fell from the deck head and landed on the vehicle deck.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser crewmember fell down a staircase and sustained a head injury.
Description: A motor cruiser crewmember fell down a staircase and hit their head. The crewmember remained responsive but was not feeling well. A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was tasked to the scene to assess the crewmember until an ambulance arrived.

Short_Description: A hire cruiser sank. All persons were rescued without injury.
Description: A hire cruiser sank with eight people on board. All persons were rescued without injury. The owner arranged for the vessel to be lifted the following day.
Pollution_Result: Vessel sank. Fuel will have been on board.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger vessel accidentally released their anchor on approach to harbour.
Description: A ro-ro passenger vessel accidentally released their anchor on approach to harbour. Approximately two cables ran out and the anchor was initially dragged along the sea bed. It transpired that the automatic release mechanism failed at speed and the entire port anchor cable was let go.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel crew member sustained a minor eye injury
Description: Whilst a cargo vessel was departing port, the steam boiler fan failed. A crew member had removed the fan and started on the repair. Whilst pulling the bearing, one of the ball bearings broke and its metal filings got into the crew member's eye. The eye was examined but no visible pieces were found but the crew member still felt discomfort in the eye. Once ashore the crew member went to hospital for an examination.

Short_Description: A vessel experienced propulsion failure and was towed.
Description: A hopper barge experienced propulsion failure and was towed back to port.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel crewmember had a cut to their upper arm.
Description: A fishing vessel crewmember had a cut to their left arm above the elbow. There was still bleeding when pressure was added. The crewmember was conscious and was moved to an ambulance once they reached shore.

Short_Description: A tanker developed a list while alongside and found a small penetration on the turn of the bilge, amidships.
Description: Tanker went alongside to refuel. Within a few hours the vessel developed a list. Following an investigation, they found a small penetration (20mm) on the turn of the bilge, amidships. The causes and circumstances of the accident have not been determined despite a company investigation.
Damage_Description: 20 mm penetration into double hull ballast space.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser had engine failure and was towed back to its mooring.
Description: A motor cruiser had engine failure and was towed back to its mooring.

Short_Description: An inflatable rescue boat capsized during training. Boat recovered with no injuries.
Description: An inflatable rescue boat capsized during a training exercise. On turning, the easterly wind and swell, as well as the distribution of persons in the boat rolled the boat from starboard to port. All crew and the boat were recovered ashore. The outboard was flushed and the restarting procedure followed before training resumed.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel nearly capsized as a result of the wash from a passing tug.
Description: A fishing vessel nearly capsized as a result of the wash from a tug passing close by. No injuries to crew or damage to vessel were reported.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel nearly capsized as a result of the wash from a passing tug.
Description: A fishing vessel nearly capsized as a result of the wash from a tug passing close by. No injuries to crew or damage to vessel were reported.

Short_Description: A sailing student had a serious back injury when a sailing dinghy collided with them.
Description: Training in sailing dinghies was taking place at a sailing club. A dinghy with an experienced helm and trainee was demonstrating coming alongside an anchored safety boat. A catamaran crewed by three people was also out free sailing and was returning to the sailing club and was sailing through the training area. During a gybing manoeuvre, to avoid another craft the catamaran collided with the two person dinghy. The starboard catamaran hull rode up the side of the dinghy and hit the trainee on the back causing significant pain. All training was stopped and the injured person was returned ashore by towing the dinghy they were in. They were meet by an ambulance crew and taken to hospital for treatment. They had internal injuries as result of the accident.

Short_Description: A sailing student had a serious back injury when a sailing dinghy collided with them.
Description: Training in sailing dinghies was taking place at a sailing club. A dinghy with an experienced helm and trainee was demonstrating coming alongside an anchored safety boat. A catamaran crewed by three people was also out free sailing and was returning to the sailing club and was sailing through the training area. During a gybing manoeuvre, to avoid another craft the catamaran collided with the two person dinghy. The starboard catamaran hull rode up the side of the dinghy and hit the trainee on the back causing significant pain. All training was stopped and the injured person was returned ashore by towing the dinghy they were in. They were meet by an ambulance crew and taken to hospital for treatment. They had internal injuries as result of the accident.

Short_Description: A sailing yacht grounded and flooded its engine.
Description: A sailing vessel grounded on a slipway and the outboard engine flooded. The three occupants abandoned vessel on the slipway. A lifeboat towed the boat off the slipway to a nearby marina. There was no damage to the boat and no injuries.

Short_Description: A motor vessel collided with a sailing yacht.
Description: A motor vessel was coming towards a sailing yacht and did not alter course resulting in a collision causing minor damage to the sailing yacht.

Short_Description: A motor vessel collided with a sailing yacht.
Description: A motor vessel was coming towards a sailing yacht and did not alter course resulting in a collision causing minor damage to the sailing yacht.

Short_Description: A yacht grounded on a wreck, started flooding and required a tow to safety.
Description: A yacht with three people on board ran aground on a wreck outside the harbour and started taking on water. On a rising tide they were cleared of the wreck and towed to safety by another vessel for repairs and assessment. No persons were injured.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting structural integrity of the ship

Short_Description: A tug crewmember injured their back whilst changing a tow wire.
Description: A tug boat's injured crewmember was part of a five-person team attempting to change the tug's tow wire whilst alongside. The crewmember felt a small twinge in the lower left side of their back and thought nothing more of it. Later the pain started to get worse and they reported it. They went home to rest and hoped that after a decent nights rest they would be fit for duty. The next day, it was apparent the crewmember was still in substantial pain and would not be able to carry out their full duties.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel experienced propulsion failure but regained power shortly afterwards.
Description: Fishing vessel experienced engine failure but regained power shortly afterwards and a lifeboat that had been dispatched was stood down before arrival at the scene.

Short_Description: A ro-ro cargo ferry shoreside crewmember fractured their arm during cargo loading operations.
Description: A tug driver sustained multiple open fractures to their arm. The incident occurred on a ro-ro vessel when the tug driver was in their cab reversing a trailer (cargo) and their arm was outside the window and became trapped between the tug and the vessel side.

Short_Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel briefly grounded whilst on passage to a port
Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel was inbound to port when the vessel started vibrating and made a few small rolls from side to side. A crew member on the bridge went to the starboard wing and saw the swell the vessel was dragging from briefly grounding. The  speed was again reduced and soon after everything was back to normal. The vessel continued to its berth.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser had water ingress and sank. The two people on board were rescued from the life raft.
Description: A motor cruiser had water ingress to the engine room, which eventually flooded and the two crew on board abandoned to the life raft and the vessel sank. The two people on board were rescued by a lifeboat and taken to shore, they did not sustain any injuries.

Short_Description: A cruise ship lost its port anchor.
Description: A cruise ship was at anchor in high winds when it started to drag the anchor. The crew started the engine and heaved up the anchor. They recovered the anchor cable, but the anchor itself was missing. The reason for this was thought to be a failed D shackle.

Short_Description: A cruise ship's UPS (uninterrupted power supply) failed resulting in a temporary interruption to bridge power supplies.
Description: The UPS (Uninterrupted Power Supply) safeguard failed, resulting in a temporary (a few seconds) interruption to bridge power supplies, causing all navigational equipment to reset and the vessel's gyros were unstable for some time.  A failed component in the UPS caused the problem.
Damage_Description: Loss of UPS 220 V AC Safeguard.

Short_Description: A shore operative was disembarking a fishing vessel and fell overboard.
Description: A shore operative boarded a fishing vessel to speak to a crew member, upon disembarking the vessel the shore operative fell between the fishing vessel and quay. A crewmember from the fishing vessel jumped into the water to keep the casualty afloat as they could not swim and did not have a life jacket on.  After they were recovered from the water CPR was preformed and the casualty airlifted to hospital. The casualty spent several days in hospital and returned home to recover.

Short_Description: A tug's expansion bellows split and released oil into the engine room.
Description: A tug's fire alarm sounded and when a crewmember checked the fire control panel it showed it was coming from the engine room. The crewmember made the other crew aware, stopped the engine and proceeded to the engine room to investigate. There was a lot of oil and smoke coming out of port engine but no flames noticed. An inspection found that the expansion bellows had split and had release approximately 1000 litres of engine oil into the engine room. The port authority was notified, the vessel returned to its berth and was taken out of service until new expansion bellows were fitted.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship
Damage_Description: Split expansion bellows for port main engine. Approx. 1000 litres of oil leaked into engine room

Short_Description: A cruise ship passenger fell down a staircase resulting in a fracture.
Description: A passenger on a cruise ship was walking down a staircase when they caught their heel and fell. They landed on their left shoulder on the deck at the base of the staircase. The passenger had a fracture to the left neck of their humerus bone.

Short_Description: A tug vessel crewmember injured their hip and back on a mooring barge.
Description: A tug crewmember had placed one end of a laden barge alongside moorings which had a second barge fixed to both ends. The crewmember was onboard the barge and was engaged in fastening the mooring lines whilst the barges came together. Once the line was fastened, the crewmember stood up and hit their right hip on the mooring barge, which caused them to lose their balance and also hit their back on the raised coaming of the laden barge. The casualty sustained bruising to their right hip and was off work for one week.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel single handed skipper broke a finger and had engine failure. A lifeboat assisted the casualty to port.
Description: A sailing vessel with just its skipper onboard had engine failure. The skipper had also broken their finger after catching it in a rope.  As they were drifting towards a wind farm a lifeboat was tasked to assist and towed the vessel back to port as the yacht had become becalmed.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel crewmember fractured their hand.
Description: Two fishing vessel crewmembers were in the process of securing the safety rope. The rope was secured while the trawl pins were approximately one metre above the deck. Once secured the pins are fully raised. While the middle pin was being raised, one of the crew put their hand on top of the pin just before it got to the fully raised position and fractured their hand.

Short_Description: A cruise ship crewmember fell in the engine room after a dizzy spell.
Description: One crewmember was working in the in the engine room assisting another crewmember to fill the bilge bulb with oil when they felt dizzy. The crewmember then fell forward, hitting their head against the floor. This caused a laceration on their forehead. They were taken to the medical centre where they were declared off–duty.

Short_Description: A sail training vessel grounded in the entrance of a harbour and was assisted by a lifeboat.
Description: A sail training vessel grounded at slow speed in the channel entrance to a marina. The search and rescue services were tasked to assist the vessel into the harbour, although if they had waited for the rising tide, the yacht would not have required assistance. There were no reported injuries or damage.

Short_Description: A cable laying vessel crewmember injured their knee after walking into machinery.
Description: A cable laying crewmember was walking in the engine room when they struck their knee joint on a main engine cylinder head. The pain increased until the crewmember could no longer bend their leg properly. They went ashore to a hospital where they were diagnosed with a contusion, fluid build up and swelling.

Short_Description: A nuclear fuel carrier crewmember slipped on the deck.
Description: Two crew members were working on deck preparing the pilot ladder for use. The vessel was alongside but they were experiencing bad weather with heavy rainfall. When unfurling the ladder, a crewmember slipped and fell on their back. After having the injury looked at, they returned to work soon after but their ankle was uncomfortable and it was later discovered after an X-ray that the ankle was broken despite having continued to work on board for over a month.

Short_Description: A chemical tanker's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: A chemical tanker's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. The pilot ladder and steps were in poor condition.

Short_Description: A cruise ship crewmember tipped on a pipe and sustained an injury.
Description: A crewmember on a cruise ship was moving a loaded trolley in an engine space. They were moving backwards pulling the trolley when their left foot hit a pipe on the deck. The trolley then hit the front of their left foot. The crewmember went to the medical centre where it was confirmed as a fracture to a bone in their left ankle. The crewmember was wearing company issued PPE (personal protective equipment) and the area was well illuminated.

Short_Description: A yacht broke down and was towed back to port.
Description: A sailing yacht broke down and was drifting near a ferry terminal so was towed back to the yacht club.

Short_Description: A work boat crewmember hit their hand on a fish farm cage.
Description: A crewmember hit their hand when disembarking the vessel on a fish farm cage. Later swelling was observed, but they felt no pain or discomfort at the time so it was not reported right away.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger ferry identified fire risk.
Description: Contractors were preparing to weld an insert which was cut on the main deck to carry out engine works just above the forward main engine. The area under which they were working was covered by fire blankets while the rest of the engine was covered with a thick plastic covering to protect it from debris going into the open engine components.  A gas cutter was being used to prepare the edges of the deck so that welding could be carried out. While this work was being carried out, it was noticed by the on duty fire watch attendant that the spatter from gas cutting was scattering past the fire blankets on to the plastic covers. Small flames were noticed by the duty fire attendant who immediately put the flame out using a foam extinguisher which was kept ready at the vicinity of the works being carried out in the engine room.
