Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger ferry made contact with a submerged rock.
Description: A ro-ro passenger vessel damaged its propulsion system after hitting a suspected submerged rock.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship
Damage_Description: Blade deflections to the aft Voith unit.

Short_Description: A sailing yacht had engine failure and was towed back to port.
Description: A sailing yacht had engine failure and could not sail so was towed back to port.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel experienced water ingress and was towed to port.
Description: Sailing vessel ran aground and reported water ingress. Assistance was provided in pumping the water out and the vessel was towed to local port. A lifeboat escorted the two vessels back.

Short_Description: A broads cruiser passenger fell overboard and was recovered and treated by ambulance staff.
Description: A passenger on board an inland waterway cruiser fell overboard. They hung onto a boat rope and had a life ring around them. The casualty was recovered by a rescue craft after some time in the water and was landed ashore and was met by ambulance staff. It was confirmed that the casualty had consumed alcohol as it was their birthday.

Short_Description: A yacht grounded during a sailing race and required assistance.
Description: A yacht ran aground during a race and required assistance. The yacht was towed into deeper water and returned to port.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel crewmember sustained a head injury and was taken to hospital.
Description: The crewmember was taking a chain off when the wire broke and hit them on the head resulting in a wound on their head.  The crewmember was airlifted off the vessel and taken ashore, where they were transferred to an ambulance and taken to hospital.

Short_Description: A yacht was struck by a sailing vessel. No injuries were sustained with both vessels sustained minor damage.
Description: A powerboat was at anchor when a sailing vessel collided with them. The harbour patrol attended both vessels and confirmed that all persons onboard were safe and both vessels were able to proceed to their destinations.

Short_Description: A yacht was struck by a sailing vessel. No injuries were sustained with both vessels sustained minor damage.
Description: A powerboat was at anchor when a sailing vessel collided with them. The harbour patrol attended both vessels and confirmed that all persons onboard were safe and both vessels were able to proceed to their destinations.
Damage_Description: Initially said that water was coming in. There was broken glass but vessel was fit to proceed.

Short_Description: A cruise ship crewmember was hit by a genie lift's wheels during a maintenance job and fractured their foot.
Description: Two crewmembers were moving a genie lift towards a deck in a passenger lounge area in order to complete a planned maintenance job.  Once they reached the specific area they were working on, one of the genie lift wheels passed over the right foot of the crewmember's as they were standing in front and guiding the genie lift.

Short_Description: Am motorboat grounded on rocks due to an engine failure and was towed to its berth by a lifeboat.
Description: A motor cruiser with four people on board had engine failure. The crew dropped the anchor but it did not hold and the boat drifted aground onto rocks. They raised the alarm and the lifeboat provided a tow back to the boat's berth. There were no injuries or damage to the vessel.

Short_Description: A cruise ship crewmember slipped on top of the gangway and sprained their knee.
Description: A crewmember was participating in a crew club organized tour and they were exiting from the ship via deck midship portside gangway. Whilst stepping down they slipped their left foot at the top of the gangway and to stop falling they grabbed the railings. They felt a pain in their left knee and they thought it would be alright, so they continued their walking and continued their tour. A few days after they were experiencing pain in their left knee and went to the medical centre and they were diagnosed with a sprained knee.

Short_Description: An offshore supply crewmember stepped from the vessel to the quayside and fell into the water.
Description: Whilst an offshore supply vessel was moored alongside a berth the crewmember slipped and fell into the dock when they were stepping from vessel to the quayside. They were wearing PPE (Personal Protective Equipment) with a lifejacket at the time and were recovered quickly from the water. No injuries were confirmed.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger ferry had a close quarters situation with a sailing yacht.
Description: After departing the harbour, the ro-ro passenger ferry had a sailing yacht alter course placing the yacht in a close-quarters situation with the ro-ro passenger ferry. The ferry had to go full astern to avoid the yacht.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger ferry had a close quarters situation with a sailing yacht.
Description: After departing the harbour, the ro-ro passenger ferry had a sailing yacht alter course placing the yacht in a close-quarters situation with the ro-ro passenger ferry. The ferry had to go full astern to avoid the yacht.

Short_Description: An oil tanker crewmember slipped and fell resulting in a suspected fractured shoulder.
Description: An oil tanker crewmember slipped on a slippery surface and fell resulting in a dislocated shoulder. A lifeboat was tasked to take the casualty to shore from the anchorage. They were taken to hospital for further treatment.

Short_Description: See MAIB investigation report, when available
Description: See MAIB investigation report, when available
Damage_Description: See MAIB investigation report, when available

Short_Description: A container ship crewmember caught their finger in a door.
Description: A container ship crewmember trapped their finger in a door whilst attempting to prevent the door from slamming.  The last section of the finger including the nail was cut off. The ship made its way to port so the crewmember could receive medical care.

Short_Description: A rescue boat capsized whilst on a training exercise. All three persons in the water managed to self-rescue.
Description: Three crew were onboard a rescue boat on training exercise on a river. The boat capsized due to a helm error. All three crew were able to self-rescue to the river bank without injury. In the capsize some equipment including the boat engine was lost but the boat was recovered.
Damage_Description: Some equipment was lost, including the the boat engine.

Short_Description: A tanker's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: A tanker's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. The ladder winnets and rubber steps were in poor repair.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser with a possible fire lost steering and collided with a moored sailing vessel. No major damage or injuries.
Description: A motor cruiser with two crew had a suspected engine fire. The vessel lost steering and collided with a moored sailing vessel. The cruiser was checked and the fault was found to be a burst header tank. The motor cruiser was taken under tow to safety. The sailing vessel was not damaged and there were no injuries.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser with a possible fire lost steering and collided with a moored sailing vessel. No major damage or injuries.
Description: A motor cruiser with two crew had a suspected engine fire. The vessel lost steering and collided with a moored sailing vessel. The cruiser was checked and the fault was found to be a burst header tank. The motor cruiser was taken under tow to safety. The sailing vessel was not damaged and there were no injuries.
Damage_Description: Fault found to to be a burst header tank.

Short_Description: A passenger ro-ro vessel's pilot ladder did not confirm to SOLAS standards.
Description: A passenger ro-ro vessel's pilot ladder did not confirm to SOLAS standards. The step fixtures were loose resulting in the steps becoming misaligned (not horizontal), and the steps rotating when pressure was applied. The ladder's only means of securing was via shackles over the side ropes and the deck pad eyes were covered with oil residue.

Short_Description: A commercial diving vessel had damage to its propeller and required assistance.
Description: A commercial diving vessel had damage to the propeller after hitting something with the propeller. Slight water ingress occurred when the vessel was being towed.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger ship had a fire in the engine room which was extinguished.
Description: A ro-ro passenger vessel had a fire in the lagging over the starboard main engine while making approach to harbour. The fire was extinguished by a portable fire extinguisher within four minutes of being reported. The cause of the fire has been identified as a joint on the lube oil sensor pipework which had worked lose and sprayed oil onto the hot engine.
Damage_Description: Small fire over starboard main engine.

Short_Description: A passenger ship contractor slipped and in attempting to break their fall, injured their hand.
Description: A marine contractor was working in an alleyway close to a cooling room. They were one of a number of contractors in a 'chain' passing black garbage bags of grey galley grease out of the area. At the time they were wearing black wellington boots with good grip. As they turned with the bag of garbage their foot slipped off the deck plate and down towards the bilge. They put their left hand out instinctively to break their fall and this struck a metal pipe bracket causing a deep cut to the left palm below the base of the thumb. The injured party disembarked by a local boat where they were landed to the care of medical facilities ashore.

Short_Description: A SAR vessel's daughter craft capsized whilst on service call.
Description: A SAR (search and rescue) vessel's daughter craft capsized on a beach when being walked to the shore by the crew. No damage or injury.

Short_Description: A jet ski and a yacht had a collision.
Description: A collision occurred between a remotely controlled jet ski and a yacht.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting structural integrity of the ship

Short_Description: A jet ski and a yacht had a collision.
Description: A collision occurred between a remotely controlled jet ski and a yacht.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel started taking on water and requested assistance.
Description: A fishing vessel discovered a leak and started taking on water. The pumps coped at first but assistance from emergency services was then requested as the water level was rising. The vessel made it back to harbour under its own power.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel crewmember was injured by the end weight of the gear and fractured their coccyx.
Description: A fishing vessel crewmember was struck in the back by the weight end of a gear line. The end of the line reached the vessel sooner than expected and the crewmember was not anticipating it being with them so quickly. The crewmember went on to develop pain in their back and pelvis. Initially a medivac by helicopter was requested but due to sea conditions and area of injury, it was decided to take the casualty into harbour and transfer them to give medical assistance there. They were diagnosed with a hairline fracture to their coccyx.

Short_Description: A crewmember received cut to the head after the gangway ladder jumped off the bracket.
Description: A gangway dropped on crewmember's head while being craned ashore using ship's gear. They were taken to hospital for an operation.

Short_Description: A chemical tanker made contact with a jetty.
Description: A chemical tanker was making an approach with a pilot on board when the weather conditions changed very rapidly. They made a misjudgement of direction which resulted in the bulbous bow making contact with the jetty. The jetty had light damage and vessel did not sustain any damage.

Short_Description: A recreational motor vessel crewmember severed their toe.
Description: A recreational motor vessel crewmember severed their toe. A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was deployed to extract the crewmember and transfer them to shore where they were passed into the care of the ambulance crew.

Short_Description: See MAIB investigation report, when available
Description: See MAIB investigation report, when available
Damage_Description: See MAIB investigation report, when available

Short_Description: A vehicle carrier had minor damage after contact whilst berthing.
Description: While berthing, a vehicle carrier had minor damage after contact with the berth. The vessel damaged the shore fendering and a walkway. The vessel itself was punctured above the waterline at the stern. No one was injured and the vessel was able to continue its voyage to its next port for repair.
Damage_Description: Damage to fender and vessel duct tail got holes on the upper section.

Short_Description: An inland waterway passenger vessel lost directional control.
Description: An inland waterway passenger vessel lost directional control on approach to a bridge. The skipper put the engines astern and used the fitted bow thruster to manoeuvre the vessel, narrowly avoiding making contact with the bridge.

Short_Description: A ro-pax vessel crewmember was hit by mooring ropes and injured their wrist.
Description: A ro-pax vessel crewmember was struck in the arm by an over-tensioned line whilst manoeuvring the vessel alongside. The line was on bits on deck and the crewmember tried to slack the weight on it when the rope came under tension and struck the crewmember on their wrist.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier's bow made contact with a tug's fendering.
Description: A bulk carrier was on an approach to a lock with a tug on the bow and  one on the stern. As the vessel started to move ahead to enter the lock, the vessel appeared to be no longer clearing on the west side. The bow thruster, head tug and propulsion all worked to move the vessel to the east with no success. The vessel's headway was reduced to a minimum using the stern tug. The port side of bow made contact with the fendering. There was no damage to the vessel and no damage to the port's infrastructure.

Short_Description: A vehicle carrier's crewmember sustained a burn injury to the face and chest.
Description: A vehicle carrier was berthing when the auxiliary boiler stopped. A crewmember opened the auxiliary boiler burner to access and replace the fuel oil injector. The crewmember sustained partial thickness burns to the face and chest as a result of either flames or hot combustion gas. The crewmember was treated at a shore side facility. The crewmember was not wearing the designated PPE (personal protective equipment) and an internal investigation was carried out.

Short_Description: A passenger ship failed to go astern and collided with a fishing vessel.
Description: The morse engine control failed on a passenger ship resulting in the vessel failing to go astern. Subsequently, the vessel collided with a fishing vessel.

Short_Description: A passenger ship failed to go astern and collided with a fishing vessel.
Description: The morse engine control failed on a passenger ship resulting in the vessel failing to go astern. Subsequently, the vessel collided with a fishing vessel.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser collided with a moored motor cruiser.
Description: A motor cruiser with one person onboard was moored at a public mooring facing upstream. Another motor cruiser was heading downstream, wanting to moor ahead of the moored motor cruiser. The helm realising the vessel wouldn't fit in the space attempted to turn away to port, but didn't have the room to carry out that manoeuvre and the starboard bow collided heavily with moored motor vessel. The moored vessel had minor damage to the bow and the person onboard sustained a knee injury and minor grazing and bruising.
Damage_Description: Portside rubbing strake detached from hull

Short_Description: A motor cruiser collided with a moored motor cruiser.
Description: A motor cruiser with one person onboard was moored at a public mooring facing upstream. Another motor cruiser was heading downstream, wanting to moor ahead of the moored motor cruiser. The helm realising the vessel wouldn't fit in the space attempted to turn away to port, but didn't have the room to carry out that manoeuvre and the starboard bow collided heavily with moored motor vessel. The moored vessel had minor damage to the bow and the person onboard sustained a knee injury and minor grazing and bruising.

Short_Description: A sailing yacht skipper had a head injury after being hit by the boom.
Description: A sailing yacht skipper had a head injury after being hit by the boom. The lone skipper was conscious but bleeding from the head. A harbour vessel assisted the yacht until a search and rescue (SAR) vessel arrived and towed the yacht. Two crew boarded and treated the skipper's injuries and upon arrival the skipper was passed into the care of the ambulance service.

Short_Description: A charter motor cruiser grounded and required a tow.
Description: A vessel grounded, no damage was sustained and it was pulled away to safety by a privately owned vessel. No further assistance from a lifeboat was required and the vessel continued on its passage.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel's wash caused a moored vessel's crewmember minor injuries.
Description: The vessel reduced speed too late and entered a speed restriction area at a cruising speed. The ferry located at the pier was affected by the wake wash.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel's wash caused a moored vessel's crewmember minor injuries.
Description: The vessel reduced speed too late and entered a speed restriction area at a cruising speed. The ferry located at the pier was affected by the wake wash.

Short_Description: A motor vessel had water ingress and required assistance.
Description: A motorboat crew was unsure where the water ingress was coming from and vessel was towed back to port.

Short_Description: A motorboat hit rock at high speed, damaging propulsion and hull. The vessel was towed to safety.
Description: A small motorboat with one person on board hit a rock at high speed damaging its propulsion and the hull. A lifeboat was tasked to assist and the crew used their salvage pump to ease the water ingress while the casualty vessel was towed to safety by another vessel. There were no injuries.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting structural integrity of the ship
Damage_Description: Water ingress and damaged propulsion. ILB used their salvage pump and another vessel towed the vessel to a local slipway to beach the craft.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel ran aground and was towed to safety by a passing vessel.
Description: A sailing vessel, with five crew onboard, ran aground as a result of steering failure. It was towed to safety by a passing vessel.

Short_Description: A RIB was towed after an electrical fire onboard.
Description: Emergency services were tasked to assist a RIB (rigid inflatable boat) with two people on board which had an electrical fire. The casualties were evacuated safely and a lifeboat towed the RIB to the marina where the fire service isolated the battery and deemed the RIB to no longer be a at risk of ignition.

Short_Description: A cruise ship crewmember fell and dislocated their shoulder
Description: A cruise ship crew member dislocated their shoulder when they slipped and fell whilst trying to pull two heavy suitcases where the deck changed from carpet to hard flooring. The crew member also struck their head as they landed. The injured crew member was disembarked and taken to hospital for treatment.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel reported a rope around its propeller and was towed back to port.
Description: A fishing vessel reported a rope around its propeller that it was unable to free. The vessel requested assistance as there were no other vessel nearby. A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was tasked and towed the fishing vessel back to port. Both crew members were wearing lifejackets.

Short_Description: A container ship's aft tow line parted.
Description: Whilst leaving a lock inward bound a cargo vessel's aft backspring parted. There were no injuries as a result of this incident.

Short_Description: A pleasure craft ran aground, was assisted with re-floating and towed to a mooring.
Description: A pleasure craft with one person on board ran aground. A lifeboat assisted the craft to re-float and then towed them clear. The vessel's skipper restarted the engine and was escorted back to their mooring.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel sunk after a rudder failure. All persons were rescued successfully.
Description: A sailing vessel with four people in board had a rudder failure. A lifeboat was tasked to tow the vessel but the casualty vessel sank. All persons were rescued with no reported injuries.
Damage_Description: Rudder failure lead to flooding that could not be controlled even after salvage pump was delivered by lifeboat

Short_Description: A crew transfer vessel had a fire in the port engine.
Description: A crew transfer vessel had an engine fire in the port engine and flames were seen on CCTV (Closed Circuit Television). The fire flaps were closed and the suppressions were released. The vessel managed to make it into port unassisted where the local fire brigade took over. They decided to leave the engine hatch secure and return the following morning to check for any further damage. The crew stayed in a hotel overnight as a  precaution. This was a result of an overheated bearing on the port engine.

Short_Description: Two container ships had a close quarters situation
Description: A container ship (1) was manoeuvring towards its intended anchor position. Another container ship (2) had been anchored but had just heaved anchor and was informed that vessel (1) was manoeuvring towards the anchor position in the deep water anchorage. A passing arrangement was made that container ship (2) would pass astern of container ship (1). Several minutes later container ship (2) had ignored the arrangement and crossed ahead of container ship (1) at close range. As a result, this action caused container ship (1) to put the engine full astern and rudder hard to starboard.

Short_Description: Two container ships had a close quarters situation
Description: A container ship (1) was manoeuvring towards its intended anchor position. Another container ship (2) had been anchored but had just heaved anchor and was informed that vessel (1) was manoeuvring towards the anchor position in the deep water anchorage. A passing arrangement was made that container ship (2) would pass astern of container ship (1). Several minutes later container ship (2) had ignored the arrangement and crossed ahead of container ship (1) at close range. As a result, this action caused container ship (1) to put the engine full astern and rudder hard to starboard.

Short_Description: A service vessel had a spill of marine gas oil on deck
Description: A service vessel had a spill of marine gas oil (MGO) on the deck. The approximate amount was less than five litres with a small amount entering the water and a sheen seen on the surface. The pollution was left to disperse naturally.

Short_Description: A yacht had a fire and grounded.
Description: A yacht had a fire in engine room and subsequently grounded. The vessel managed to re-float with the next tide.

Short_Description: A SAR vessel struck a submerged rock during a rescue operation.
Description: A SAR (search and rescue) vessel made contact with a submerged rock during a rescue operation. There was slight damage to the propeller but the vessel was able to continue unaffected.

Short_Description: A Ro-Ro vessel crewmember sustained a head injury.
Description: Three crew members were tasked with preparing the mooring ropes for the vessel's arrival at the port the following day. One crewmember was not in direct view of the other two personnel. It was reported by the two crew that they found the other crewmember unconscious on the deck with an injury on their head. First aid was administered and the injured crewmember was shifted to the ships hospital. The crewmember was evacuated ashore to hospital.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel damaged their propeller blades after briefly grounding.
Description: A SAR (search and rescue)  vessel was proceeding out of a small  harbour. There was a thud heard from underneath the vessel and the starboard propeller developed a vibration. The mechanic went below to assess and checked all was watertight. The vessel made slow passage back to base and further checks were made alongside. It was found several blades were bent and misshaped on the starboard propeller.  The safe route into and out of the harbour was reviewed as result of grounding.

Short_Description: A workboat's lifting gear parted causing the block to swing and go overboard. There were no injuries.
Description: A workboat's crew were removing a piece of equipment using the vessel's crane. The lifting gear had been attached to the platform's lifting points. On taking the weight with the crane, the equipment appeared not to move, so the crane operator continued to lift. The lifting gear parted causing the block to swing in the direction of the crew who were required to dodge the fast swinging hook, which then flew overboard.
Damage_Description: Lifting gear parted. No other damage to the vessel.

Short_Description: Two fishing vessels had a near-miss collision.
Description: The fishing vessel was hauling pots when another fishing vessel was noticed and was coming at them at full speed with no persons seen in the wheelhouse. The vessel managed to turn away in time before a potential collision could happen.

Short_Description: Two fishing vessels had a near-miss collision.
Description: The fishing vessel was hauling pots when another fishing vessel was noticed and was coming at them at full speed with no persons seen in the wheelhouse. The vessel managed to turn away in time before a potential collision could happen.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel had a fire onboard.
Description: A sailing vessel had a small fire onboard. The fire was contained and the vessel was assisted to a place of safety.

Short_Description: A research vessel had water ingress on its arrival at a port
Description: A research vessel with a pilot onboard reported that there was water ingress, the vessel continued into port where it berthed. Divers were deployed to inspect for damage, the survey discovered a crack around nine centimetres in size. The divers put a temporary patch over the area with a through bolt and tightened it from the inside of the bilge well. The bilge well was blanked off as an extra precaution and the class society allowed the vessel to continue operation and affect permanent repairs in dry dock.

Short_Description: A chemical tanker crewmember sustained an injury to their hand.
Description: A tanker crewmember caught their finger on a door resulting in an open fracture where the top of the finger was partially amputated. The crewmember was medevac'd to hospital for assessment and treatment.

Short_Description: A broads cruiser crewmember fell and injured their head.
Description: A broads cruiser crewmember fell onboard resulting in a 7.6cm laceration to their head. The crewmember was removed from the vessel and taken to hospital.

Short_Description: A sailing yacht grounded at a river entrance.
Description: A sailing yacht was leaving a river when it turned too early and grounded on a mud bank. The lone skipper onboard waited for the flood tide to re-float the vessel. No injuries to crew or damage to vessel were reported.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel reported a coolant leak causing smoke and loss of power.
Description: A sailing vessel reported a coolant leak causing smoke and loss of power.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger ferry crewmember had a back injury.
Description: A crewmember on ro-ro passenger ferry injured their back when bending down to secure a vehicle to the deck. Upon standing up again they felt their back go into spasm and it severely restricted in their movement. They ceased work immediately and were sent home to seek medical advice.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel damaged a sponson whilst on exercise
Description: A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was undertaking a familiarisation exercise with crew when the vessel came alongside the jetty for crew change. The helm left the vessel while waiting for the crew. Once everyone was onboard, the vessel  was taken away from the jetty and during this it became apparent that the front sponson had deflated. The helm then made the decision to recover the boat to its carriage for examination and repair. The repair was effected and the vessel returned to service within 36 hours.
Damage_Description: Puncture to port side forward sponson.

Short_Description: A cruise ship damaged an anchor whilst recovering it.
Description: A cruise ship was recovering its starboard anchor in order to proceed to sea. An increased gust of wind caused the vessel to yaw off the starboard anchor. At this point, with the brake on and the anchor in gear it walked back approximately three metres. This happened again and some smoke was sighted from the windlass motor casing. The anchor was able to be recovered to one shackle on deck where the windlass cut out and would not heave any further. Further investigation and fault finding then allowed heaving to re-commence. The anchor was sighted however only the shank was recovered and the flukes were missing.

Short_Description: A leisure fishing vessel ran aground on a mudbank and required assistance due to listing.
Description: A leisure vessel ran aground on a mudbank. Two of the four crew were rescued by a hovercraft, the other two remained onboard until the vessel refloated.

Short_Description: A passenger on a ro-ro passenger vessel tripped on a toilet door threshold, fracturing their pelvic bone in the fall.
Description: A passenger on board a ro-ro passenger vessel tripped over the toilet door threshold on exiting. First aid was administered at the time and the passenger was advised to seek further assistance if the pain did not cease. The passenger completed their holiday and returned home, but were still in pain. The casualty visited a hospital where a CT scan and x-ray revealed a fracture in the lower pelvic bone.

Short_Description: A survey vessel had a lifting equipment failure while lifting a load.
Description: A survey vessel's lifting equipment failed with a suspended load. It is believed from the crew that the pin that secured the catch plate in place released as on inspection the pin was a loose fit and rusty. With the pin released and the securing plate above able to move this would have allowed the tether to move more in the block and allow the block to become twisted, which would have placed strain on the mechanism and block itself. There was no damage to vessel or injuries to crew.

Description: See MAIB investigation report, when available
