Description: Container vessel pilot  ladder snapped on one side when the pilot initially stood on it,  then rope appeared rotten from the inside out, however the pilot was uninjured, and another ladder was rigged instead.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger vessel reported loss of propulsion due to a detached piston crown.
Description: A ro-ro passenger vessel reported loss of propulsion due to a detached piston crown. The piston crown detached from piston skirt causing major internal damage to the engine.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship

Short_Description: Duplicate of 4039/2021
Description: Duplicate of 4039/2021

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had an engine fire resulting in a tow from a sailing  vessel.
Description: A fishing vessel had an electrical battery fire and was towed to shore by a sailing vessel.

Short_Description: A passenger vessel's boarding ramp fell due to the jet water of another vessel. One passenger was on the ramp at the time but was uninjured.
Description: A passenger on the boarding ramp of a passenger vessel fell and landed on the vessel with no injuries. This was because the passenger vessel's boarding ramp shifted and fell between the pier and the vessel but was held onto the quay by chains. This was caused by another passenger vessel departing having been moored directly astern and the resultant jet of water caused the passenger vessel to surge ahead on its single spring line.

Short_Description: A passenger vessel's boarding ramp fell due to the jet water of another vessel. One passenger was on the ramp at the time but was uninjured.
Description: A passenger on the boarding ramp of a passenger vessel fell and landed on the vessel with no injuries. This was because the passenger vessel's boarding ramp shifted and fell between the pier and the vessel but was held onto the quay by chains. This was caused by another passenger vessel departing having been moored directly astern and the resultant jet of water caused the passenger vessel to surge ahead on its single spring line.

Short_Description: A tug grounded.
Description: A tug grounded in mud during low tide and re-floated on the rising tide. The channel was dredged to prevent future groundings.

Short_Description: A supply vessel made contact with an oil rig platform.
Description: A supply vessel working alongside at oil installation decided to pull off due to poor weather and came around the other to the other side of the instillation. Power failure caused the shutdown of two thrusters and the vessel came into contact with the platform. There was superficial damage to the installation. No injuries were reported. Damage was sustained to the main mast and navigational equipment including X Band Radar, S Band Radar, Sat C, Wind Sensors and DGPS. The ship returned to port for repair. The propulsion control system load reduction software defaulted to manual from auto due to internal battery depletion. The load reduction in the developing weather conditions close to the platform when the propulsion was operating at 100% did not occur causing a generator under-frequency issue  and shutdown of the generator.
Damage_Description: Superficial damage to the instillation, but no description of damage to vessel.

Short_Description: A passenger ro-ro vessel had watertight door failure.
Description: A crewmember of a ro-ro ferry was shaken but uninjured when a hydraulically operated watertight door was moving to the open position, then rapidly and unexpectedly moved to the closed position.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel reported engine issues and requested assistance, before managing to restart.
Description: Fishing vessel reported engine issues and requested assistance. The vessel managed to restart engine and made its own way into port.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel reported leaking battery fumes and the crew were recovered off the vessel by a lifeboat.
Description: Two fishing vessel crew members were overcome with battery fumes and were recovered by a lifeboat.

Short_Description: A yacht had engine failure and was towed back to port.
Description: A sailing yacht had engine failure and was towed back to port by a lifeboat.

Short_Description: A close quarters situation occurred between two passenger vessels.
Description: A close quarters situation occurred between two passenger vessels.

Short_Description: A close quarters situation occurred between two passenger vessels.
Description: A close quarters situation occurred between two passenger vessels.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. The ship's deck boarding area was not adequately lit. - A tripping line was fitted to the bottom of the ladder, or was rigged not in accordance with IMO Resolution A.1045(27) 2.1.5.

Short_Description: A passenger ship passenger fell down some stairs and sustained a head injury.
Description: A passenger onboard a cruise ship which was at anchor fell down the last few steps of a staircase sustaining facial injuries. A lifeboat transferred the casualty ashore where they received six stitches in hospital to the forehead. They returned to the vessel the same day and continued their cruise.

Short_Description: An inflatable dingy crewmember was found deceased after a collision with a jet ski.
Description: An inflatable dingy crewmember was found deceased after a collision with a jet ski.

Short_Description: An inflatable dingy crewmember was found deceased after a collision with a jet ski.
Description: An inflatable dingy crewmember was found deceased after a collision with a jet ski.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel reported engine issues and was towed back by another vessel.
Description: A fishing vessel reported engine issues and was towed back by another vessel.

Short_Description: A ro-pax vessel experienced a generator failure.
Description: A ro-pax vessel left a dock after a repairs. The vessel was powered by four Voith units which were powered by two generators. Whilst outbound one of the generators failed, but the vessel could still proceed on half power. Shortly after that, the two forward propulsion units failed. The remainder of the voyage was done using two Voith units on half power.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had a small fire that was extinguished.
Description: A fishing vessel was at sea when a smell of smoke was detected followed by smoke coming from the engine room air intake. Upon inspection, the morse control cables were found to be on fire, due to an electrical short circuit. The engines were stopped and electrical systems isolated. The fire was extinguished by a damping down process to minimise further damage to vessel. The vessel was towed back to port by another fishing vessel. There were no injuries to crew and no pollution reported.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel crewmember sustained an injury to a tendon in their hand.
Description: A sailing catamaran departed on a trans-ocean trip when a crewmember cut a tendon in their hand two days into the voyage. The vessel turned back to port while a nurse, who was onboard, treated the injury.

Short_Description: A cruise ship crewmember fell from scaffolding in the engine room and was airlifted to hospital.
Description: A cruise ship crewmember was in the engine room. CCTV (closed circuit television) showed the crewmember climbed to the top of some scaffolding whilst not wearing a safety harness. The crewmember was airlifted to hospital.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel made contact with rocks and a lifeboat assisted it back to the marina.
Description: A sailing vessel made contact with rocks and a lifeboat assisted it back to the marina.

Short_Description: A chartered sailing vessel grounded experiencing minor damage to the keel and the rudder.
Description: A chartered sailing vessel grounded as they left a harbour as the two crew were unfamiliar with the harbour. They refloated and returned to base where the yacht was later lifted and surveyed. There was no damage to hull or interior keel support structure.
Damage_Description: Some abrasion to the keel.  Minor damage to the trailing edge of the rudder.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser experienced a fire.
Description: A motor cruiser with one person on board experienced a fire on board. The single crewmember self-recovered to shore and required hospitalisation. The fire service attended and extinguished the fire, but the boat sustained significant damage.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship

Short_Description: A cruise ship crewmember was injured by a winch handle when recovering a fast rescue craft.
Description: A cruise ship crewmember was putting the starboard FRC (Fast Rescue Craft) into its storage position, using a windlass crank handle. The windlass unexpectedly spun around at a high speed, hitting the crewmember on their right hand causing a distal radius fracture.

Short_Description: A yacht experienced propulsion failure and was towed.
Description: A yacht experienced propulsion failure and was towed to port by lifeboat.

Short_Description: A container ship broke an anchor winch.
Description: A container vessel broke an anchor winch whilst heaving up at the anchorage.

Short_Description: A tanker reported a close quarter's situation with a passenger ro-ro vessel.
Description: A tanker reported a close quarter's situation with a passenger ro-ro vessel. The passenger ro-ro vessel reportedly did not alter course to avoid collision.

Short_Description: A tanker reported a close quarter's situation with a passenger ro-ro vessel.
Description: A tanker reported a close quarter's situation with a passenger ro-ro vessel. The passenger ro-ro vessel reportedly did not alter course to avoid collision.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigger as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. The rigging of the ladder was such that the bottom spreader was hard against the hand rail stanchions. The ladder was secured with shackles (further inboard) over the ropes. There was no tension at all inboard of the spreader towards the shackles. The rigging was adjusted prior to embarkation. The matter was discussed with the Captain. The Captain stated that normally the ladder is rigged with the spreader on the outboard side and shackles securing the ladder.

Short_Description: A yacht grounded on shingle bank and was towed off by a fishing vessel.
Description: A yacht grounded on a shingle bank and was towed by a fishing vessel off the bank. No damage was sustained.

Short_Description: A weighted heaving line was used in berthing operations.
Description: A nut and compacted sand was used as part of a heaving line, during berthing operations.

Short_Description: A hire cruiser passenger fell and injured their leg. They were assessed by paramedics and remained on the vessel.
Description: An occupant of a hire cruiser fell on board whilst the vessel was alongside. Emergency services assisted with extracting the casualty. The assessment revealed the casualty may have torn something in their leg and the ambulance crew were happy to leave the casualty on the vessel resting for the rest of them holiday.

Short_Description: A vessel's pilot ladder construction and winch reel ladder did not meet SOLAS requirements.
Description: A vessel's pilot ladder construction did not meet current SOLAS standards and the ladder was not rigged as per current SOLAS regulations. The winch reel ladder arrangement was not secured at deck level, lugs were on the coaming round adjacent to the side ropes and the ladder went straight to the reel.

Short_Description: A crude oil tanker's pilot lost their footing on a ladder whilst boarding.
Description: A pilot was boarding a crude oil tanker. As the pilot climbed the ladder the pilot launch dropped back. The ladder caught on the fendering and was also pulled aft preventing the pilot getting a footing on the steps. The ladder returned to position and pilot regained their footing and boarded the vessel.

Short_Description: A lifeboat hit a rock during a rescue operation.
Description: A lifeboat was tasked on a shoreline search for missing paddle boarders.  Conditions were marginal for paddle boarding so there was concern for the boarders’ welfare.  The lifeboat was launched and proceeded to the first line of submerged rocks that were visible amongst the breaking waves. Just on the plane the crew suddenly felt a sudden slowing of the lifeboat which forced the helm backwards who managed to stay in the boat using the foot straps. At first they believed the propeller had become fouled in heavy weed, however on closer inspection it became apparent that they had struck a sharp edge, most likely a rock, with the sponson which had consequently ripped.

Short_Description: A charter motor cruiser lost all steering and was towed to by a lifeboat.
Description: A charter motor cruiser with three people on board lost all steering following a hydraulic failure. A pan pan was issued as the vessel drifted and the casualty vessel was towed by a lifeboat to harbour.

Short_Description: A cruise ship crewmember injured their shoulder whilst preparing a heaving line.
Description: A cruise ship crewmember injured their shoulder whilst preparing a heaving line on the mooring deck. The casualty tripped over a horizontal guide roller as they were stepping backwards. The medical diagnosis was a muscle strain of the left shoulder and the crewmember was signed off work for four days.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel made contact with a passenger ship during bunker operations.
Description: A bunker barge was coming alongside a ferry to complete bunkering operations. Once the bunker barge was alongside it swung towards it, colliding in the aft section and damaging a lifeboat davit.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel made contact with a passenger ship during bunker operations.
Description: A bunker barge was coming alongside a ferry to complete bunkering operations. Once the bunker barge was alongside it swung towards it, colliding in the aft section and damaging a lifeboat davit.
Damage_Description: The contact was made on the port aft corner of the products tanker. The outboard supporting FFLB davit leg. It looks as if the davit leg has flexed forward causing the flange and flange bolts to distort before popping back into position

Short_Description: A fishing vessel sustained a damaged gearbox
Description: A fishing vessel had problems with the propulsion gearbox. After an unsuccessful attempt to repair the gearbox at sea, it was towed to a port and berthed there.

Short_Description: A tug vessel crewmember cut their hand whilst preparing a burger.
Description: A crewmember on a tug cut their hand with a knife whilst splitting frozen burgers. The motion of the vessel is believed to have contributed to the accident. The knife cut through the thumb, tendon and nerve. The crewmember was taken to hospital for treatment.

Short_Description: A RIB run aground and required assistance.
Description: A RIB (rigid inflatable boat) ran aground and required assistance. The people on board were taken ashore.  Only one person was wearing a lifejacket.

Short_Description: A yacht crewmember fell overboard.
Description: A crewmember tripped and fell into water from their vessel. They were recovered and taken to hospital.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel grounded causing damage to the outboard engine gearbox.
Description: A small lifeboat was utilised as a boarding boat for another search and rescue vessel. The crew were returning from a routine exercise and, due to the low tide, grounded causing damage to the outboard engine gearbox. No persons were injured.
Damage_Description: Damage to the outboard engine gearbox.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. The ladder was secured by a bar. The vessel's agreed to use ropes to secure pilot ladder at departure. A deck tongue was present but not used to secure the ladder.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. Upon disembarkation, the pilot found out the vessel was using a trapdoor arrangement.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger ferry had a near miss collision with a workboat.
Description: A ferry departed its terminal within a busy harbour. A workboat towing two inflatable race marker buoys was passing the port beam, paralleling the ferry's course at a safe distance. The lookout reported that the workboat had altered course and speed and was close on the port bow and a risk of collision was deemed to exist. The person driving the workboat had their back to the ferry and seemed unaware of the ferry's presence, so a long blast on the ship's whistle was sounded to alert them. Avoiding action was taken by operating engines astern to take all way off and altering to starboard as far as possible within confines of the channel. On hearing the whistle, the workboat abruptly altered to port and increased speed to get out of the way.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger ferry had a near miss collision with a workboat.
Description: A ferry departed its terminal within a busy harbour. A workboat towing two inflatable race marker buoys was passing the port beam, paralleling the ferry's course at a safe distance. The lookout reported that the workboat had altered course and speed and was close on the port bow and a risk of collision was deemed to exist. The person driving the workboat had their back to the ferry and seemed unaware of the ferry's presence, so a long blast on the ship's whistle was sounded to alert them. Avoiding action was taken by operating engines astern to take all way off and altering to starboard as far as possible within confines of the channel. On hearing the whistle, the workboat abruptly altered to port and increased speed to get out of the way.

Short_Description: A person fell overboard from the cockpit after getting hit by the boom and had a minor cut to their eye.
Description: A person fell overboard from their vessel's cockpit whilst putting out fenders when the boom came across and hit them. The lanyard was worn at the time with a lifejacket, the other crewmember released the lanyard. The authorities were contacted and a fishing vessel managed to assist with picking up the casualty from the water. The casualty was taken by lifeboat first, then transferred to an ambulance and taken to hospital. They had a cut to their head.

Short_Description: A search and rescue craft made contact with an infrastructure and punctured a sponson.
Description: A search and rescue craft was alongside. Whilst alongside, the inflatable sponson of the craft was punctured by a nail protruding from the area the vessel was moored. The craft was able to make its way back to base and repairs were carried out on the puncture.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting structural integrity of the ship

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS.

Short_Description: A chemical tanker's pilot ladder rigging did not conform with SOLAS.
Description: A chemical tanker's pilot ladder rigging did not conform with SOLAS.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser had an electrical issue and was towed back to harbour.
Description: A motor cruiser had an electrical issue and was towed back to harbour.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel had a fire in the engine room that was contained.
Description: A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was on a routine training exercise. Mid-exercise a fire was detected in the lagging surrounding the port turbocharger. The fire was contained whilst at sea without further spread. The lagging was able to be removed and the vessel continued on passage back to harbour without further incident or the need for assistance. There were no injuries and, other than to the lagging, no damage to the vessel.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel grounded and was pulled off the rocks by a lifeboat and then escorted to harbour.
Description: A fishing vessel grounded on transit and a lifeboat was tasked to pull the vessel off the rocks. The casualty vessel then was escorted, under its own power, back to the harbour where the vessel was inspected and shown to have slight damage to the stem but was watertight and fit to proceed to the slip in another port.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had steering failure resulting in a grounding and towage back to port.
Description: A fishing vessel experienced steering failure as it approached a port. The vessel veered away from the port entrance and grounded on the breakwater. The vessel was towed free by the search and rescue services.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel made contact with the quayside.
Description: A general cargo vessel made contact with the quayside.

Short_Description: A trailer collided with a passenger bus on the vehicle deck of a ro-ro passenger vessel
Description: A ro-ro passenger vessel was in the process of unloading the cargo deck when a tug driver pulling a trailer collided with a passenger bus that was parked on the main deck. The bus sustained body dents and damage to the rear window but no persons were injured.
Damage_Description: The bus had body dents and damage to the rear window.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel crewmember cut themself with a knife.
Description: A fishing vessel crewmember accidentally cut and punctured their wrist with a knife. First aid was provided on board to stem the bleeding. The fishing vessel headed back to port and the crewmember was taken to hospital for treatment.

Short_Description: A dredger made contact with the quay edge.
Description: The vessel was dredging in the yacht basin entrance. The vessel was positioned across the outer bridge channel with its stern fendering in contact with the inner north. As the tide decreased and the vessel draft increased, the vessels fender belt caught on the quay edge causing some damage to concrete capping.

Short_Description: A sailing dinghy student fell overboard.
Description: A student on dinghy instructor's course fell overboard. As they recovered themself over the transom of the dinghy they prevent the helmsperson from steering and the boat gybed twice. The casualty lay on the floor of the boat complaining of back and neck pain. They were evacuated ashore to a waiting ambulance where a head injury was suspected but they had not been hit on the head or fallen unconscious. They were taken to hospital for checks and it was thought a pre-existing injury was aggravated during the incident. They returned to the sailing centre and continued the course the next day.

Short_Description: A sail training vessel fouled its propeller resulting in ingress of water.
Description: A sailing training vessel's crew were retrieving the cruising chute while running the engine in ahead. A sheet went over the side and was caught by the propeller. The engine stalled and could not be restarted. The shaft appears to have been pulled aft, shearing the gearbox coupling and the shaft seal. The vessel took on a small amount of water through the shaft seal following the incident. The yacht sailed into harbour and picked up a mooring buoy. A workboat towed the vessel into a marina so that it could be lifted out of the water the following day.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting structural integrity of the ship
Damage_Description: A rope was wrapped around the propeller, stalling the engine. The shaft appears to have been pulled aft, shearing the gearbox coupling and the shaft seal. The cutlass bearing has worn where the rope was pulled into it and the ‘P’ bracket has cracks visible in the anti-foul paint around it’s base. The vessel was taking on a small amount of water through the shaft seal following the incident.

Short_Description: A yacht fouled its propeller on a mooring buoy and was recovered by a lifeboat.
Description: A yacht fouled its propeller on a mooring buoy and a lifeboat cleared the line and recovered the vessel to the harbour.

Short_Description: A motorboat had propulsion failure and required a tow.
Description: A motorboat with four people on board had propulsion failure and was towed back to port.

Short_Description: A container vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A container vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. The loose ladder was rigged close to the accommodation ladder. Meaning, one couldn't grip the side rope as the accommodation ladder was covering the side rope. The platform at the bottom was not flat. The accommodation ladder was not secured tight against the ship's hull.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger ferry hit a fender on arrival to port.
Description: A ro-ro passenger ferry was approaching a berth. The crew applied transverse thrust to bring the vessel alongside but the vessel did not respond to the joystick order. The crew then set the joystick to full astern and tried to thrust to reduce the speed of approach to the fenders. The vessel struck the berth. There were two minor injures and damage to the forward prow of the vessel and the linkspan.

Short_Description: A sailing yacht had water ingress and lost its rudder.
Description: A recreational sailing yacht was taking on water as well as having lost their rudder. The lifeboat service attended and the lifeboat towed the vessel back to the harbour.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder was not rigged to SOLAS regulations. The ladder was secured by the spreader across the railings. Only one crew member on deck and they did not understand the problem.

Short_Description: A search and rescue vessel crewmember had an injury after the vessel came off a wave.
Description: A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was on service when the vessel was hit by a larger than average wave. As the vessel landed a crewmember felt a sharp pain through their right leg when their right foot made contact with the foot rest after the seat suspension compressed and bottomed out. The crewmember sustained a minor injury to their right hip and stood down from service to recover from the injury.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser passenger fell and broke their ankle and were assisted by ambulance staff.
Description: A passenger on a motor cruiser fell and broke their ankle whilst alongside. The casualty was taken into the care of the ambulance staff.

Short_Description: A passenger vessel had engine failure and was towed back to shore.
Description: A passenger tour vessel had engine failure mid-trip with twelve passengers on board, all wearing life jackets. The twelve passengers were transferred to another vessel and taken to shore. The one crewmember remained on board and helped as the vessel was towed back to port by a lifeboat.

Short_Description: A chartered motor cruiser hit rocks after loosing steerage, damaging the propellers.
Description: A charter motor yacht hit rocks after loosing steering due to a hydraulic failure. The passengers were taken ashore by another vessel after the vessel was anchored. There were no injuries and when the boat was lifted out of the water it was found the propellers were damaged and the hull had had some scratches to the antifouling.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship

Short_Description: A lighthouse tender vessel's pin sheered from a brake plate.
Description: On board a lighthouse tender, following a report of a grinding noise coming from the main speed crane topping motor, two crew members were tasked to investigate. They discovered the source of the problem. A pin had sheered from the brake plate causing it to rub. With the crane still in the raised position, the crew started to dismantle the topping gear before consulting any risk assessment or obtaining a permit to work. The shaft then began to turn without the brake in position. One crewmember was able to hold a spanner on a strong back to stop the shaft turning. A recovery plan was then put in place to safely lower the derrick into its cradle so that the repair work could be completed. The crew had become task focused and had not stopped to consider the risks of what they were doing.

Short_Description: A crew transfer vessel made contact with a wind turbine.
Description: Crew member of a crew transfer vessel (CTW) had decided to split a watch and a comprehensive handover was conducted to the crewmember coming onto the watch. The crewmember on watch had fallen asleep in the wheelhouse and was no longer keeping watch. The vessel was on a slow passage to the windfarm area when it collided with a wind turbine. A visual inspection was carried out by another CTW where minor damage to the hull was noted but there were no pollution and no injuries to crew. When the vessel returned to port a technical assessment of the vessel was carried out.
Damage_Description: Minor outer hull damage, no breach of hull integrity.

Short_Description: A commercial RIB crewmember went overboard.
Description: During a training exercise a RIB (rigid inflatable boat) transited beneath a pier. During this transit, contact was made with the underside of a pipe rack hanging below the pier.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser ran aground due to the anchor dragging.
Description: A motor cruiser had had engine failure, the lone skipper dropped an anchor but it was not holding. The skipper tried to anchor again but lost the anchor, the vessel drifted and grounded on rocks on an ebb tide. A search and rescue vessel was tasked but stood down as the vessel had grounded. The skipper was able to get off the vessel and returned later once the vessel was re-floated on the flood tide. No damage to vessel was reported.

Short_Description: A yacht broke down and started taking on water.
Description: A yacht broke down and started taking on water. The vessel required assistance back to port.

Short_Description: A crew transfer vessel lost propulsion whilst berthing resulting in damage.
Description: A crew transfer vessel experienced a failure of control of its jet propulsion whilst berthing. The vessel impacted heavily with a vertical timber fender, breaking the fender in two and removing the fender top bracket. No persons were injured, but the vessel holed above the starboard bow fendering.
Damage_Description: The starboard forward bulwark was holed.

Short_Description: A cruise ship had a fire in the galley.
Description: A cruise ship had a fire in the galley when a tray with bacon on it caught alight. The galley crew tried to remove the tray but were unable to because of the heat which had warped the tray so that it got stuck on the grills of the shelf.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier made contact with a crane on the quay side.
Description: As a bulk carrier departed the berth, the port quarter made contact with a shore crane causing damage to crane handrails.
Damage_Description: No damage to vessel, minor damage to shore equipment.

Short_Description: A Ro-Ro cargo vessel had engine failure to one engine.
Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel had engine failure to the port engine whilst on passage. The vessel made its way into port on the starboard engine with two tugs standing by. An electrical problem was identified as the issue and rectified swiftly on arrival.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier pilot ladder rigging didn't conform to SOLAS.
Description: A bulk carrier pilot ladder rigging didn't conform to SOLAS. . The mid way ladder lashings came off as I was half way up - the climb was a combination arrangement approx. 7-8m to the accommodation ladder. 2. Electrical tape was used all over instead of whip

Short_Description: A motor cruiser had engine failure and was towed back to port.
Description: A motor cruiser had engine failure and was drifting towards rocks so was towed by the local lifeboat service.

Short_Description: An oil tanker lost electrical power whilst manoeuvring in port.
Description: An oil tanker was waiting to berth alongside when the vessel experienced a momentary blackout. Emergency power restored power to systems on the bridge however the engine control, revs and pitch were acting erratically. The decision was taken to abort the berthing where originally intended and proceed to a layby berth. The bow thruster was working normally, so the vessel later proceeded at slow speed to its intended berth, assisted by a tug.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.  A tripping line was fitted to the bottom of the ladder, or was rigged not in accordance with IMO Resolution A.1045(27) 2.1.5. No ID on ladder. No certification Loose step securing.  The ladder was secured with shackles over the side ropes.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel lost propulsion and was in danger of being washed up on rocks
Description: A sailing vessel experienced propulsion failure and was in danger of being washed up on rocks. In an attempt to assist, a workboat from the harbour came out but was unable to carry out an effective rescue and at one point made light contact with the casualty vessel. No damage or injuries were sustained. The sailing vessel was taken under tow by a lifeboat and was towed to safety.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged a per SOLAS regulations. The life saving appliances were incorrect. There was no heaving line.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger vessel's fuel filter ruptured which caused an emergency generator shutdown resulting in a blackout.
Description: A ro-ro passenger vessel was alongside with its emergency generator running when it suddenly shut down causing the ship to blackout. A smoke detector also activated in the emergency generator room. Fire fighting precautions were taken and the shore fire service was called. On entry to the space it was found the fuel filter had ruptured spilling 336 litres of fuel into the space. The fuel filter had lost its integrity, but fortunately the fuel spill was contained within the compartment.

Short_Description: A tug crew member fell overboard but was rescued
Description: A tug was manoeuvring a barge alongside another barge. As the two barges came together, As a crew member on the towed barge went to put ropes on the other barge, it moved away causing the crew member to loose their balance and fall in the water. The crew member's lifejacket inflated and they were able to hold onto a mooring line. Crew onboard were able to recover the crew member from the water. A man overboard alert had been issued and a search and rescue (SAR) vessel arrived on scene. The SAR crew assessed the crew member, once ashore they were passed into the care of the ambulance service.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel sent a dangerous heaving line ashore.
Description: A general cargo vessel sent a heaving line ashore with a metal hook on the end during berthing operations.

Short_Description: A yacht had a fuel line rupture and was towed back to port.
Description: A search and rescue vessel was tasked to assist a sailing yacht which had a rupture fuel line. They were towed back to port.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel lost steering and required a tow.
Description: A small fishing vessel lost steering and required a tow back into harbour.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel had an engine failure and was towed by a lifeboat.
Description: A sailing vessel with five people on board had engine failure in a river and deployed its anchor. The vessel was towed clear of danger by a lifeboat. No injuries or damage were sustained to the yacht.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. The bottom two rubber steps cracked around the holes that the side ropes pass through.

Short_Description: A chartered angling vessel had a gearbox failure and was escorted to harbour by a lifeboat.
Description: A charter angling fishing vessel with twelve people on board had a gearbox malfunction and was escorted back to harbour by a lifeboat that happened to be on a training exercise nearby.

Short_Description: An inland waterway vessel crewmember climbed a ladder and dislocated their shoulder.
Description: A crewmember was tasked to climb a ladder on the bow of the vessel, as they reached the top step they needed to step over a rail. They had their feet on the ladder, one hand on the rail at the bow and another crewmember then gave them a hand for support as they stepped over the rail. There was a slight pulling effect and at this point their shoulder dislocated. They were taken to hospital and were also found to have a history of several dislocations of the same shoulder.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS.
Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS. The ladder was secured by several turns of light line rather than equivalent strength rope to the side ropes. The accommodation ladder was not secured to hull.

Short_Description: A cruise ship used the incorrect shell door for pilot embarkation.
Description: On arrival, the wrong pilot embarkation shell door was used. It was not the agreed shell door that does not pose a risk to the pilot launch.

Short_Description: A service vessel crewmember twisted awkwardly sustaining lower back pain.
Description: The vessel was alongside when a crewmember was checking some equipment in the bow thruster space when they twisted awkwardly resulting in a back injury.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel had engine failure several times in a dock.
Description: On arrival in port while proceeding stern first from a lock, a cargo vessel had engine failure several times. The pilot decided to drop anchor and await for further assistance as they did not believe that it was prudent to attempt to pass through a narrow section of the dock with only one tug assisting.

Short_Description: A workboat experienced a fire in the starboard engine that self extinguished.
Description: A workboat was on an outbound passage when a fire alarm sounded on the bridge for the engine room. On investigation there was no smoke at the engine room door. On proceeding into the engine space there was light smoke and small flickering flames coming from behind the exhaust heat shield on the starboard engine. A report was made to the bridge and the starboard engine stopped. The flames self extinguished and the smoke dissipated. A crewmember continued to monitor the starboard engine until the vessel arrived in port. An investigation was carried out, the pipe and exhaust lagging was replaced. On investigation it was discovered the lube oil pipe had split.

Short_Description: A vessel's crewmember dislocated their knee when jumping onto a pontoon next to a fuel barge.
Description: A crewmember of a vessel jumped onto a pontoon next to a fuel barge and dislocated their knee and were taken to hospital.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel grounded and refloated successfully.
Description: A fishing vessel had a grounding, all four crew members were taken off by another fishing vessel and the vessel managed to re-float successfully without any damage sustained or further assistance required.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel went aground on the approach to the berth.
Description: During the final approach to the berth, a general cargo vessel grounded on the starboard side. This was reported to be due to debris/mud accumulation on the seabed close to the quay.

Short_Description: A commercial barge ran aground and intended to re-float at high tide.
Description: A commercial barge ran aground and re-floated at high tide. There was no damage.

Short_Description: A hopper dredger was making an approach to a lock when the vessel landed heavily at the entrance causing damage to fenders.
Description: Whilst making an approach to a lock with a pilot on board, the vessel landed heavily at the entrance causing damage to the wooden fenders.

Short_Description: A crew transfer vessel entered a harbour and both engines began to overheat.
Description: A crew transfer vessel was entering a harbour to berth in a marina. There was a thin slush of ice on the surface near the marina, both engines began to overheat. An anchor was deployed whilst it was investigated. Upon inspection it was found that both engine cooling intakes had frozen resulting in the cooling water not flowing.

Short_Description: A narrow boat partially sank.
Description: A narrow boat partially sank.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship

Short_Description: A cruise ship contractor fractured their wrist after slipping on a staircase.
Description: A cruise ship contractor was on a staircase when their foot slipped on the top step which was covered in protective plastic. This resulted in a fall and a left wrist fracture. The contractor was wearing rubber moulded open toe footwear at the time of the incident.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel grounded due to a navigational error and was towed by lifeboat.
Description: The vessel grounded at a harbour entrance due to a navigational error. A passing vessel assisted them and a lifeboat towed them to their designated berth. No damage or pollution was sustained to the vessel and no injuries to any of the crew members.

Short_Description: A sailing barge ran aground in port during passenger transfer.
Description: Whilst waiting to conduct a passenger transfer by boat in port a sailing barge grounded and required assistance to be re-floated.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel was taking on water. The ingress was stopped and casualty vessel was towed to harbour.
Description: A sailing vessel with three people on board started taking on water but the manual bilge pump coped with the water. The crew issued a pan pan and all were wearing lifejackets. A lifeboat was tasked to assist. The source of the leak was located to the engine cooling water intake so the seacock was shut off. The yacht's crew tried to sail to the nearest port.  A nearby training vessel provided a tow into the local harbour.
Damage_Description: Water leak in cooling water system, seacock shut off.

Short_Description: A charter yacht grounded on return to port and managed to free itself with minor damage sustained.
Description: A yacht charter grounded on shingle when returning to port on a falling tide. The harbourmaster dispatched a rib to attempt a tow, but the rib was not able to free the yacht. The yacht unfurled a jib and managed to sail itself free from the shingle. A subsequent survey and out of water report outlined abrasion to the keel and rudder, but no structural defects.
Damage_Description: Surveyor report outlines abrasion to the keel and the rudder, but no structural damage.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel had a fire in one of the holds.
Description: A general cargo vessel had a large fire in the hold. Non-fire-fighting crew on the casualty vessel and all crew on neighbouring vessels were evacuated.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel's pilot ladder parted whilst pilot was routinely weight testing ladder before boarding vessel.
Description: When the pilot launch came alongside the vessel, the launch deckhand put their weight on the bottom of the ladder and routinely weight tested the ladder. This however, caused the left side rope to part close to the top as it passed over the deck.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier made contact with a lock entrance.
Description: A bulk carrier made contact with the lock entrance on its approach into port. There was a pilot on board and three tugs assisting the vessel. The incident happened due to a miscommunication over VHF (Very High Frequency) Radio. Another nearby vessel was using the same channel to communicate meaning the pilot and the tugs were unable to communicate effectively. The vessel didn't sustain any damage and the berthing operations continued without incident.

Short_Description: A yacht had an electrical malfunction.
Description: A vessel had electrical problems and issues with its autopilot and was towed into port by a lifeboat.

Short_Description: A cruise ship reported a loss of electrical power.
Description: A cruise ship lost propulsion for ten minutes, resulting in the vessel being not under command.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had an engine malfunction and was towed.
Description: A fishing vessel had engine failure and was towed by a lifeboat.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had rope around propeller and had to be towed to safety.
Description: A creel vessel was struggling with rope wrapped around the propeller. They were drifting towards the rocks and were towed to safety. There was no reported damage to the vessel and no injuries.
Damage_Description: Rope was wrapped around the prop but no reported damage.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel crewmember slipped over sustaining a suspected broken rib.
Description: A cargo vessel crewmember had a fall resulting in suspected broken rib.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser ran aground.
Description: A motor cruiser ran aground. It was in close proximately to a marker buoy and was deemed to be a hazard to navigation. As a result, it was towed to deeper water.

Short_Description: A SAR vessel's daughter craft made contact with breakwater and sustained hole in the bow.
Description: A SAR (search and rescue) vessel's daughter craft made contact with breakwater whilst coming alongside.  A hole was sustained in the bow of the daughter craft.  The daughter craft is not out of service and has not affected the service of the SAR mother vessel. No injuries were sustained.
Damage_Description: Puncture to STBD bow area of sponson to the ALB’s Daughter Craft (Y Boat), deflation of bow section. Able to be recovered, no pollution.

Short_Description: A patrol vessel had an accidental release of CO2 into the CO2 manifold. Additional safety valves prevented CO2 from entering any space.
Description: A crewmember on a patrol vessel was conducting routine maintenance within the CO2 room which led to the decision to isolate the CO2 system using isolation pins on each CO2 bottle within the space. When reinstating the system and on removing one isolation pin the crewmember's glove snagged on the system causing the accidental release of the CO2 into the CO2 manifold. The CO2 released was prevented from entering any space due to additional safety valves and was subsequently vented to atmosphere.

Short_Description: A vessel's crew members fell overboard resulting in no injuries and the vessel later washed up ashore.
Description: A vessel's crew members fell overboard. They were wearing PFDs (personal floatation devices) and they self-recovered ashore. The vessel was later washed ashore. There were no injuries and the crew made their own way home.

Short_Description: A tug ran over its own towline.
Description: A tug ran over its own towline and had damages including a bent shaft, arriving at the port to undergo repairs.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. The ladder was secured to the deck using shackles only. The master stated that they had not been made aware of this before however they will rectify the rigging arrangement prior to next use.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel crewmember fell from the deck.
Description: A crewmember fell from deck and landed on the vessel's hull. They sustained injuries to their neck and back.

Short_Description: A passenger on commercial RIB sustained minor back pain whilst on board.
Description: A RIB (rigid inflatable boat) skipper was leaving harbour for a cruise when they went over a wave and the subsequent jolt hurt a passenger's back. The skipper returned to harbour and the passenger left the vessel, confirming later by email that after a walk and pain killers they felt better.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser went aground and was towed to safety.
Description: A motor cruiser went aground with seven people on board. The vessel was towed free before being escorted back to port. No injuries or damage were sustained.

Short_Description: A tall ship had engine issues and was towed into port.
Description: A tall ship had engine issues in its approach to port. The vessel was assisted by a tug and entered the port without further issue.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel fouled its propeller and was towed back to port by another fishing vessel.
Description: A fishing vessel with three crew onboard fouled its propeller. The vessel was drifting towards a windfarm but in no immediate danger. The fishing vessel's sister vessel towed the vessel back to its home port. No injuries to crew were reported.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel had a loss of propulsion but then proceeded with no further incident.
Description: A cargo vessel main engine failure whilst outbound from a port. The vessel was anchored in a channel. A tug was put on standby, the main engine restarted and vessel proceeded without further incident.

Short_Description: A tender from leisure sailing yacht reported water ingress and required assistance.
Description: A tender from leisure sailing yacht reported water ingress and required assistance.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser crewmember jumped into the water and sustained a head injury.
Description: A motor cruiser crewmember jumped into the water, as they were climbing back onboard they grabbed the wrong rope and pulled the lead weight anchor onto their head. They were not knocked out but had a deep laceration two inches above their hairline. They were treated on the river bank until the ambulance arrived.

Short_Description: A safety boat capsized in heavy surf. The vessel self-recovered.
Description: A safety boat capsized in heavy surf while providing safety cover for a triathlon. While the local lifeboat crew were still mustering, the casualty vessel and two crew self-recovered to shore. There were no injuries and all of the triathlon participants were out of the water shortly after.

Short_Description: A passenger vessel crewmember fell overboard after slipping from the gunwale during departure operations.
Description: As the vessel was departing berth, a crewmember was securing the mooring line to the vessel's handrail and misplaced their footing on the gunwale, which was approximately one metre above the water surface. The crewmember grabbed the vessel fender line to try and prevent themself from falling in, but ended up waist-deep in the water. There were no injuries and the casualty was helped out of the water by another crewmember.

Short_Description: A container ship lost 36 containers overboard during heavy weather
Description: Conditions were a very rough sea and swell, the ship was rolling moderately within 10 degrees to both sides. The ship suddenly started rolling 13-15 degrees to both side and then the duty officer on bridge heard one abnormal sound on ship's starboard side. They went to the bridgewing to look and found some containers had collapsed overboard. The crew mustered and assessed the damage, also adjusting ship’s course and reducing speed. After checking any potential damage, they found that 36 containers had fallen overboard, 21 containers had fallen over on deck, another 2 leaning on the bulwark and some others were deformed.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting marine infrastructure or other ship

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel made contact with lock gate.
Description: A general cargo vessel was entering a lock when it collided with the lock gates, causing damage to the gate and the vessel.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting structural integrity of the ship

Short_Description: A fishing vessel fouled its gear.
Description: A fishing vessel fouled its gear on its propeller and was towed by a lifeboat.

Short_Description: A motor cruiser had engine failure and was towed back to port.
Description: A motor cruiser had engine failure and was towed back to port by a lifeboat.

Short_Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A ro-ro cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. A metal bar was clamped over the ladder to secure it. The weight was on a step and not the side ropes. There was also a broken step above the weight bearing end of the ladder.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. The replacement steps did not appear to comply with regulations.

Short_Description: A container ship's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS.
Description: A container ship's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS.

Short_Description: A Motorboat ran aground and began to flood.
Description: A motorboat lost propulsion and ran aground. This resulted in damage allowing flooding to take place. The vessel was able to make its way back to its berth and was pumped out by the marina staff and local lifeboat crewmembers.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship

Short_Description: A Ro-Ro ferry crewmember trapped their fingers in a set of doors, resulting in two fractured digits.
Description: A ro-ro vessel crewmember was taking used cooking oil drums from the galley to the car deck, to be put into a van and landed ashore. After they had removed the oil drums from a lift, they pulled the lift door down and trapped their index and fore-finger between the two vertical doors. On returning to the galley, they noted a slight cut to their index finger and both fingers were showing signs of redness, they applied a plaster to the cut and also put some ice on them and continued to finish their shift. Overnight the fingers swelled up and turned purple. The casualty was sent to hospital where it was determined the crewmember had sustained two broken fingers.

Short_Description: A cruise ship crewmember caught their hand between a trolley and a door frame resulting in a fracture.
Description: A cruise ship crewmember was pulling a trolly holding trays of food, holding the trolly by the vertical frame and when looking behind to make sure the path was clear they hit their hand on the door frame resulting in a fractured hand.

Short_Description: A container vessel's forward fall broke after returning the lifeboat into the stowage position.
Description: The vessel was undertaking an abandon ship drill, whilst they were returning the port side lifeboat to its stowage position in the davits the forward fall broke. Fortunately, the aft fall held firm and the crew as a temporary measure were able to affix the additional securing to reduce the stress of the intact fall. No further damage was confirmed, flag states were also informed and the vessel proceeded to a port in order to make the relevant repairs to replace the wire and rigged. The lifeboat was returned back to its stowed position, it was found after an inspection of the wire that there was some rusting in the core despite regular greasing and checking. The lifeboat did suffer some scraping but was not holed and the crew managed to repair the damage.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had an alternator failure and was assisted by a lifeboat.
Description: A fishing vessel had a main engine alternator failure which caused a spark and set off the fire alarm. There was no fire but the skipper did not restart the engine as precaution. They called the coastguard and a tow by a local lifeboat back to port was arranged.

Short_Description: A ro-pax vessel's davit winch failed whilst hoisting its rescue boat.
Description: A ro-pax vessel was alongside carrying out a drill using the vessel's rescue boat. During the recovery by the davit winch, the boat was close to being fully hoisted when it lowered back by approximately 0.3 metres unexpectedly. The rescue boat crewmember was taken back aboard the ro-pax vessel. The davit was tested again and the same fault occurred. Davit use was suspended with an alternative means of recovery for the rescue boat to be decided.

Short_Description: A leisure vessel reported an engine fire.  The crew extinguished the fire.
Description: A leisure vessel reported an engine fire. The crew extinguished fire.  No damage was reported.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had mechanical failure and was towed to safety by the RNLI.
Description: A small fishing vessel with one crewmember lost its propeller.  The vessel anchored and the skipper called for assistance and a lifeboat towed the boat back to its mooring.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship

Short_Description: A motor cruiser fouled its propeller and required assistance.
Description: A motor cruiser fouled its propeller. The four crew onboard were wearing lifejackets and the anchor had been deployed. Assistance was required as they were unable to free the propeller, a search and rescue (SAR) vessel was tasked and towed the vessel to safety.

Short_Description: A lifeboat made contact with the berth resulting in some damage to the rubbing strip.
Description: A lifeboat was undertaking boat handling training, a trainee crewmember was manoeuvring the lifeboat alongside the pontoon. A gust of wind caught the lifeboat and began push it towards the shallow water located close to the berth. The trainee crewmember counteracted the drift by applying power. However, in compensating for the drift the trainee crewmember applied excessive power causing the lifeboat to surge towards the berth. Unable to counteract this quickly enough the supervising crewmember took control but was unable to prevent the lifeboat making contact with the pontoon.

Short_Description: A speedboat grounded on mud and was assisted back to safety.
Description: A motor boat ran aground on mud. The four people on board were happy to wait for high tide, but the search and rescue team were not confident about their ability so assisted them and provided a tow back to port. There was no damage to the vessel and all persons were recovered safe and well.

Short_Description: A yacht fouled its propeller with a rope.
Description: Yacht had a fouled propeller from a floating rope and was towed into port.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had engine failure and was towed.
Description: A fishing vessel had steering failure and was towed back into port by the local lifeboat.

Short_Description: Duplicate of 4521/2021
Description: Duplicate of 4521/2022

Short_Description: A yacht crewmember fell overboard from a tender when trying to grab a mooring line and injured their shoulder.
Description: A charter yacht crewmember fell overboard from the tender when they were reaching across from the tender in big swells to grab the mooring rope. The crewmember held onto the vessel when they fell resulting in torn muscles in their shoulder.

Short_Description: A racing boat capsized with all persons recovered to the shore and the vessel was recovered by the club's rescue boat.
Description: A racing sailing boat with four people on board capsized.  All persons onboard were recovered to shore by the yacht club's rescue boat. All people were wearing personal floatation devices and they operated correctly.  The yacht initially obstructed the navigational channel but was towed clear.  After cutting away the sails and other equipment, the yacht was recovered to a harbour for assessment and repair. A lifeboat and pilot boat attended but the yacht club rescue boat recovered the casualty vessel to shore without assistance.

Short_Description: A vehicle carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged in compliance with SOLAS guidance.
Description: A vehicle carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged in compliance with SOLAS guidance. The step of the ladder was resting against a raised platform.

Short_Description: A yacht grounded.
Description: A vessel grounded after experiencing loss of propulsion, anchor chain braking off and loss of steering.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting performance or operational characteristics of the ship

Short_Description: A motor vessel fouled its propeller on a lobster pot rope which was then freed with assistance.
Description: A motor vessel with two people on board fouled its propeller on a lobster pot rope. A near by boat crew managed to untangle the rope. However, the motor vessel then ran aground on transit to port but refloated later on rising tide. No damage or injuries.

Short_Description: A yacht and personal water craft collided whilst departing port.
Description: A jet ski (Personal Water Craft or PWC) collided with a yacht as it was leaving the harbour. The yacht was making its way under power at approximately four knots and preparing the sails. There were two jet skis in the local area proceeding at speed. The jet ski driver was watching the ring they were towing before making a sharp turn, flinging the passenger out of the inflatable ring and colliding with the bow of the yacht. The driver of the jet ski then re-mounted and left the area without speaking to the skipper of the yacht. There was damage to the gel coat of the yacht. The jet ski sustained damage to the right-hand side. There were no injuries to any parties involved and the yacht went back to port.

Short_Description: A yacht and personal water craft collided whilst departing port.
Description: A jet ski (Personal Water Craft or PWC) collided with a yacht as it was leaving the harbour. The yacht was making its way under power at approximately four knots and preparing the sails. There were two jet skis in the local area proceeding at speed. The jet ski driver was watching the ring they were towing before making a sharp turn, flinging the passenger out of the inflatable ring and colliding with the bow of the yacht. The driver of the jet ski then re-mounted and left the area without speaking to the skipper of the yacht. There was damage to the gel coat of the yacht. The jet ski sustained damage to the right-hand side. There were no injuries to any parties involved and the yacht went back to port.
Damage_Description: Superficial gel coat damage to bow

Short_Description: A sailing vessel grounded on rocks and broke up.
Description: A sailing vessel, crewed by two people, left a marina using transom mounted outboard motor to go fishing.  Once clear of the harbour, the crew quickly realised that it was too rough and turned back. Unfortunately, during passage back, the outboard motor was lost overboard when its bracket sheared off the yacht's transom. Adrift, the yacht was quickly blown onto and grounded on a breakwater. The crew was rescued by the marina's power boat. The local lifeboat service attempted to tow the yacht clear without success. During  following week the vessel broke up before the insurance company could arrange for its the removal . The yacht was declared a constructive total loss.

Short_Description: An oil tanker grounded on entering a port.
Description: Whilst an oil tanker was manoeuvring astern towards its berth, the bow sheered to port resulting in grounding. The vessel remained safely aground with the stern afloat and propeller and rudder clear. Tug assistance was used to get the vessel alongside with no further incident. The vessel was undamaged.

Short_Description: A lifeboat struck an object in a channel resulting in minor damage to the bow.
Description: A lifeboat launched on a spring tide low water. The bow struck a submerged object, believed to be a rock in the slipway channel, resulting in minor damage.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier crewmember sustained a partial amputation of a finger.
Description: A bulk carrier crewmember was overhauling a deck air compressor and assembling a belt pulley. The crewmember and another crewmember then tried a test run of the deck air compressor and to check the belt alignment. The crewmember did not know that the  compressor was in automatic mode and forgot to switch off the power supply. The crewmember went to perform a small adjustment of the belt when the compressor suddenly started up and caught the crew member's left index finger in the belt resulting in a partial amputation.  First aid was administered onboard, the crewmember was then disembarked for further treatment at a hospital.

Short_Description: An oil tanker crewmember threw a weighted heaving line.
Description: An oil tanker crewmember threw a weighted heaving line.

Short_Description: A tug crewmember fell down a set of steps and sustained fractured shoulders.
Description: A tug crewmember was descending a set of stairs when they caught their heel on a step and fell down the steps to the deck. Other crew members assisted the injured crewmember who was semi-conscious. The vessel diverted to the nearest port to get the crewmember to hospital. The crewmember was assessed and confirmed they had fractured shoulder blades.

Short_Description: A commercial dive vessel reported gearbox issues, but made their own way into port.
Description: A commercial dive vessel reported gearbox issues, but made their own way into port.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel, being used as a guard vessel, grounded and was pulled off a sandbank once the tide allowed.
Description: A fishing vessel with four people on board, being used as a guard vessel grounded and was assisted off the sandbank by a search and rescue vessel. There were no reported injuries or damage.
Damage_Description: No damage - database validation check inconsistent

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger vessel crewmember sustained a burn injury to their arm
Description: A ro-ro passenger vessel crewmember burned their arm on a cooker as a result of rough seas. The casualty was signed off work the following day and received medical care at home.

Short_Description: A commercial sailing vessel sustained damage after a collision with a channel marker after autopilot problems.
Description: A commercial sailing vessel undertaking training with four people on board sustained damage above the waterline after a collision with a channel marker. While sailing up a channel the skipper lent on the coach roof to adjust the mainsheet which caused the autopilot to engage. It was apparent the yacht was on a collision course with a buoy. The crew became aware the autopilot had been engaged and the instructor tried to switch off the autopilot but the writing on the control buttons had worn out. All efforts to disengage the autopilot failed and the vessel collided with the channel buoy leading to damage to the hull above the waterline. Eventually the instructor disengaged the batteries to regain control of the yacht's wheel.
Damage_Description: Hole to bow above the waterline and below the forestay plate.

Short_Description: A chemical tanker experienced engine failure whilst in port.
Description: A chemical tanker had an engine failure whilst in port waters. While the vessel was under pilotage to the berth the main engine cooling water temperature raised suddenly causing the high temperature safety device to shut down the main propulsion engine. The vessel dropped anchor and investigation revealed that one of the isolating valves was shut. The valve likely shut itself due to vibrations and thrust of the water flow. The valve was reopened and secured and then the main engine was tested and the ship proceeded to the berth.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations because it was secured by shackles.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel had engine failure and had a near miss with passenger ferry.
Description: Whilst a general cargo vessel was under pilotage when the vessel had a complete engine failure. The vessel was swinging to starboard into the pathway of an oncoming passenger ferry. The general cargo vessel attempted to call the passenger ferry to warn them of their situation but the ferry had their radio turned down and couldn't hear the calls. The passenger ferry altered course after seeing the general cargo ship swing to starboard to avoid a collision.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel had engine failure and had a near miss with passenger ferry.
Description: Whilst a general cargo vessel was under pilotage when the vessel had a complete engine failure. The vessel was swinging to starboard into the pathway of an oncoming passenger ferry. The general cargo vessel attempted to call the passenger ferry to warn them of their situation but the ferry had their radio turned down and couldn't hear the calls. The passenger ferry altered course after seeing the general cargo ship swing to starboard to avoid a collision.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had engine failure and was towed back to port.
Description: A fishing vessel had engine failure and requested a tow and another fishing vessel nearby towed the vessel back to port. No injuries to crew or vessel damage was reported.

Short_Description: A pilot boarding a container ship reported a calf injury.
Description: A pilot had calf injury to their lower left leg, whilst climbing a pilot ladder boarding a container ship. No other parties were involved at the time. The pilot made it onboard where ice was applied and an ambulance was waiting at the port to take them to get checked out at the hospital.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations.
Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. The pilot ladder's bottom two rubber steps were cracked where side ropes passed through.

Short_Description: A recreational motor vessel fouled its propeller and was towed.
Description: A recreational motor vessel fouled its propeller. The two people onboard were unable to free it. A search and rescue (SAR) vessel was deployed to tow the vessel back to shore.

Short_Description: A container vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A container vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. The ladder was on a reel and secured with a bar across the ropes.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel crewmember fell down a ladder and hit their hand.
Description: A cargo vessel crewmember fell down a ladder and hit their hand whilst trying to restore balance. The crewmember was in pain but it subsided until the following day when their hand began to swell. The following day the vessel was alongside and the crewmember went to the local hospital. After being taken for an x-ray, the crewmember was diagnosed with broken metatarsals in their right hand. The hand was placed in a cast and they returned to the vessel the same evening before being repatriated two days later.

Short_Description: A sailing yacht had water ingress due to bilge pump malfunction.
Description: Sailing yacht with five people on board called MAYDAY after the vessel started filling with water. Search and rescue assets were tasked to the vessel but it was soon discovered that the cause of the water ingress was the bilge pump which was pumping water into the vessel rather than out.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel made contact with a lock after a spring line was accidentally released.
Description: Whilst backing into the lock, the vessel's crew let go of the back spring from the jetty and came astern and the vessel's port quarter made contact with the east side of the lock.

Short_Description: A cruise ship passenger fell exiting the bathroom and fractured their hip.
Description: A cruise ship passenger tripped and fell while exiting the bathroom in their cabin resulting in a fractured left hip. The vessel was in harbour at the time of the accident and the casualty was landed ashore before sailing.

Short_Description: A crew member on yacht sustained a hand injury.
Description: A crew member on yacht sustained a hand injury. The finger was crushed by the windlass.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged in compliance with SOLAS guidance.
Description: A general cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged in compliance with SOLAS guidance. There were no strongpoints to secure ladder lashings and it was looped around a fire main.

Short_Description: A service ship had a fire in its daughter craft and there minor damage to the daughter craft.
Description: The daughter craft from a service vessel reported a small engine fire, which was rapidly extinguished and the boat was recovered by davit.
Damage_Description: SLIGHT DAMAGE CAUSED BY SMALL FIRE IN DAUGHTER CRAFT ENGINE BAY THERE WAS NO POLLUTION AS FIRE WAS CONTAINED AND EXTINGUISHED USING FIRE EXTINGUISHER

Short_Description: A cargo vessel's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations
Description: A cargo vessel's pilot ladder did not conform to SOLAS regulations. The ladder was in poor condition with excessive play in the steps. The crew were advised to replace the ladder before the next port.

Short_Description: A hire motorboat ran aground and was recovered on the rising tide with no damage.
Description: A hire motorboat with five people on board drifted aground after another boat went across their bow and they cut their engine, but could not restart it. The hire company recovered the crew and the vessel on the rising tide with no damage or injuries sustained.

Short_Description: A replenishment tanker experienced overheating of a cooling pump resulting in smoke detector activation.
Description: A replenishment tanker was at anchor when two smoke detectors activated in the forward auxiliary room. The crew mustered at harbour emergency stations whilst the duty element of the harbour emergency organisation investigated the alarms. On entering the space, a smoke haze was identified in the compartment, caused by the overheating of the mechanical seal on a cooling pump supplying the air treatment units covering the replenishment at sea machinery space. The smoke was generated by the overheating of the associated grease on the seal and the pump was stopped. The pump was allowed to cool naturally and the compartment ventilation re-started to clear the smoke haze. The harbour emergency stations were released around sixteen minutes after the first smoke detector activated. The incident was attributed to the sea water supply having been shut down to the air treatment units three days before the incident without stopping the associated cooling pump; this was due to a lack of communication between the duty engineer and system maintainer/operator.

Short_Description: A dredger and a fishing vessel had a near miss collision.
Description: A dredger was following a fishing vessel out of a port. The fishing vessel stopped and turned 180 degrees. The dredger called the fishing vessel and asked it to pass down its port side. The fishing vessel then appeared to turn to port to pass down the starboard side and then altered course again to starboard. Concerned of a collision occurring, the dredger took evasive action going astern and using its bow thruster to stay on course. The fishing vessel passed closely down the port side of the dredger.

Short_Description: A dredger and a fishing vessel had a near miss collision.
Description: A dredger was following a fishing vessel out of a port. The fishing vessel stopped and turned 180 degrees. The dredger called the fishing vessel and asked it to pass down its port side. The fishing vessel then appeared to turn to port to pass down the starboard side and then altered course again to starboard. Concerned of a collision occurring, the dredger took evasive action going astern and using its bow thruster to stay on course. The fishing vessel passed closely down the port side of the dredger.

Short_Description: A hopper dredger grounded whilst alongside and later re-floated on the flood tide.
Description: A hopper dredger was alongside to discharge cargo. The cargo was refused so a pilot was requested to take the vessel back to sea. When the pilot got on board, the vessel began to go aground with the ebb tide. The vessel re-floated on the flood tide and left the berth under pilotage. There was no damage to the vessel.

Short_Description: An oil tanker grounded as a result of a rudder issue.
Description: A cargo vessel with a pilot on board was proceeding along a channel. The pilot noticed the vessel was sluggish and had to give the vessel lots of helm for the rudder to be effective. During the operation, control of the vessel was lost due to the rudder issue and the bow thrusters were turned off at the time meaning they could not be used to prevent the grounding. It was a soft grounding, there was no damage sustained to the vessel. The vessel was aground for approximately seven minutes before being re-floated.

Short_Description: A dredger had propulsion failure and a blackout.
Description: Whilst holding position in the entrance to a port for outbound traffic, a dredger experienced propulsion failure, bow thruster failure and subsequently a blackout due to the loss of the port alternator. With the use of the starboard engine, the vessel was manoeuvred into the turning basin and taken out to sea.

Short_Description: A SAR craft crewmember fell overboard during a training exercise.
Description: A SAR (search and rescue vessel) was on a training exercise in the surf zone. The task being trained was parallel running to the surf. The helm was being trained with the crew person in the boat being the trainer assessor. The craft was hit by a small wave port side beam-on to the surf and the helm fell out of the boat. The helm fell out on the seaward side of the boat so the boat washed away from the helm with no risk of the boat being washed over the top of them. The incident happened in chest deep water. The helm swam to shore and the crew trainer assessor moved to the helm position and returned the boat to shore.

Short_Description: A passenger ship's passenger fell down some steps and fractured their ankle.
Description: A passenger ship's passenger fell down some steps and fractured their ankle.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger vessel crewmember fractured their wrist whilst descending the car deck stairwell.
Description: A crewmember on a ferry was carrying a coiled roll of rubber seal down a stairwell. The seal uncoiled and tripped them resulting in a fall down the stairwell and they fractured their fractured wrist.

Short_Description: A general cargo vessel experienced main engines and systems failure.
