Description: A general cargo vessel experienced main engines and systems failure.

Short_Description: A sailing yacht crewmember was found deceased next to the vessel.
Description: A sailing yacht crewmember was found deceased next to the vessel.

Short_Description: A recreational angling vessel ran aground but later re-floated.
Description: A recreational angling vessel ran aground. The two people onboard were in a fishing competition. The two people had provisions onboard and waited for the flood tide to re-float the vessel. No damage was reported and there were no injuries to persons onboard.

Short_Description: a Leisure RIB crewmember had a back injury and was taken to hospital.
Description: A leisure RIB (rigid inflatable boat) with four people on board had a crewmember who sustained a back injury after wave impact. The casualty was evacuated to hospital by helicopter following medical advice.

Short_Description: A sailing vessel grounded and sustained a crack in the matrix of the hull.
Description: A chartered sailing vessel ran aground just after they had dropped the spinnaker. There were no injuries or flooding but visual inspection later showed a crack to the matrix of the hull.
Damage_Description: A crack to the matrix of the hull which had to be examined by a surveyor

Short_Description: A research vessel crewmember injured their knee when a chain snapped out of position.
Description: A crewmember had abrasions and bruising injuries to their knee whilst the vessel was shooting fishing nets. A chain snapped out of position and caught the crewmember in their knee. There was no requirement to airlift casualty because a doctor confirmed they were happy for them to remain onboard to recover.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel crewmember slipped during a mooring operation resulting in a fractured arm.
Description: A cargo vessel crewmember slipped on the deck during mooring operation and hit their arm on the mooring winch resulting in a fracture.

Short_Description: Two leisure vessels collided resulting in one person overboard. The casualty was recovered with no injuries and there was minor vessel damage.
Description: A small angling vessel was moored near the shore and saw a motorboat approaching on a collision course. The skipper of the angling boat sounded their horn and then jumped overboard to avoid potential injury as the motorboat collided with them. They were not wearing a lifejacket. The skipper of the motorboat stopped and recovered the  person from the water. A lifeboat then towed the angling vessel whilst the motorboat made its own way to the marina. The casualty was assessed to be cold and shocked but uninjured. There was minor damage sustained to both vessels.  The skipper admitted being distracted and that they had not seen the angling vessel ahead.

Short_Description: Two leisure vessels collided resulting in one person overboard. The casualty was recovered with no injuries and there was minor vessel damage.
Description: A small angling vessel was moored near the shore and saw a motorboat approaching on a collision course. The skipper of the angling boat sounded their horn and then jumped overboard to avoid potential injury as the motorboat collided with them. They were not wearing a lifejacket. The skipper of the motorboat stopped and recovered the  person from the water. A lifeboat then towed the angling vessel whilst the motorboat made its own way to the marina. The casualty was assessed to be cold and shocked but uninjured. There was minor damage sustained to both vessels.  The skipper admitted being distracted and that they had not seen the angling vessel ahead.
Damage_Description: Superficial damage to where stanchions came away from the deck on impact.

Short_Description: A ro-ro passenger ferry had a fire in the boiler.
Description: During a passage the fire detection system alarm sounded, the crew on duty saw a flame emanating from the top of the boiler. The fuel and oil supplies were immediately shut off. The flame subsided and they continued to monitor to ensure the flame had completely extinguished. There was minimal damage caused that was scorch marks to the top of the boiler.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel had engine failure.
Description: A fishing vessel had engine failure but managed to re-start their engines.  A lifeboat shadowed vessel back to port.

Short_Description: A chartered angling vessel experienced engine failure.
Description: A chartered angling vessel experienced engine failure and was towed to port by a lifeboat.

Short_Description: A SAR vessel made contact with a submerged object resulting in minor damage.
Description: A SAR (search and rescue) vessel was completing a routine training exercise near the shoreline when an outboard engine skeg made contact with a submerged object causing minor damage. The boat made its own way back to the lifeboat station.
Damage_Description: Minor damage to the outboard engine - gearbox casing.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS.
Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder rigging did not conform to SOLAS. The bottom platform was not five metres from the water line. The tripping line rigged on bottom of ladder was not correct.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel crewmember slipped and injured their knee.
Description: A fishing vessel was waiting in a lock to leave and a crewmember had brought in the ropes and fenders thinking it was free flow state in the lock but it was not. The crewmember put the ropes and fenders back out, as they ran towards the bow to tie off a rope, they slipped and twisted their knee.

Short_Description: A hire cruiser passenger landed awkwardly and fractured their leg.
Description: A passenger was stepping off a hire vessel when it was mooring when they fell and landed awkwardly. The passenger was diagnosed with a fractured leg.

Short_Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations.
Description: A bulk carrier's pilot ladder was not rigged as per SOLAS regulations. A tripping line was fitted to the bottom of the ladder, or was rigged not in accordance with IMO Resolution A.1045(27) 2.1.5.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel's autopilot failed and it hit rocks causing water ingress.
Description: The vessel was outside of a harbour when the autopilot failed and it ended up hitting rocks. As a result, they proceeded to the nearest harbour to request assistance and noticed that the vessel was experiencing from water ingress. A hole was located behind the bulkhead, pumps were used to stem the water flow by a lifeboat and two crew members managed to get themselves off the vessel. They waited for the low tide to try to fix the hole. The skipper was taken to hospital because of suspicions that they could be experiencing from carbon dioxide poisoning but there were no injuries to the other crew member.
Loss_Of_Vessel_Damage: Material damage -> Affecting structural integrity of the ship

Short_Description: A sailing yacht had a fire and it sank.
Description: A sailing yacht with one person on board had a fire resulting in its sinking.

Short_Description: A cruise ship passenger fell and sustained a fracture and dislocation resulting in a transfer to hospital care.
Description: A cruise ship passenger tripped over a door sill and fell fracturing their right shoulder and bruising their right thumb. The passenger received medical treatment on board before transfer ashore by lifeboat.

Short_Description: A survey vessel made contact with the quayside after experiencing engine failure causing minor damage to the bow.
Description: While manoeuvring ready for an outward bound transit, a survey vessel had a main engine control system failure. This caused the master to momentarily lose full control of the vessel. While trying to regain control the vessel impacted two quay areas causing minor damage to the quay and vessel bow.

Short_Description: A cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged in compliance with SOLAS guidance.
Description: A cargo vessel's pilot ladder was not rigged in compliance with SOLAS guidance. The ladder secured to air vent and had no load test certificate. There was not an officer present. The master advised that they did not have sufficient officers. A tripping line was secured to the bottom of the ladder.

Short_Description: A mooring launch became caught under the aft of a container vessel.
Description: A mooring launch became caught under aft of a container vessel. No damage was reported.

Short_Description: A mooring launch became caught under the aft of a container vessel.
Description: A mooring launch became caught under aft of a container vessel. No damage was reported.

Short_Description: A tug made contact with the berth.
Description: A tug was assisting a tanker during berthing, when it made contact with the berth and damage was sustained to the forward handrail.

Short_Description: A hire cruiser had a fire on board and the occupants moved to another vessel.
Description: A moored motor cruiser was evacuated when smoke emerged from the engine compartment. The local fire brigade found the engine compartment very hot, but no fire. All occupants were uninjured.

Short_Description: A recreational motor cruiser was at anchor due to mechanical issues and was dragging toward rocks.
Description: A recreational motor cruiser was at anchor due to mechanical issues and was dragging toward rocks. They were approximately 100 metres from the rocks to begin with and were reported to be drifting at 20 meters per hour.
Damage_Description: Unknown if any damage and unknown if towage was performed

Short_Description: A replenishment tanker had a fire from a bow thruster unit.
Description: A replenishment tanker had shut down propulsion due to a flood and was drifting whilst the water was removed. The bow thrust unit (BTU) was being used to maintain the tanker's head into the prevailing conditions. Whilst the BTU was running, smoke was seen coming from the forward compartment. The tanker went to emergency stations and a fire was confirmed. The fire was extinguished with by the fire team who cooled the brake assembly and carried out temperature monitoring. The compartment ventilation was reinstated and the area sealed off to await atmosphere testing. There were no reported crew injuries. The brake tyre assembly and brake solenoid were replaced.
Damage_Description: Brake tyre assembly and brake solenoid overheated, to be replaced

Short_Description: A cruise ship's crew detected water ingress in a water ballast tank during hull cleaning.
Description: While a cruise ship was alongside, underwater cleaning of the hull was taking place. Sea water ingress was detected in a double bottom ballast tank as the tank was empty prior to the incident.  There was no pollution and no danger to the stability of vessel. Divers discovered a small hole in the hull caused during the hull cleaning and a temporary repair plug was installed.
Damage_Description: While cleaning the hull underwater a small puncture was caused into a double bottom tank.

Short_Description: A fishing vessel capsized and sank.
Description: A fishing vessel capsized and sank just outside of a harbour. The emergency services rescued the one person on board.

Short_Description: A workboat's tow rope broke during a ship assist towage operation.
Description: A tug was assisting a bulk carrier to a berth. The tug was connected up to the centre lead aft. The pilot asked for 50% dead astern on the tug and this request was adhered to. After about eight minutes the tow parted. The spare tow rope was reconnected to the bulk carrier to complete the berthing operations.

Short_Description: A yacht crewmember was hit by a boom and injured their head.
Description: A crewmember was hit by a boom on board and had a head injury. The crewmember was taken straight to hospital but because it wasn't deemed to be as serious as initially thought, no ambulance was required.

Short_Description: Two shoreside crane operators were hospitalised with respiratory symptoms possibly caused by a heating system.
Description: Two crane operators fell ill with breathing difficulties, after it was suspected that the heating system had emitted something that had caused the illness. One casualty was released from hospital on the same day the second casualty remained in hospital.

Short_Description: A pilot boat reported engine failure and required assistance.
Description: A pilot boat reported engine failure and required assistance.

Short_Description: An oil tanker crewmember had a crushed hand and loss of a finger and was airlifted and transferred to hospital.
Description: An oil tanker crewmember was airlifted from the vessel and transferred to hospital after sustaining a hand crush injury. They lost one finger on the right hand and there was damage to the other fingers.
